Title: InfernoFusion: An Edge-Optimized Audio-Visual Deep Learning Framework for Early Fire Smoke Detection
Abstract: The requirement for early, dependable fire detection is very high because it reduces damage and satisfies public safety requirements in large-scale complex environments. The paper presents an audio-visual early fire and smoke detection system based on deep learning for real-time deployment on edge devices. Besides, the system is not limited to vision alone, which can fail at low illumination or be compromised by occlusion due to visual ambiguity, but combines the visual features of fire and smoke with cracks and hissing as complementary acoustic cues to curb robustness. Convolutional neural networks are used to process visual data along with preprocessing and augmentation techniques aimed at enhancing generalization, while audio signals are analyzed using spectral features for the detection of fire-related acoustic patterns. A fusion multimodal strategy combines the predictions of both modalities, which can greatly reduce the number of false alarms and improve detection accuracy. It is also optimized to perform lightweight inference and assessed under different lighting conditions, thus sustaining performance across varied low-lux environments with particular reliance on audio cues in circumstances where visual clarity is compromised. Title: Enhanced Gender Recognition in Telugu Speech Using Augmented Transgender Audio
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive approach to gender classification in Telugu audio using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and pitch features. This work fills a critical gap in inclusivity within speech-based systems by expanding the problem to include transgender voices, building on earlier research that mainly concentrated on binary (male/female) classification. The proposed system has two primary objectives: robust preprocessing and feature extraction, and multi-model classification for gender prediction. Each audio sample was processed to extract MFCCs and pitch from a carefully selected and balanced dataset of male, female, and transgender voices that was standardized to 16 kHz. Five popular machine learning models - Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and XGBoost - were trained and evaluated. Data augmentation techniques, including minor pitch shifting and noise addition, were applied to improve model generalization, only for limited transgender samples to reduce data imbalance. The results show that the integration of the MFCC and pitch features with augmentation significantly improved performance, achieving a total accuracy of over 97% in both both SVM and MLP models. This study underscores the effectiveness of feature fusion and data balancing in multi-class gender classification and promotes inclusivity in modern voice recognition systems.

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction and Detection of 5G-Induced Nonlinear Interference in Radio Altimeters
Abstract: Systems coexisting with mid-band 5G with aeronautical radio altimeters (RAs) have brought about a substantial safety issue by adjacent-band electromagnetic interference that has the potential to cause nonlinear distortion, compress gain on the IF, and cause errors in altitude measurements. These mechanisms are found to be described by conventional analytical and simulation-based studies, which do not have the ability to predict the severity of interference quantitatively, nor do they have the ability to detect the degradation of performance in real time. In this paper, a machine learning-based scheme will be suggested to detect and forecast the effect of 5 G on RAs due to interference. Classification and regression models were built using the features obtained by using the IF spectral responses and experimental injection measurements that were used to estimate the state of interference, height-error ratio, and the onset of nonlinear saturation. The offered classifier was found to be 98.4 percent accurate, and the regression model was able to predict height-error ratios with a ratio error rate of 0.37. The model found the critical interference threshold (e.g., -15 dBm at 4000 MHz) accurately, and the sensitivity of predicting the NCD conditions was 95.1 %. The outcomes prove that ML is an effective tool in improving the assessment of RA interference and assurance of safety.

Title: A Multimodal AI Framework for Tamil Speech Transcription, Translation, and Generative Visualization
Abstract: Multimodal artificial intelligence takes an integrated approach to language processing by combining various models. Tamil has over 75 million speakers worldwide but faces challenges in modern content processing because most conventional systems lack cultural understanding. This work presents a unified multimodal framework that converts Tamil audio into five synchronized outputs: Tamil transcription, English translation with cultural preservation, emotion classification, culturally relevant images, and creative text expansion. The framework includes five advanced models: Whisper Large V3 (transcription), Gemma 2 9B-IT (translation), DistilBERT (emotion analysis), FLUX.1-dev (image generation), and DeepSeek-R1 (text expansion). These operate in a parallel processing system where three independent branches work at the same time, cutting processing time by 40 percent. Experiments show 93.8 percent transcription accuracy, BLEU scores ranging from 0.68 to 0.78, 85.3 percent accuracy in emotion classification, image CLIP scores of 0.82, with a cultural relevance rating of 4.1 out of 5 from native speakers, and a text expansion ROUGE-L score of 0.76. Importantly, parallel processing keeps quality metrics the same as sequential execution without any decline. This work makes five specific contributions: (1) the first integrated Tamil-focused multimodal pipeline with cultural preservation, (2) practical application of cultural context through prompt engineering, (3) a parallel architecture that reduces latency by 40 percent, (4) emotioninformed image and text generation, and (5) a thorough evaluation that combines technical metrics with native speaker feedback. These findings show that multimodal systems can promote linguistic variety and digital accessibility for lowresource languages, laying the groundwork for culturally-aware content transformation in the Tamil ecosystem.

Title: LLM-Based Bitrate Selection Method for CMR-Supported Audio Codec
Abstract: Recent advances in AI-driven network algorithms have aimed to enhance user experience under diverse network conditions. However, designing and validating optimal AI models tailored to specific network environments and objectives remains a challenge for developers. To address this, frameworks such as netLLM [1], which integrates pretrained large language models (LLMs) with multimodal encoders, network heads, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) [2], have been proposed and shown to improve performance through offline fine-tuning. In this paper, we extend the concept of netLLM to the bitrate optimization problem of audio codecs supporting Codec Mode Request (CMR). Unlike conventional offline training approaches, we propose an online learning-based bitrate selection method that dynamically adapts to fluctuating real-time communication environments. Our method leverages pretrained LLMs to adjust audio stream bitrates according to network conditions, achieving significant improvements in speech quality, as measured by the E-MODEL R-factor [4], compared to conventional AI models [7]. This study demonstrates an effective approach to audio streaming optimization through online fine-tuning, offering a novel pathway for improving speech quality under variable network conditions.

Title: An interpretable intelligent recognition method for voltage signals induced by wear debris in lubricating oil
Abstract: Monitoring and evaluating the in-service condition of equipment in real time is essential for maintaining the stable operation of large-scale complex electromechanical systems. Inductive oil debris sensors detect wear particles in lubricating oil via electromagnetic induction, providing a reliable basis for assessing the wear condition of critical mechanical components, and have been widely applied in the maintenance of large-scale mechanical equipment. However, the induced voltage signals generated by debris are usually weak and are difficult to identify accurately by manual feature extraction under the influence of various interferences, which limits the identification accuracy and generalization capability of inductive oil debris sensors. To address this issue, this paper proposes an intelligent recognition method for oil debris signals, referred to as PCatten. Firstly, the morphological stability of debris-induced signals under multiscale filtering is exploited to construct multiscale filtering features, which characterize the key geometric profiles and energy distribution of debris events and provide physically meaningful input representations for subsequent deep learning. Subsequently, a parallel convolution module is designed to perform branch-wise deep convolutional modeling of features at different scales, and an improved fusion attention module is introduced to adaptively recalibrate feature weights along the channel and temporal dimensions, thereby highlighting debrissensitive components and suppressing complex background interference. Finally, the reconstructed multiscale feature sequence is fed into a Vision Transformer, which captures long-range dependencies and cross-scale correlations through the self-attention mechanism, enabling accurate discrimination of debris-induced voltage signals under strong interference and low signal-to-noise ratios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves excellent performance on both three-coil sensor dataset and high-gradient static magnetic field sensor dataset, the interference elimination rate, debris identification rate, and debris identification accuracy are 99. 72%, 98. 94%, and 99. 44%, respectively, and the proposed method still exhibits superior debris-detection performance compared with traditional algorithms under low signal-to-noise ratios ranging from -5 to 0 dB.

Title: Graph-Structured Deep Learning Framework for Multi-task Contention Identification with High-dimensional Metrics
Abstract: This study addresses the challenge of accurately identifying multi-task contention types in high-dimensional system environments and proposes a unified contention classification framework that integrates representation transformation, structural modeling, and a task decoupling mechanism. The method first constructs system state representations from high-dimensional metric sequences, applies nonlinear transformations to extract cross-dimensional dynamic features, and integrates multiple source information such as resource utilization, scheduling behavior, and task load variations within a shared representation space. It then introduces a graph-based modeling mechanism to capture latent dependencies among metrics, allowing the model to learn competitive propagation patterns and structural interference across resource links. On this basis, task-specific mapping structures are designed to model the differences among contention types and enhance the classifier's ability to distinguish multiple contention patterns. To achieve stable performance, the method employs an adaptive multi-task loss weighting strategy that balances shared feature learning with task-specific feature extraction and generates final contention predictions through a standardized inference process. Experiments conducted on a public system trace dataset demonstrate advantages in accuracy, recall, precision, and F1, and sensitivity analyses on batch size, training sample scale, and metric dimensionality further confirm the model's stability and applicability. The study shows that structured representations and multi-task classification based on high-dimensional metrics can significantly improve contention pattern recognition and offer a reliable technical approach for performance management in complex computing environments.

Title: OFTNet: Omni-Feature and Texture-Aware Enhancement Learning Network for Continuous Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
Abstract: Continuous-scale super-resolution (CSSR) for remote sensing images (RSIs) offers critical flexibility for diverse Earth observation tasks, overcoming the fixed-scale limitations of conventional SR methods. However, current CSSR methods are primarily tailored for natural images, failing to address the unique characteristics of remote sensing scenes. Unlike object-centric natural images with clear foregrounds, RSIs feature arbitrary orientations, vast scale variations, and dense repetitive patterns. First, standard hierarchical extractors in existing methods exhibit limited receptive fields, struggling to capture the global context required for large-scale land covers while preserving the fine-grained details of small targets. Second, the inherent spectral bias in implicit neural representations (INRs) exacerbates the loss of high-frequency information, causing severe over-smoothing in regions with intricate textures. To address these challenges, we propose an omni-feature and texture-aware enhancement learning network (OFTNet), a novel network specifically designed for continuous-scale RSI super-resolution (SR). Our method introduces a powerful omni-feature enhancement and refinement pipeline, comprising three key modules: an omni-feature enhancement module (OFEM) that synergistically models global spatial dependencies, interchannel correlations, and multiscale local patterns; a texture-aware enhancement module (TAEM) that explicitly preserves high-frequency information and models nonlocal spatial correlations; and a learnable weighting aggregation module (LWAM) for intelligent, context-aware feature aggregation. Extensive experiments on commonly used benchmark remote sensing datasets demonstrate that OFTNet achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of in-distribution scales, while also showing robust and highly competitive performance on out-of-distribution (OOD) scales.

Title: A hybrid STL-LightGBM framework with probabilistic forecasting for Influenza A incidence in the post-pandemic Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Influenza A outbreaks in Saudi Arabia exhibit different seasonal patterns, influenced by significant changes, including a near-total halt during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2021) and a substantial rebound, as evidenced by national surveillance data, until the end of 2023. Traditional time-series models rely on stationarity and stable seasonal patterns; however, these assumptions are significantly undermined by regime shifts. This study introduces a forecasting method that uses light gradient boost machine (LightGBM) regression, along with Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL), to better track influenza in changing contexts. The proposed method adapts to the evolving epidemiological dynamics shaped by policy and behavioral changes by decomposing the incidence series into long-term trends, stable annual seasonal components, and irregular residual fluctuations prior to nonlinear learning. Exploratory analysis supports strong winter seasonality, linear correlations with meteorological variables, and major structural disruptions linked to pandemic-related interventions. shows how standard SARIMAX and seasonal baseline models cannot be used across all epidemiological regimes. The hybrid model, when evaluated during the test window, shows strong out-of-sample performance, substantially outperforming the benchmark models (R2 = 0.831, MAE = 89.0). In-sample fitting throughout the study period indicates a high degree of representational capacity (R2 = 0.987). The framework is further extended to probabilistic forecasting via quantile regression, resulting in accurately calibrated 95% prediction intervals. The uncertainty in the predictions increases appropriately during periods of epidemiological disruption, highlighting the importance of uncertainty-aware prediction under structural change. The proposed STL-LightGBM architecture is a resilient and comprehensible instrument for monitoring influenza in post-pandemic contexts, facilitating early warning systems and expeditious public health decision-making in Saudi Arabia and analogous regions.

Title: Semiconductor Metrology and Inspection with Ultrafast Coherent Extreme Ultraviolet Light Source (Invited)
Abstract: Significance The rapid advancement of fields such as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing has intensified demand for advanced, high-performance integrated circuits (ICs). Lithography, as a core fabrication step in integrated circuit manufacturing, represents the most complex and critical process, directly determining chip performance. As lithographic processes evolve toward cutting-edge nodes, the scale of features to be patterned and defects to be detected continues to shrink. This miniaturization imposes stringent requirements on next-generation metrology tools. Measurement techniques based on short-wavelength, high-brightness, and coherent extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light sources have therefore emerged as a pivotal research direction. Progress From the perspective of lithography light source development, lithography systems have evolved from high-pressure mercury discharge lamps in the ultraviolet band to ArF excimer lasers in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) band, culminating in today’s state-of-the-art EUV lithography machines. The dramatic reduction in lithography wavelength—from 193 nm to 13.5 nm—necessitates entirely new optical components and materials compatible with EUV conditions, requiring renewed emphasis on optical component testing and material interaction studies at the operational wavelength (i.e., 13.5 nm). For instance, the shift from DUV transmissive photomasks to EUV reflective masks introduces phase-sensitive defects, creating new challenges for mask inspection. Similarly, EUV photoresist development must achieve reduced line edge roughness and controlled shot noise, imposing increasingly stringent demands at advanced process nodes. Furthermore, as process nodes and device dimensions continue to scale down, and integrated circuits adopt three-dimensional architectures, the need for three-dimensional (3D) metrology grows significantly. These trends introduce multiple technical challenges for measurement equipment related to feature miniaturization, structural complexity, and novel materials. Future progress will require extensive technological innovation to meet the specifications outlined in the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors (ITRS) and those demanded by integrated device manufacturers (IDMs). Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy, leveraging its short-wavelength radiation, offers unique advantages for metrology and defect inspection at advanced nodes. Its spectral range—spanning several to tens of nanometers—enables nanometer-scale spatial resolution. Additionally, the limited penetration depth of EUV radiation allows non-destructive imaging of internal structures within micron-thick samples, while element-specific absorption edges in this spectral region facilitate high-contrast imaging without labeling or staining. When combined with quantitative phase-sensitive detection methods, coherent EUV sources enable even nanoscale material differentiation, making the development of quantitative EUV-band metrology a critical research frontier. With semiconductor technology scaling to sub-nanometer dimensions and the adoption of three-dimensional stacked architectures, thermal management in integrated circuits has become a paramount concern. Understanding and engineering material properties at the nanoscale represent major scientific objectives with significant technological implications. For example, elucidating the dynamics of heat transfer and dissipation at the nanoscale can accelerate the design of next-generation chip architectures featuring lower power consumption, higher integration density, and increased operating frequencies. Indeed, a device’s thermal relaxation time influences its maximum sustainable frequency, while inadequate heat removal leading to excessive temperature rise may result in irreversible degradation or failure. Likewise, insights into nanoscale mechanical behavior can enhance the efficiency of micro-/nano-electromechanical systems (MEMS/NEMS) in harvesting energy from ambient vibrations. Transient gratings in the extreme ultraviolet regime have substantially enhanced Fourier-domain measurements of high-wavevector excitations, enabling contactless, all-optical characterization of nanoscale thermal and mechanical phenomena. Conclusions and Prospects This paper reviews the exploration and recent advances in semiconductor metrology and inspection technologies based on EUV light sources, primarily focusing on EUV coherent diffraction imaging (CDI) and EUV scattering measurements. Coherent diffraction imaging offers nanometer-scale resolution and enables non-destructive mapping of sample chemical composition. Meanwhile, EUV scattering extends the capabilities of conventional white-light optical critical dimension (OCD) metrology and defect inspection methods—widely employed in semiconductor manufacturing—into the shorter-wavelength EUV regime. Furthermore, this paper discusses the application of ultrafast EUV light sources in measuring elastic modulus and investigating thermal transport in nanoscale structures. Specifically, nanostructure thermal transport studies leveraging ultrafast EUV sources introduce a powerful new methodology. These advancements hold significant promise for next-generation semiconductor metrology and inspection technologies.

Title: DravHate-XAI: A Multimodal Transformer Approach for Hate Speech Detection
Abstract: Dealing with online hate speech is a nightmare, specifically in those linguistic communities which are very small and have not been taken into consideration by AI-developed differently. What we do is exactly the opposite; our work is directly filling the gap for the three major Dravidian languages - Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam. We have implemented a single structure that is capable of identifying hateful content not only in the written form but in speech as well. The first step is speech transcription using Wav2Vec2. We also provide a model for performance evaluation with a big emphasis on openness. Our measuring instrument involves a spectrum of methods starting from classic SVM classifiers and going up to various transformer (e.g. XLM-RoBERTa, IndicBERT, MuRIL, DistilBERT, ALBERT) methods. For each model, we have made use of our explainable AI tools, LIME and SHAP, to enhance the understandability of the predictions and to help explain the static conclusions produced by the system. The outcome is a system that is consistent in its operations for both written and spoken materials in all three languages. What is more, we provided the evidence that high accuracy and transparency are not mutually exclusive. We have shown that it is possible to develop ethical and trustworthy moderation tools for languages that have been traditionally overlooked by AI.

Title: Comparative Evaluation of Thai Speech-to-Text Models and Entity Extraction Methods for Beverage Ordering Systems
Abstract: Deploying robust voice-based ordering systems for tonal languages like Thai requires balancing transcription fidelity with real-time responsiveness. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of twelve end-to-end pipeline configurations, combining three Speech-to-Text (STT) architectures-OpenAI Whisper, FasterWhisper, and Biodatlab-Whisper-with four entity extraction strategies. We benchmark performance on a specialized beverage-ordering domain using an independent test set of 50 utterances (comprising both real-world recordings and AI-generated samples). Experimental results demonstrate that Faster-Whisper optimizes the latency-accuracy trade-off, achieving the lowest transcription latency via its optimized inference engine. Crucially, we address the issue of cascading errors by implementing a domain-adapted Custom NER model, fine-tuned on a synthetic corpus of 201,245 labeled samples. This proposed model significantly mitigates upstream transcription noise, achieving a peak entity-wise accuracy of 77.5%, drastically outperforming rule-based and general-purpose baselines. These findings offer actionable architectural guidelines for building scalable, real-time Thai voice interfaces.

Title: Unmasking Deepfakes: An AI Approach with Audio-Visual Analysis
Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models has enabled the generation of unrealistically convincing manipulated audio-visual content, commonly referred to as DeepFakes. This type of content poses a serious threat to digital trust, security, biometric authentication systems, and the authenticity of digital media. In order to address these concerns, this work proposes a robust DeepFake detection system that jointly takes into consideration both input visual and audio signals. Different from methods that rely exclusively on either facial appearance or speech patterns, the system integrates deep spatial feature extraction using a ResNet architecture with temporal audio modeling through Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This framework extracts from the visual modality facial texture inconsistencies, micro-expressions, and blending artifacts, while from the audio modality, it models speech features, pitch variations, and lip-audio synchronization patterns. In contrast, the presented approach integrates high-level abstractions from these two modalities to identify the very subtle incongruities that usually arise in manipulated content. Extensive experiments over benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework significantly outperforms unimodal techniques in terms of accuracy, compression resistance, and cross-dataset generalizability. Moreover, the model provides reliable performance under low-resolution and noisy conditions, which makes it suitable for practical applications with resource-limited deployments.

Title: Interpretable Gender Classification from Malayalam Speech
Abstract: Speech serves as a primary medium of human communication and conveys important paralinguistic information such as speaker gender. This work investigates acoustic featurebased gender classification for Malayalam, a low resource Dravidian language that remains underexplored in speech processing research. A multi-speaker Malayalam speech corpus has been used in this study, from which a comprehensive feature set comprising of spectral, energy based and voice based characteristics of speech such as Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, Jitter, Shimmer etc. have been extracted. Multiple machine learning classifiers are compared, among which Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy of 94.65% and a weighted F-measure of 94.6% on unseen speakers under speaker independent evaluation. Statistical significance tests, including McNemar, paired t-test, Wilcoxon, and Friedman tests, confirm meaningful performance differences across models. Robustness analysis under additive white noise demonstrates that Logistic Regression is the model most robust to noise with 90.84% accuracy at 20dB SNR, 84.90% at 15dB SNR and 82.88% at 10 dB SNR. Feature-level interpretability using SHAP on the best model further highlights the dominant role of MFCC-derived and spectral features.

Title: RoPEHAR: A Real-Time Rotary Position Encoding Informer for mmWave-Based Human Activity Recognition in Substations
Abstract: Safety monitoring of power operations in substations is crucial for accident prevention. However, traditional methods such as wearable devices and video surveillance suffer from limitations including high costs and reliance on lighting conditions. A solution that integrates millimeter-wave radar with deep learning ensures operational compliance by high precision gesture detection. This paper proposes RoPEHAR, a human activity recognition system based on millimeter-wave radar, which combines traditional transformer architecture with rotary positional encoding, specifically designed for human posture recognition in indoor industrial environments. To reduce interference from the coupling of human and instrument signals and noise in electrical scenarios, RoPEHAR introduces a hybrid filtering pipeline that combines hierarchical SNR denoising with enhanced DBSCAN clustering to accurately segment the point cloud data of limbs and instruments. The core innovation lies in the introduction of a spatiotemporal Informer, Roformer. It enhances the 3D-space vector information about data points through dynamic rotary positional encoding. This system effectively models limb motion trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that RoPEHAR achieves high-precision performance, reaching an accuracy of 95.8%, enabling real-time and reliable activity recognition for substation safety monitoring.

Title: MAFNet-DETR: Multi-Branch Adaptive Fusion Network for Small Object Detection in UAV Aerial Images
Abstract: Small object detection in high-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery presents formidable challenges, including severely constrained target scale and intricate background interference. To address these issues, this paper proposes MAFNet-DETR, a novel detection framework built upon RT-DETR-R18, designed to augment feature representation capability on densely populated small-object benchmarks such as VisDrone2019. MAFNet-DETR systematically advances detection performance through four core architectural innovations: the Three-branch Gated Enhancement Block (TGEB), which employs large-kernel convolutions to capture expansive global contextual information in conjunction with a gating mechanism for adaptive salient feature modulation, substantially elevating the model's perceptual sensitivity to sparse and inconspicuous signals; the Global-Local Spatial Attention (GLSA) module, which adopts a dual-branch parallel architecture to independently extract fine-grained local spatial details and long-range global dependencies, thereby achieving an effective equilibrium between local perceptual acuity and holistic contextual comprehension; the Adaptive Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (Adaptive-BiFPN), which incorporates a dual-weight fusion mechanism coupling spatially adaptive weights with globally learnable weights to realize fine-grained and computationally efficient multi-scale feature aggregation, significantly mitigating the degradation of small-object detail information during hierarchical feature propagation; and the Lightweight Progressive Upsampling Block (LPUB), which achieves high-fidelity feature map resolution restoration through the synergistic integration of depthwise separable convolutions, channel shuffling, and shift channel mixing operations. Extensive experimental evaluations conducted on three publicly available benchmark datasets - VisDrone2019, SIMD, and AI-TOD - demonstrate that, relative to the baseline RT-DETR-R18, the proposed method achieves improvements in mAP50 of 6.1%, 4.6%, and 4.8%, and in mAP 50-95 of 4.5%, 2.7%, and 3.3%, respectively, while concurrently reducing the parameter count by 12.46%, 8.7%, and 9.45%. The proposed model attains substantial gains in detection accuracy and exhibits strong applicability to small object detection under complex background conditions.

Title: Microphone Optimization and Development for AI-Based Detection of Flying Wildlife
Abstract: Acoustic monitoring is crucial for assessing the impact of renewable energy projects on biodiversity. However, commonly used Micro Electro Mechanical System (MEMS) microphones are susceptible to electromagnetic interference and ambient noise, which degrades the quality of recordings. This study compared the performance of a MEMS microphone with an electret microphone using bird songs from Monfragüe National Park and metrics such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), total harmonic distortion (THD) and acoustic diversity index (ADI). The results revealed that the electret microphones outperformed MEMS in noise reduction, signal clarity and sensitivity, providing higher quality recordings that benefit artificial intelligence analysis for accurate species detection. This improvement is critical for more precise assessments of the environmental impact of renewable energy projects and for informed decision-making in the sustainable management of these infrastructures. These findings support the integration of electret-based systems into large-scale acoustic monitoring networks and the development of long-term biodiversity databases, strengthening the role of bioacoustics in conservation strategies aligned with renewable energy expansion.

Title: Adaptive Efficacy Assessment Method for Music Education via Multimodal Deep Learning Fusion
Abstract: Addressing the limitations inherent in traditional music education assessment - specifically strong subjectivity, delayed feedback, and the loss of technical details due to single-modality information - this paper proposes a novel Adaptive Efficacy Assessment Method (MAAF) based on multimodal deep learning fusion. The method constructs an audio-visual dual-stream neural network architecture: the auditory channel utilizes an improved ResNet to extract high-dimensional acoustic features from Mel-spectrograms; the visual channel integrates OpenPose hand keypoint detection with Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCN) to capture fine-grained performance techniques, employing a confidence-based masking strategy to effectively suppress occlusion noise. Furthermore, to address the challenge of spatiotemporal asynchrony in heterogeneous data, we design a linear interpolation alignment strategy and an Adaptive Gated Attention Mechanism to realize dynamic weight allocation for audio-visual features. Empirical research based on the URMP dataset and a newly constructed Real-World Classroom Dataset (RWCD), validated by expert reliability tests, demonstrates that the proposed model achieves an assessment accuracy (PCC=0.898) that is significantly superior to mainstream SOTA architectures (e.g., Transformers). Furthermore, extensive experiments on heterogeneous instruments (e.g., Piano, Guitar) confirm the model's robustness and cross-domain generalization capabilities. The model effectively simulates the multi-sensory collaborative assessment logic of human experts.

Title: Improve OMI Observations on Ground-Level NO2 Using Multiple Observations, Simulations, and Machine Learning
Abstract: Nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf>2</inf> ) is a criteria air pollutant with adverse impacts on human health and the environment. An accurate ground-level NO<inf>2</inf> dataset with high spatial resolution is beneficial for NO<inf>2</inf> pollution management and public health studies. In this study, we leverage long-term ozone monitoring instrument (OMI) NO<inf>2</inf> observations by converting OMI NO<inf>2</inf> vertical column densities into ground-level NO<inf>2</inf> concentrations and improving its spatial resolution to 1×1 km by using the light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) learning model in three metro areas in USA: Metro New York, New York (NY), Baltimore, Maryland (MD), and Houston, Texas (TX). Our improved ground-level NO2 products achieved robust performance across all regions, with a correlation coefficient of 0.897 in NY, 0.876 in Baltimore, and 0.914 in Houston. The corresponding root-mean-squared error (RMSE) was 3.278 ppb in NY, 2.385 ppb in Baltimore, and 2.084 ppb in Houston, respectively. Furthermore, the products effectively captured the temporal variations in observed NO<inf>2</inf> concentrations across all cities. We also found that emissions, population density, boundary layer height (BLH), and winds are consistently important contributors to NO<inf>2</inf> concentrations across all three cities, while each city also has its own significant factors. This attribution analysis will be helpful to state and local air pollution agencies in their air pollution management efforts.

Title: Real-Time Symbolic Music Accompaniment Generation for Edge Devices
Abstract: Music generation is a complex and challenging problem that has made significant progress through recent machine learning solutions. The challenge lies not only in rendering natural-sounding audio but also in capturing the underlying musical structure. This paper presents a real-time system that generates a musical accompaniment for an input lead melody in the MIDI format. In this paper, we introduce REMIBlock, a novel tokenization approach, and show that it is suited for accompaniment generation. Our method uses the GPT-2 architecture [11], optimized for efficient on-device performance, to generate accompaniments that are rhythmically and harmonically coherent with a musician’s performance. The model used in this papers reaches a perplexity of 7.69 on the test set, proving the model’s ability to understand musical language. Additionally, using two metrics—groove and scale consistency—proposed in [3], we show that the generated accompaniments closely match the ground truth, differing by at most 3.4%. This further highlights our model’s ability to capture the intricacies of musical language. The model weights and inference code is available at https://github.com/UncleBen420/JazzyGPT2.

Title: Real-Time Detection Method for Cracked Eggs Based on Improved YOLOv8 and Dual Verification with Triple Classification Granularity
Abstract: Addressing the urgent need for real-time detection of cracked eggs on production lines, this study proposes a high-precision real-time detection algorithm based on an improved YOLOv8 framework. This study innovatively introduced a dual-detection method, incorporating a "crack region" classification to assist in distinguishing between intact eggs and cracked eggs. This method identifies cracked eggs by recognizing either local or overall crack characteristics, effectively reducing both false negatives and false positives. At the architectural level, the model innovatively integrates Weighted Bidirectional Feature Pyramid (BiFPN) to optimize multi-scale feature fusion, Deformable Convolutional Network v2 (DCNv2) to enhance perception of irregular geometric deformations in cracks, Weighted Intersection over Union v2 (WIoUv2) loss function to improve detection accuracy for occluded samples, and adds a small object detection layer to strengthen recognition of minute defects. Experiments demonstrate that the improved model achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 92.9% on the test set, representing a 5.2% improvement over the original model and outperforming current mainstream detection models. In real-world production deployment testing, the system achieved a real-time detection speed of 45 FPS, with a false negative rate of only 0.46% and a false positive rate of 2.18% for intact eggs, while keeping the false positive rate for broken eggs below 2%. This performance far surpasses that of the original model and fully meets the requirements for industrial-grade real-time online quality inspection. Title: MSRA-Net: Multiscale Residual Attention Network for Land Use Land Cover Scene Classification From Remote Sensing Images
Abstract: Remote sensing image classification plays an important role in environmental monitoring, urban planning, and disaster management. Current deep-learning methods have major limitations, including single-scale feature extraction, suboptimal attention mechanisms, high computational complexity, and poor spectral-spatial integration, indicating the need for stronger classification frameworks. In this article, we propose a novel multiscale residual attention network (MSRA-Net), a multiscale residual attention network, composed of several multicomponent approaches to address these limitations. MSRA-Net incorporates adaptive inverted bottleneck blocks for efficient multiscale feature extraction, which are followed by lightweight dense blocks to promote feature reuse and gradient flow. After that, a comprehensive attention mechanism is adopted for optimal spectral-spatial integration, incorporating multiscale channel attention to dynamically weigh feature importance. We use an advanced cross-scale feature fusion module with attention-weighted aggregation to effectively represent features across different scales, along with an atrous spatial pyramid pooling based classification head that captures contextual information using dilated convolutions. Training is performed using a comprehensive data augmentation framework, AdamW optimization, and an early stopping strategy to ensure robust classification performance. The proposed model is evaluated on two publicly diverse datasets, such as MLRSNet and NWPU-RESISC45. On these datasets, the proposed model achieved superior performance with overall class accuracies of 93.71% and 97.95%, respectively, significantly outperforming conventional pretrained and contemporary state-of-the-art models.

Title: MOSAIC: A Unified Multilingual Deep Learning Framework for Detecting Manipulated Speech Audio Using Geometry-Aware Foundation Model Representations
Abstract: Audio deepfakes (AD) are increasingly used to spread misinformation, yet many detectors are evaluated in monolingual or narrowly multilingual settings and break under language mismatch. In this study, we take a step toward truly multilingual forensic audio deepfake detection (ADD). We conduct a systematic evaluation of pretrained speech encoders in multilingual settings. We observe that different pretrained encoders capture complementary spoofing cues arising from their distinct pretraining objectives. To leverage this complementarity, we propose MOSAIC, which fuses pretrained speech representations across multiple geometric spaces. MOSAIC performs gated additive fusion in hyperbolic, spherical, and Euclidean spaces, followed by self-attention for feature refinement. Experiments on large-scale multilingual benchmarks demonstrate strong crosslanguage generalization of the proposed framework. MOSAIC achieves SOTA performance, with MMS+PaSST attaining 0.02% EER on SpeechFake-MD and 0.07% on MLAAD. Through MOSAIC and complementary pretrained FMs, we attain top performance over individual FMs and standard fusion baselines. Such manipulated speech constitutes a form of audio misinformation that can mislead listeners across languages and platforms.

Title: Machine Vision based Chili Species Recognition
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive exploration of automated chili species classification using deep learning. We cover the full pipeline - data collection, preprocessing, model selection, and experimental analysis. A dataset of chili pepper images spanning multiple species was manually curated and augmented to increase diversity and size, then split 80/20 into training and test sets. Three state-of-the-art CNN backbones, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, and Xception, were employed with transfer learning, initializing from large-scale image recognition weights. Each model was fine-tuned and optimized for accurate chili classification. Experiments yielded strong results, with the best configuration achieving 93% test accuracy. For each species, we report precision, recall, and F<inf>1</inf>-score, showing consistent performance across classes and validating both the model choices and the augmentation strategy. Beyond the technical results, the work has practical implications for agriculture, biodiversity research, and plant breeding programs. An automated chili species classification system can streamline field operations, enable precise species identification, and support monitoring of plant diversity and conservation efforts. Overall, our findings demonstrate that modern deep learning, coupled with careful dataset design, provides an effective and scalable approach to fine-grained plant identification. The approach is lightweight enough for deployment on modest hardware and can be extended to related crops with minimal additional labeling effort.

Title: Beyond the Leaderboard: A Survey of the Science of Evaluation, Benchmarking, and Methodologies for Large Language Models
Abstract: The field of artificial intelligence is grappling with an evaluation crisis. Despite the proliferation of benchmarks and the relentless pursuit of state-of-the-art scores on public leaderboards, confidence in what these metrics truly measure is eroding. Large Language Models (LLMs) now consistently outperform humans on established benchmarks. However, their real-world utility is often undermined by brittleness, a lack of common sense, and a tendency to generate harmful or factually incorrect content. This paper argues that this disconnect stems from treating evaluation as a competitive afterthought rather than a rigorous metrological science. We contend that the current paradigm, characterized by static benchmarks and a narrow focus on accuracy, is fundamentally ill-equipped to assess the complex, multifaceted capabilities of modern LLMs. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive reference for the science of LLM evaluation by making four principal contributions. First, we offer a historical analysis of evaluation, tracing its evolution from traditional lexical-overlap metrics to the massive, holistic frameworks of today. Second, we introduce a systematic taxonomy of evaluation methodologies, classifying them into five key paradigms: static benchmarks, dynamic and adaptive evaluation, interactive and agentic evaluation, human-in-the-loop evaluation, and model-based evaluation (LLM-as-a-Judge). Third, we conduct a critical analysis of the pathologies plaguing the field, with a deep focus on the existential threat of data contamination, the perverse incentives of the leaderboard obsession, and the pervasive mismatch between benchmark performance and true capability. Finally, we propose a new conceptual framework, the Benchmark Lifecycle, to professionalize the design, validation, deployment, monitoring, and retirement of evaluation instruments. By framing evaluation as a scientific discipline, we aim to move beyond the leaderboard and build a more robust, reliable, and trustworthy foundation for measuring progress in artificial intelligence.

Title: Temporal Data and Short-Time Averages Improve Multiphase Mass Flow Metering
Abstract: Reliable flow measurements are essential in many industries, but current instruments often fail to accurately estimate multiphase flows, which are frequently encountered in real-world operations. Combining machine learning (ML) algorithms with accurate single-phase flowmeters has therefore received extensive research attention in recent years. The Coriolis mass flowmeter is a widely used single-phase meter that provides direct mass flow measurements, which ML models can be trained to correct, thereby reducing measurement errors in multiphase conditions. This paper demonstrates that preserving temporal information significantly improves model performance in such scenarios. We compare a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a windowed MLP, a long short-term memory model, and a convolutional neural network (CNN) on three-phase air–water–oil flow data from 342 experiments. Whereas prior work typically compresses each experiment into a single averaged sample, we instead compute short-time averages from within each experiment and train models that preserve temporal information at several downsampling intervals. The CNN performed best at 0.25 Hz with approximately 95% of relative errors below 13%, a normalized root mean squared error of 0.03, and a mean absolute percentage error of approximately 4.3%, clearly outperforming the best single-averaged model and demonstrating that short-time averaging within individual experiments is preferable. While the CNN performed best, all three sequence models outperformed the non-temporal baseline MLP, clearly illustrating the benefits of temporal data and short-time averages. Results are consistent acrossmultiple data splits and random seeds, demonstrating robustness.

Title: Application of Computer Vision Technology in the Recognition of Guzheng Playing Posture
Abstract: This study addresses the performance teaching needs of traditional Chinese Guzheng and attempts to introduce computer vision and deep learning technologies into gesture recognition tasks. By constructing a dataset that includes various Guzheng playing actions, image sequences are collected during the performance process. Combined with convolutional neural networks for feature extraction, this approach achieves automatic recognition of multiple basic gestures. The model employs an optimized ResNet50 structure, maintaining high recognition accuracy under standardized image input and weighted classifiers. Experiments show that the system performs stably in recognizing typical actions and has a certain tolerance for complex action transitions and partial hand occlusions. When deployed in educational settings, the system can provide real-time feedback and visual presentations, assisting teachers in evaluating students’ gesture standards and enhancing interactive teaching effects. From the perspective of engineering implementation and practicality in education, this research provides methodological support for the integration of traditional arts and artificial intelligence, laying the groundwork for future intelligent musical instrument training systems. Overall results indicate that this technical approach holds practical significance and application potential in improving Guzheng performance quality and reducing teaching costs.

Title: Data-Driven Energy Planning in Developing Countries: An Integrated LEAP-Machine Learning Approach
Abstract: Developing countries encounter substantial obstacles in regional energy planning stemming from scarce historical data and insufficient forecasting methodologies, thereby impeding the formulation of effective sustainable energy transition strategies. Conventional Long-range Energy Alternative Planning (LEAP) models frequently depend on static assumptions that diminish projection accuracy, especially under data-limited conditions. This study develops and applies an integrated hybrid algorithm–LEAP (HA–LEAP) framework to improve the precision of long-term regional energy planning and assess sustainable energy transition scenarios in Gorontalo Province, Indonesia. The research utilizes a quantitative case study methodology that integrates artificial intelligence with LEAP modeling, incorporating genetic algorithms and various optimization techniques. The HA–LEAP framework exhibits significant predictive performance enhancements compared to conventional LEAP approaches, achieving higher accuracy and diminished forecasting errors. Modeling results project a fundamental transformation in Gorontalo’s energy portfolio, with renewable energy penetration rising from 1.0% in 2015–41.8% by 2050, while petroleum dependency declines by 83% to 15.4%. Energy elasticity projections indicate successful decoupling between economic growth and energy consumption. This investigation presents the first comprehensive artificial intelligence-integrated energy planning methodology specifically designed for developing regions experiencing data constraints. The framework provides policymakers with superior analytical instruments for evidence-based sustainable energy transition planning, demonstrating the viability of ambitious renewable energy targets while preserving energy security objectives.

Title: Framework for Personalized Music and Lyrics Generation
Abstract: The Framework for Personalized Music and Lyrics Generation is designed to generate customized lyrics and corresponding melodies based on user input. The framework comprises two key components: lyrics generation and music melody generation. The lyrics generation module explores and compares two different approaches: topic modeling-based generation and retrieval-augmented generation. The effectiveness of these approaches is evaluated using various linguistic and structural metrics, including perplexity score, repetition score, coherence, and syllable variance. The music melody generation module takes the syllabified lyrics as input and generates suitable musical notes using different sequential models. The performance of these models is assessed based on statistical metrics to determine their effectiveness in producing musically coherent melodies. By integrating these components, the proposed framework aims to enhance personalized music composition by leveraging advanced techniques in natural language processing and deep learning.

Title: A laser embedding frame work for cross-lingual hate speech detection
Abstract: Detection of hate speech in multilingual as well as code-switched settings continues to remain a major challenge for online content moderation. This paper presents a new method that employs Language-Agnostic SEntence Representations (LASER) embeddings with token-level language identification along with adapter layers for efficient hate speech identification in 13 languages. Our method provides three contributions: (1) token-level language identification to analyze code-switching behavior, (2) light-weight adapter layers for per-language few-shot learning with no loss of multilingual representation, as well as (3) an explanation module with clear decision-making. We experiment on a multilingual collection of 219,981 samples, which shows that our new model attains an F1-score of 0.7337 as well as AUC-ROC of 0.8802 with a 0.65 percentage point improvement over a baseline. Token-level analysis shows that 60.78% of text samples display code-switching behavior, indicating a need for fine-grain language identification. Our explanation study shows that LASER embeddings contribute 3.5 times more than language features towards final prediction. The generalizability of the model extends over a large range of languages that cover European, Asian, as well as low-resource languages, with good cross-lingual performance with hate detection rates between 20.10% as well as 48.71% across test languages.

Title: Real-Time Human Tracking and Predictive Danger Zone Forecasting for Public Safety
Abstract: Community safety and security in high-density urban environments such as public transport terminals, commercial zones, schools, colleges, and places of public assembly need precautionary monitoring of pedestrian movement to mitigate accidents, risks, and hazards. Existing and available surveillance infrastructure primarily supports incident-based monitoring with limited prediction-driven capability to identify risks and hazards prior to occurrence. This proposed research paper introduces a novel implementation framework titled "Real-Time Human Tracking and Predictive Danger Zone Forecasting for Public Safety". The proposed system processes and analyzes video surveillance recordings captured by the existing CCTV cameras, reduces the resolution from 720p to 480p using gray-scale conversion to reduce computational complexity, applies YOLO variants based on human object detection, and utilizes light-weight AI-powered tracking to investigate the trajectories of persons in the crowd environment. Explicitly defined high-risk and hazard zones are marked, and the proposed system focuses on single or multiple persons entering from multiple trajectories who may move towards danger or hazard-prone areas. Real-time alerts are produced as output to support early-stage intervention to reduce risks and hazards. Primary analysis demonstrates that the proposed method delivers high-performance, accurate human detection and predictive accuracy without using GPU accelerations, while maintaining computational viability for real-time visualization.

Title: Enhancing Music Pedagogy with Generative AI
Abstract: Through this article, I encourage music educators to enrich traditional pedagogical practices by embodying a spirit of exploration regarding emerging generative artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. To explore the capabilities of generative AI tools, music educators require a basic understanding of their function and limitations. Large language models may be used as an assistive tool for (a) curricular planning, (b) administrative tasks, (c) compositional activities, and (d) reading and writing assignments. AI music generators may be used (a) to develop supplemental curricular materials, (b) to facilitate multimedia performances, (c) as an exploratory tool, (d) as a composition assistant, or (e) as a means of self-expression. By developing a foundational understanding of generative AI technologies, music educators empower themselves to effectively modernize traditional instructional approaches.

Title: Effective, Explainable, and Trustworthy Client Selection in Federated Learning
Abstract: Client selection is a pivotal process in Federated Learning (FL). Despite their contributions to the learning effectiveness of global and local models, most current client selection approaches overlook the importance of ensuring trustworthiness and providing explanations in this process to promote FL adoption. This paper introduces xCS, a novel approach that provides effective, explainable, and trustworthy client selection. xCS accomplishes effectiveness by extending the traditional FL architecture with two algorithms: one that enables Ranking and Quartile policies, and another, the Contribution Value Calculator, that computes client contributions during training using indices from game theory; remarkably, we are pioneers in proposing Banzhaf (BZ), Least Core (LC), and Johnston (JT) indices as alternatives to Shapley Values (SV) to offer explanations and trustworthiness in client selection. xCS was prototyped and extensively evaluated on the MNIST and FMNIST datasets regarding effectiveness and trustworthiness under homogeneous and heterogeneous data distributions. Results revealed that, regardless of the dataset, data heterogeneity, or index, xCS is highly effective and trustworthy, as evidenced by high accuracy and F1 score, low validation loss and convergence time, and strong robustness. Overall, results indicate that xCS is a promising solution for explainable, effective, and trustworthy client selection, showing that, in order, BZ, LC, and JT are lightweight and efficient alternatives to SV, with comparable learning performance.

Title: Subject-Independent Imagined Speech Detection via Cross-Subject Generalization and Calibration
Abstract: Achieving robust generalization across individuals remains a major challenge in electroencephalogram-based imagined-speech decoding due to substantial variability in neural activity patterns. This study examined how training dynamics and lightweight subject-specific adaptation influence cross-subject performance in a neural decoding framework. A cyclic inter-subject training approach, involving shorter per-subject training segments and frequent alternation among subjects, led to modest yet consistent improvements in decoding performance across unseen target data. Furthermore, under the subject-calibrated leave-one-subject-out scheme, incorporating only 10 % of the target subject's data for calibration achieved an accuracy of 0.781 and an AUC of 0.801, demonstrating the effectiveness of few-shot adaptation. These findings suggest that integrating cyclic training with minimal calibration provides a simple and effective strategy for developing scalable, user-adaptive brain-computer interface systems that balance generalization and personalization.

Title: Neural Signatures of Emotion Processing in Native and Non-native Speech Imagery
Abstract: This study investigates the neural signatures of emotion processing during speech imagery under native (L1) and non-native (L2) language conditions using electroencephalography (EEG). Participants performed a speech imagery (SI) task involving four valence-oriented emotion sentences, and power spectral density (PSD) features were extracted to compare full-spectrum and band-specific frequency representations. Three ma-chine learning models, including support vector machines (SVM), regularized linear discriminant analysis (RLDA), and gaussian naïve bayes(GNB), were applied to classify emotional valence. The results show that L1 processing exhibited higher performance with band-specific features, while L2 processing benefited from full-spectrum information, suggesting a more distributed neural activation pattern induced by increased cognitive load during L2 emotional processing. Alpha-band analysis further revealed language-dependent spatial differences, with L2 showing broader distributed activation across regions of interest. Channel expansion from base to extended electrode configurations did not yield substantial performance improvement in either condition, indicating that the core emotional information is localized or sufficiently captured by the base channels. These findings pro-vide insight into language-dependent affective processing during speech imagery and highlight the importance of spectral-spatial characteristics in bilingual neural decoding.

Title: 4×400 Gbit/s Coherent-Lite Transceiver for Data Center Interconnection
Abstract: Objective: The explosive growth of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and high-performance computing has driven an unprecedented surge in data center traffic. This creates an urgent demand for optical interconnect solutions that are high-bandwidth, low-cost, and low-power. Intensity-modulation direct-detection (IM-DD) technology faces limitations in transmission distance, often failing to exceed 10 km for multi-terabit capacities. Conversely, traditional coherent transceivers suffer from high complexity, cost, and power consumption, primarily due to their reliance on full-featured digital signal processors (DSPs), tunable lasers, and sophisticated packaging. To address this gap, a simplified coherent, or coherent-lite, approach is critically needed. It aims to retain the high sensitivity and spectral efficiency of coherent detection while significantly reducing system complexity. This paper proposes and demonstrates a 1.6 Tbit/s coherent-lite transceiver, configured as 4×400 Gbit/s, specifically designed for data center interconnects spanning 2–40 km. It offers a balanced and practical solution in terms of performance, power consumption, and cost. Methods: The proposed transceiver is built on system-level optimizations encompassing photonic integration, control algorithms, and advanced packaging. At its heart is a narrow-linewidth distributed feedback (DFB) laser operating in the O-band at 1310 nm. This design eliminates the need for complex wavelength locking mechanisms. A dedicated frequency offset control loop is implemented, utilizing a high-precision resistance temperature detector (RTD), a microcontroller unit (MCU), and a thermo-electric cooler (TEC). This loop actively stabilizes the laser output frequency, maintaining it within a ±400 MHz window. For signal modulation, a dual-polarization silicon photonic in-phase quadrature (IQ) modulator is employed. A key innovation is the introduction of a PN junction differential dual-arm dithering technique. This method enables rapid and stable bias point locking for the modulator, replacing conventional slower thermal dithering approaches, and lowering operational voltage requirements. To achieve high integration density, the transceiver incorporates four photonic integrated circuits (PICs) within a single OSFP-XD package using 3D flip-chip stacking technology. This packaging choice enhances electrical performance and thermal management. A central aspect of the simplification is the implementation of a streamlined DSP. Leveraging the favorable dispersion characteristics of the O-band, the DSP omits the digital dispersion compensation module required in traditional C-band coherent systems. It employs low-complexity, feed-forward algorithms for carrier phase recovery and uses fixed digital polarization rotation matrices instead of adaptive polarization tracking. These changes, along with a reduced analog-to-digital converter (ADC) sampling rate, drastically cut power consumption and silicon complexity compared to a full DSP. Results and Discussions: The fabricated transceiver underwent comprehensive experimental validation. The DFB laser demonstrated excellent performance with a calculated linewidth below 400 kHz. Long-term stability tests confirmed that the frequency offset control loop successfully maintained the carrier frequency within the designed ±400 MHz tolerance without any loss of lock. The optical spectrum of the transmitted signal, measured after fiber propagation, exhibited a 3 dB bandwidth of 78.91 GHz. In back-to-back testing, the module achieved a high receiver sensitivity of −25.56 dBm at a pre-forward error correction (FEC) bit error rate (BER) threshold of 1.11×10<sup>-2</sup> for each 400 Gbit/s channel. Constellation diagrams were obtained for the 16-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (16-QAM) signals under back-to-back and after 40 km of standard single-mode fiber transmission. These clear constellations confirmed robust signal recovery and the module’s capability for error-free 40 km transmission without optical amplification. Power consumption was measured under full 1.6 Tbit/s load at 25 °C, totaling 39.112 W. The breakdown showed DSP dominance. For a fair comparison at the same aggregate data rate, the coherent-lite design consumed only 44.2% of the power required by a system composed of four traditional 400 Gbit/s coherent modules. Furthermore, it consumed merely 9.5% more power than a system built with four 100 Gbit/s IM-DD DR4 modules, while offering a dramatically extended transmission reach. A summary table contrasts key system parameters including energy per bit, latency, and supported distance among IM-DD, the proposed coherent-lite, and traditional coherent schemes, underscoring the balanced advantages of the new design. Conclusions: This work successfully presents the design, implementation, and experimental validation of a fully integrated 1.6 Tbit/s coherent-lite optical transceiver. Optimized for medium-reach 2–40 km data center interconnections, the design synthesizes multiple innovations: a simplified O-band DFB laser with an effective lock-free frequency control loop, a fast bias stabilization technique based on PN junction differential dithering, high-density 3D flip-chip packaging, and a purpose-streamlined low-power DSP. The prototype demonstrates the ability to deliver 400 Gbit/s per channel over 40 km with a receiver sensitivity of −25.56 dBm, while maintaining a total power consumption of 39.112 W. This architecture provides a practical, high-performance, and economically viable solution for next-generation high-capacity data center links. The path forward includes further DSP simplification and adoption of higher-order modulation formats to push single-channel rates to 800 Gbit/s while continuing to reduce power consumption.

Title: Hands, Mouth, and Mind: Distinct EEG Patterns of Speech, Motor, and Sign-Language Imagery
Abstract: Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology has significant potential as an intuitive communication tool and as a platform for language rehabilitation. This study systematically compared three forms of imagined expression - speech imagery (SI), motor imagery (MI), and sign-language imagery (SLI) - under identical experimental conditions to examine their neural characteristics and decoding feasibility. EEG was recorded using a 16-channel system while a participant imagined four target words, and neurophysiological analyses including time-frequency mapping, sLORETA source localization, and phase-locking value (PLV) connectivity were applied to characterize cortical activation and network dynamics. Classification was performed using common spatial pattern (CSP) features and evaluated across five machine-learning models, with linear discriminant analysis (LDA) used for detailed analysis. SLI consistently achieved the highest performance across models, showing the highest accuracy in 4-class word decoding; moreover, SI, MI, and SLI were perfectly separable in 3-class imagery classification. These findings demonstrate that SLI produces robust and discriminative neural signatures that differ from both SI and MI, indicating its potential as a distinct and effective neural input modality for communication-oriented BCIs.

Title: A Deep Learning-Powered Smartphone Application for Real-Time Vertical Jump Height Measurement by Sound in Sports Science
Abstract: Vertical jump height is a critical metric for assessing lower-limb muscle power and neuromuscular status in athletic populations. While laboratory-grade instruments provide high accuracy, their cost and lack of portability limit their widespread use. Recent alternatives, such as smartphone apps based on manual video analysis, suffer from inaccuracies due to limited temporal resolution, motion blur, and observer bias. This paper presents a novel, fully-automated smartphone application that measures jump height in real time by analyzing the audio signature of the jump. We detail the evolution of our methodology, beginning with a classical signal processing algorithm that differentiates take-off and landing events based on their spectral characteristics. We then describe its enhancement into a robust, noise-immune system powered by a deep convolutional neural network (CNN), trained to accurately detect these events even in acoustically challenging environments. The core contribution of this work is the implementation of this AI-powered engine into a user-friendly Android application. We discuss the real-time system architecture, including audio capture using native Android libraries, continuous buffering, and an efficient two-stage detection pipeline triggered by the landing event. Furthermore, we outline the application's comprehensive user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) design, featuring live feedback, results visualization, and historical data tracking. This application transforms a standard smartphone into a reliable, accessible, and scientifically validated instrument for sports scientists, coaches, and athletes, enabling accurate and effortless performance monitoring in any setting.

Title: AI-Assisted Classical Piano Intervention for Enhancing Resilience, Mindfulness, and Emotional Processing in Young Adults With Mild-to-Moderate Anxiety or Depression
Abstract: Mental-health-oriented interventions increasingly require structured, scalable, and nonpharmacological formats that can strengthen psychological functioning without reducing clinician oversight. This study examined whether a therapist-led, AI-assisted classical piano intervention could produce stronger process-level psychological gains than matched therapist-led piano instruction without adaptive AI feedback among young adults diagnosed with mild-to-moderate anxiety or depression. A randomized controlled mixed-methods design was used with 120 Mandarin-speaking participants aged 18–30 years assigned to either an AI-assisted condition or a non-AI control condition. Over a 10-week program, both groups completed weekly 90-min supervised sessions, and pretest/post-test changes were assessed in resilience, mindfulness, and music-related emotional processing. Quantitative data were analyzed using 2 × 2 mixed repeated-measures ANOVA and follow-up tests, while post-intervention interviews from a stratified experimental subsample were analyzed using interpretative phenomenological analysis. The findings showed significant improvement in both groups; however, the AI-assisted condition demonstrated larger gains across all three primary outcomes, together with a steeper trajectory of weekly musical performance development. Engagement indicators within the AI-assisted group were positively associated with psychological improvement. Qualitative findings reinforced this pattern, with emotional release, increased self-awareness, and stronger motivation to continue practice emerging as the most frequent themes. The study suggests that AI can contribute meaningfully to music-based intervention in supervised contexts, not as an autonomous agent but as an adaptive feedback layer. From a practical viewpoint, the model provides a viable framework for structured mental health-focused practice in various contexts.

Title: Valuation challenges of equity in early-stage ventures
Abstract: Early-stage ventures present a fundamental challenge for valuation due to the lack of stable cash flows, historical performance data, and reliable market benchmarks. As a result, investors rely on a diverse range of valuation approaches that combine financial modelling, heuristic judgment, and information signals. This study provides a method-focused systematic literature review of valuation approaches used for early-stage ventures. Following established systematic review procedures, we analyzed 75 peer-reviewed studies published between 1991 and 2025 across entrepreneurship, finance, and management journals. The review identifies and synthesizes the methodological approaches used to value entrepreneurial ventures. This includes financial valuation models, practitioner-oriented heuristics, signaling-based assessments, and emerging platform-based valuation mechanisms. The findings confirm that early-stage valuation is rarely determined by a single method. Instead, investors apply combinations of financial techniques, credibility signals, and governance mechanisms such as staged-financing and convertible instruments to manage uncertainty. To enhance methodological transparency in the synthesis process, the review has also demonstrated how AI-assisted semantic analysis can support the classification and integration of heterogeneous valuation methods within systematic literature reviews. We also derive insights from semi-structured interviews with venture capital and entrepreneurial ecosystem practitioners used to reflect on how valuation approaches are implemented in practice. The study contributes to the entrepreneurial finance literature by clarifying how early-stage venture valuation is operationalized across research contexts. We also propose a conceptual framework of valuation mechanisms, and directions for future research on emerging valuation practices in entrepreneurial ecosystems.

Title: Motion Capture and Machine Learning-Based Evaluation of Surgical Skills in Laparoscopic Cadaver Training*
Abstract: To promote efficient laparoscopic surgery education, a system utilizing machine learning has been developed to quantify surgical skill levels based on the movement of surgical instruments. In this system, the movements of surgical instruments operated by surgeons during laparoscopic cadaver surgery training are recorded using an optical motion capture system, and kinematic features are extracted from the recorded data. These extracted features are then used as input for machine learning models, with expert-evaluated scores - based on the Global Operative Assessment of Laparoscopic Skills (GOALS) - serving as the training data. The entire nephrectomy procedure was divided into three distinct processes: colon mobilization (Process 1), renal vascular dissection (Process 2), and incision and removal of the remaining tissues (Process 3). In this study, interpretable kinematic features were extracted from instrument movements during the colon mobilization phase (Phase 1). These features were used to train three regression models: Principal Component Analysis followed by Support Vector Regression (PCA-SVR), Partial Least Squares regression (PLS), and Ridge Regression. The models aimed to predict GOALS scores across five key domains: depth perception, bimanual dexterity, efficiency, tissue handling, and autonomy. Model performance was evaluated using 5-fold nested cross-validation repeated 100 times. Among the models, Ridge Regression consistently demonstrated high accuracy, with median mean absolute errors (MAEs) below 0.82 in most domains. This system is expected to contribute to more effective surgical education by providing multidimensional, objective feedback on surgical performance.

Title: Evaluation of Surgical Skills Using Machine Learning and Interpretation of Results with Explainable AI in Practical Laparoscopic Surgery Training
Abstract: To facilitate efficient laparoscopic surgical education, a system was developed that utilizes machine learning to classify surgical skill levels - novice, intermediate, and expert - based on the motion dynamics of surgical instruments. This system not only categorizes surgical proficiency but also incorporates SHAP, an Explainable AI technique, to provide insights into the rationale behind each classification result. For the machine learning dataset, the movements of four surgical instruments were recorded using a motion capture (mocap) system during total nephrectomy training sessions conducted on 46 cadaveric specimens prepared for laparoscopic surgery. The entire nephrectomy procedure was divided into three distinct processes: colon mobilization (Process 1), renal vascular dissection (Process 2), and incision and removal of the remaining tissues (Process 3). Title: Wearable Sensor Technology for Real-Time Biomechanical Analysis in Competitive Sports
Abstract: The wearable sensor technology is able to give real-time data on the patterns of movement, strain on physiological levels, in addition to a measure of injury risk whereas offering a viable alternative to the costly motion capture systems which depend on the analysis of the post-test data. The paper will suggest an AI-enhanced biomechanical system, which includes IMUs, EMG sensors, pressure sensors, GPS, and heart-rate sensor to track the performance of an athlete, identify inefficient movements, and predict injury. The combination of machine learning and cloud processing allows providing immediate feedback and custom training suggestions. The architecture integrates wireless transfer of data, AI-driven identification of patterns and real-time visualization to the athletes and coaches. The experimental findings have shown that there is an increase in movement efficiency and decreased risk of injury, which makes this valid and scalable substitute to mainstream biomechanical instruments less expensive. Future enhancement will involve augmented reality, better predictive analytics, and minimization of sensors.
