Title: Renewable Energy Output Prediction using Machine Learning and Logistic Regression - A Framework
Abstract: This work attempts to explore the improved applicability of a logistic regression framework to predict the renewable energy output of a place based on natural and engineered weather condition data, such as temperature, wind speed, humidity, air pressure, solar radiation, and wind power index. After cleaning and processing the dataset, the machine learning model was trained to classify the energy output of that place into high or low energy categories with 92.88% accuracy. The Confusion Matrix approach was taken to test the other aspects of the model performance, such as Precision, Recall, and F1 Score, and all came out to be 0.93 on a scale of 0 - 1 (weighted mean). A feature engineering approach for creating a Wind Power Index helped improve the results, leading to the observation that the classifier is highly precise in identifying high-energy output locations (a precision score of 0.98) after proper training. Though the dataset lacks temporal features such as the time of the day/week/month/year, the energy will be high; future implementations can certainly include these features.

Title: AI Generative Tools: Redefining Learning for Malaysian University Students
Abstract: In the contemporary digital era, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has exerted a substantial impact on higher education, particularly through generative AI tools that facilitate idea generation, summarization, and assignment enhancement. While these technologies offer notable academic advantages, concerns persist regarding their potential to diminish students' independent thinking, academic integrity, and intrinsic motivation. This study examines the influence of generative AI on university students across five domains: critical thinking, academic performance, fact-checking behavior, academic integrity, and study motivation. Data was collected from 124 students via Google Forms and analyzed using PSPP software, employing Spearman's rank correlation, one-sample t-tests, and chi-square tests. Findings reveal a positive but modest association between AI usage and improvements in academic performance, critical thinking, fact-checking, and motivation. Although more frequent users tend to exhibit permissive attitudes toward AI, its use does not demonstrate a strong relationship with academic misconduct. Overall, generative AI functions primarily as a supportive academic instrument rather than a transformative force within higher education.

Title: Dynamic Multi-Scale Selective Graph Convolutional Network with Multi-Level Feature Refinement
Abstract: Skeleton-based action recognition technology holds significant application value in fields such as intelligent surveillance and human-computer interaction. However, existing methods still face severe challenges when processing visually similar yet semantically distinct ambiguous actions, primarily manifested as insufficient discriminative power of semantic features and inadequate use of multi-scale features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dynamic Multi-Scale Selective Graph Convolutional Network with Multi-Level Feature Refinement (DMS-GCN-HFR). The core innovations of this work are: (1) Selective Hierarchical Feature Refinement Mechanism, which selectively deploys the feature refinement module at the network's deeper layers (L6, L7), leveraging the rich semantic information inherent in deep features, and enhances feature discriminative power within higher-order semantic spaces while introducing feature optimization only at these deeper layers, significantly reducing computational overhead; (2) Dynamic Spatio-temporal Weight Fusion Strategy, which adapts the contribution weights of spatial and temporal branches based on action complexity, replacing traditional fixed-weight fusion; (3) Multi-granularity Contrastive Learning Framework, which combines scale-aware contrastive loss with differentiated prototype update strategies to achieve fine-grained discrimination of ambiguous actions. Experimental results on NTU60 and NTU120 datasets demonstrate a significant performance improvement on challenging similar actions, while maintaining excellent parameter efficiency with only marginal increases in computational complexity.

Title: Lightweight Multi-Step Refinement Network for 3D Registration Based on State Space Model
Abstract: 3D registration plays a crucial role in the manufacturing, precision measurement, and installation of large-scale astronomical instruments and similar equipment. Most existing learning-based PCR methods rely on Transformers, which suffer from quadratic computational complexity, limiting their usage in astronomical instruments with limited computational capabilities. To address this issue, a lightweight multi-step refinement 3D registration network (LMRN) based on state space models is proposed. First, a lightweight state space model is introduced, reducing the quadratic complexity of existing Transformer-based registration networks to linear complexity while achieving a balance between low floating-point operations and registration performance. Then, a multi-step refinement module is incorporated to overcome the registration failure issues faced by existing networks in low-overlap scenarios. Experimental results on the 3DMatch dataset demonstrate that the proposed registration network reduces computational requirements for both training and inference while minimizing performance degradation, achieving an effective balance between the two.

Title: AI-Driven Predictive Analytics for Financial Risk Assessment and Smart Investment Decision-Making in Global Markets
Abstract: Climate risks, sustainability prerequisites and digital transformation have increased the volatility of international financial markets and hastened the adoption of artificial intelligence to conduct predictive analytics in financial risk analysis and investment choices. The literature indicates the application of the various methods: machine learning regression and decision tree models have been applied to capture behavioral finance patterns, deep learning can improve the accuracy of stock market forecasting by 10 to 15 % over classical econometric models, as well as natural language processing of financial disclosures improves the performance of ESG portfolios by about 12 % over traditional benchmarks. Moreover, AI-powered robo-advisors have also boosted the number of investors adopting sustainable investing by almost 20% and blockchain-based infrastructures have lowered the exposure to operational risks by an average of 30. Although these wins are successful, there still exist issues with prioritizing predictive accuracy and regulatory compliance and ethical issues. In this work, these methodologies are integrated and a hybrid predictive analytics approach is proposed, based on financial text mining, behavioral modeling and climate-risk remote sensing data. The framework will enhance greater precision in forecasts by at least 18% than traditional single-model forecasts and will match investment policy with indicators of sustainability. What will emerge is a stronger, flexible, and transparent decision-making instrument in global markets that will enable investors in reducing systemic risks and exploiting opportunities in a more uncertain world.

Title: AI-Enabled Orbital Trajectory Optimization for Low-Earth Satellites: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Hybrid deep learning architectures have become effective instruments for simulating nonlinear orbital dynamics in Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) systems. This paper suggests a hybrid framework that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) to combine Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for accurate orbital trajectory optimization. The model uses Two-Line Element (TLE) data from the NORAD/CelesTrak General Perturbations (GP) catalogue and the Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4) model to make normalised Cartesian position vectors. The CNN layers find spatial correlations in orbital sequences, and the LSTM layers find long-term temporal dependencies. Experimental evaluation shows that the suggested model has an overall prediction accuracy of 96.4%, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.021 km and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.94%. The model also makes calculations more efficient, with an energy-performance ratio 2.5 times higher than baseline methods and an average inference time of 8.6 milliseconds per prediction step. Combining physics-based orbital parameters with data-driven learning makes it possible to make reliable, understandable, and energy-efficient predictions about trajectories. The results show that the framework can be used for real-time satellite navigation, avoiding collisions, and smart mission planning in future autonomous LEO operations.

Title: Design and Performance Optimization of an Infrasonic Recording System for Elephant Call Detection
Abstract: Many animals, such as elephants, whales, crocodiles, big cats like tigers and lions, use infrasonic sound to communicate. This low-frequency channel is mostly invisible to human senses. Studying this range helps us understand animal behavior and tackles the increasing issue of human-wildlife conflict. However, current infrasonic recording systems tend to be costly and are not meant for ecological studies. This limits their use in conservation efforts. This paper introduces a new, low-cost infrasonic recording system that turns a geophone into a microphone. It includes special amplification, filtering circuits, and software modules for signal analysis. The system was tested with indoor trials using HG-24HS and HG-07 sensor setups. The HG-24HS geophone has shown the best results for sensitivity, signal-to-noise ratio, and classification accuracy. Signal processing has been enhanced with Kalman filtering, the Enhanced Empirical Denoising Method (EEDM), and machine learning algorithms. A Support Vector Machine classifier attained superior Accuracy and Precision in separating infrasonic calls from background noise. Field validation at Theppakadu Elephant Camp proved that the system could successfully record elephant infrasonic signals in controlled tests. Analyzing these recordings demonstrated clear communication patterns and reduced false detections. The results indicate that this system offers an affordable, portable, and scalable option for wildlife monitoring. Besides contributing to behavioral research, it has practical uses in early warning systems for reducing human-elephant conflicts and opens new paths for bioacoustics research in low-frequency communication.

Title: Animal sound classification using Machine Learning
Abstract: This paper describes the development of a monitoring solution utilizing acoustics data for the automated recognition and classification of wild animals. We implemented machine learning (ML) algorithms for classification fed with features extracted from audio file streams. Mel-frequency cepstrum coefficients (MFCCs), Low-level, Psychoacoustic, and Auditory filterbank temporal envelope features were applied as four subset features. The data used in this study comes from different sources: the data science community Kaggle, Macauley Library, xeno-canto, and the Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund. Together, these sources provided 2944 audio files on five taxa, including Birds (7.2% of files), cats (5.6% of files), domestic dogs (3.9% of files), Pan Troglodytes (chimpanzee) (66.4 % of files), Gorilla beringei (mountain gorilla) (1.6% of files), and wind (15.3 % of files) as background noise. Methodically, the results of Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Naive Bayes are presented. ML algorithms were compared, considering the use of the macro average (F1 score) as a performance metric instead of accuracy due to the imbalanced nature of the dataset. SVM performed best (93%), followed by Random Forest (92%). The MFCC feature set performed well against all other feature sets combined.

Title: AI-Driven Pre-Identification of Mental Health Issues and Adaptive Learning Tools to Enhance Academic Performance in Students
Abstract: Mental health and emotional well-being are crucial to academic success and workplace productivity. The rising stress levels amongst students due to prolonged exposure to stressors in schools and workplaces calls for early detection and intervention strategies, owing to the demands of modern education and professional settings. Classic evaluation methods, like self-reported surveys, are frequently centered on speculation and omit on-the-spot adaptability. This work introduces a system that employs machine learning models for the evaluation of mental health disorders and their control.For students, it uses the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21) to compute real-time psychological, behavioral and physiological indicators of user stress levels. When detected, automated alerts and intervention strategies (psychiatrist consultations, parental notifications, adaptive learning. In corporate environments, a real-time emotion detection system uses computer vision, speech analysis, and biometric sensors to assess employees' emotional states, allowing for tailored workplace interventions such as personalized workload management and mindfulness initiatives. Moreover, a music recommendation system creates personalized playlists tailored to their needs, curbing workplace stress and improving productivity.

Title: Beyond Traditional Diarization: Enhancing Speaker Attribution Using GenAI
Abstract: Speaker diarization, the process of segmenting and labeling audio recordings by speaker identity, is essential for various applications but remains challenging, particularly in multilingual and noisy environments. This paper investigates the performance of state-of-the-art diarization methods, such as Pyannote, WhisperX, Speechlib, channel split approaches, Azure, and NVIDIA NeMo, on multilingual datasets featuring Thai, Indonesian, and English languages. Comparative Analysis is extensively conducted on these approaches and incorporated novel post-processing solution that integrates Generative AI (GenAI) techniques, specifically large language models (LLMs), to refine the diarization results, addressing common issues such as word errors, missing segments, and unresolved speaker overlaps. This comprehensive comparison of existing techniques and introduction of a new GenAI-based post-processing method demonstrate enhanced performance and accuracy in real-world applications, with broad implications for both academic research and practical applications in multilingual and noisy environments.

Title: Deep learning-based Covariance Matrix Reconstruction for Root-MUSIC Algorithm
Abstract: Root-MUSIC is a classical high-resolution DOA estimation algorithm. However, it is based on strict model assumptions, and its performance degrades when model mismatches occur, such as scenarios involving sparse linear arrays (SLAs), coherent signals, or broadband signals. Its performance further deteriorates with limited snapshots and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To address these challenges, we propose the Residual Covariance Reconstruction Network (RCR-Net), a deep learning framework that reconstructs an ideal, full-rank Hermitian-Toeplitz covariance matrix of a virtual uniform linear array (ULA) for Root-MUSIC. By leveraging the differentiability of the Root-MUSIC algorithm, the proposed framework enables end-to-end training and avoids requiring ground truth labels of the virtual covariance matrix for DOA estimation. The proposed method provides continuous, high-precision estimates and avoids the grid mismatch errors of classification-based approaches. A single network architecture can handle diverse scenarios without modification and successfully estimates more sources than physical sensors. Simulations show that the proposed method outperforms other sparse reconstruction methods and existing deep learning methods in challenging scenarios.

Title: Probabilistic Deep Learning for Musicians' Concentration Recognition from Facial Expressions via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD)
Abstract: This study proposes a musician concentration recognition algorithm based on probabilistic deep learning and stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics. This algorithm models the state of concentration during performance by using dynamic features of facial expressions. At the algorithmic level, unlike traditional classification models, this algorithm geometrically views the evolution of facial expressions as a stochastic dynamical system on a manifold. It then uses SGLD to implement Bayesian approximate parameter sampling and posterior distribution estimation. This study created a four-layer hierarchical optimization framework in terms of model structure. In particular, the distillation layer uses variational inequalities to guarantee semantic transfer stability, the entropy control layer modifies the temperature and variance of the predicted distribution, the KL layer preserves distribution alignment, and the SGLD layer handles posterior sampling and uncertainty modeling. Efficient studies were carried out on the self-constructed Musicians' Concentration Facial Expression Dataset (MC-FED) to confirm its efficacy. Expert-annotated five-level concentration ratings and 18,000 high-resolution facial photos of ten musicians are included in this database. According to the results, the model outperforms ResNet-18 by 6.6% and conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by 11.3% in terms of classification accuracy. In terms of prediction uncertainty and mean squared error, it also performs the best. Ablation experiments further validate the key role of SGLD, entropy regularization, and distillation loss in improving the model stability and reliability. Time series prediction experiments demonstrate that the model can effectively capture the dynamic changes in concentration during performance.

Title: Improving Small Object Detection Through Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanisms in Deep Learning Models
Abstract: The detection of small objects has become one of the most difficult problems in the field of computer vision because of the loss of fine-grained spatial information, confusion with a limited number of pixels, and random background, which is common with deep convolutional-based and transformer-based models. To overcome these inadequacies, this paper introduces a new Multi-Scale Attention-Enhanced Small Object Detection (MSAE-SOD) network that combines multi-scale adaptive multi scale feature fusion with hierarchical attention. It starts with an architecture that has a strong foundation based on feature extractions and can maintain low-level spatial details as well as meaningful semantics pattern. Multi-scale feature fusion module is then used to combine features at various depths with learnable fusion weights and this feature is done in a way that the resulting features should have an optimal balance of both texture insight and contextual knowledge. To make the discriminative power even stronger, channel attention, spatial attention, as well as transformer-based contextual attention are added to point out the corresponding channels, focus on the vital spatial areas, and establish long-range relationships. It is tested using the proposed model on the challenging datasets that have a large percentage of small objects such as MS COCO and VisDrone. The experimental output proves that MSAE-SOD beats the state of the art models like Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, YOLOv8, and DETR by a significant margin and improves mAP and specifically AP[[-S]] which will go as high as 7-8 percentage points. Moreover, the model is appropriate in terms of supporting real-time performance of more than 100 FPS, which is why it can be used in real-life applications as UAV surveillance, autonomous navigation, and remote sensing.

Title: An Intelligent Assessment System for Yao Suona Performance Techniques Based on a Cross-Spectral Temporal Adaptive Attention Model
Abstract: Traditional folk instrument assessments suffer from low efficiency, poor consistency, and lack of visual feedback. To address these issues, we propose an end-to-end intelligent assessment and visual feedback system. It aims to enhance accuracy and teaching utility. The system employs a multi-branch convolutional neural network to extract STFT, constant-Q transform, and pitch contour features. A bidirectional gated recurrent unit and an adaptive attention mechanism enable dynamic modeling of individual techniques. Moreover, the accompanying visualization module presents performance differences in pitch, rhythm, and technique. It uses multiscale heatmaps and pitch deviation charts. The module supports segment analysis and interactive zooming. This aids targeted improvements. The system integrates audio input, feature extraction, temporal modeling, prediction, and visualization output. It forms a complete closed loop. Experiments show the framework outperforms traditional methods in accuracy, speed, and user experience. User surveys also indicate strong practicality and instructional value. However, the study also notes room for improvement in data diversity, streaming feedback, and model extension. Future work will explore additional instrument types. We will adopt advanced architectures and integrate with online teaching platforms.

Title: Adapter-Tuned IndicBERT for Hate and Source Detection in Code-Mixed Indic Texts
Abstract: The spread of hate speech in multilingual online environments especially in low resource, code mixed Indic languages is a serious technical and social issue. In this paper, we introduce a two stage pipeline that encompass hate speech normalization and determine its source of generation. In the first stage, we generate and making a new Indic hate to neutral text rewrite dataset available languages, and fine tune a multilingual encoder decoder model to do context sensitive normalization without changing the semantic intent. During the second stage, we confront the new challenge of AI generated vs human written hate speech detection. Building on adapter-based training on a light Indic language IndicBERT model, obtain a 90.3% accuracy in hate content source attribution, exceeding fully fine tuned MURIL and other baselines. Our finding shows that parameter light-weight, optimized implementations can compete with robust performance in content moderation and AI forensics. This paper provides the first end to end hate normalization analysis with AI vs human source attribution in hybrid Indic code environments, with implications for safer language technologies and accountable AI regulation.

Title: Omni-R1: Do You Really Need Audio to Fine-Tune Your Audio LLM?
Abstract: We propose Omni-R1 which fine-tunes a recent multi-modal LLM, Qwen2.5-Omni, on an audio question answering dataset with the reinforcement learning method GRPO. This leads to new State-of-the-Art performance on the recent MMAU and MMAR benchmarks. On MMAU, Omni-R1 achieves the highest accuracies on the sounds, music, speech, and overall average categories, both on the Test-mini and Test-full splits. To understand the performance improvement, we tested models both with and without audio and found that much of the performance improvement from GRPO could be attributed to better text-based reasoning. We also made a surprising discovery that fine-tuning without audio on a text-only dataset was effective at improving the audio-based performance.

Title: KAN-AST: Kolmogorov-Arnold Network based Audio Spectrogram Transformer for Audio Classification
Abstract: Recently, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) have emerged as a promising alternative to enhance the performance of Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs). Instead of relying on traditional linear weights, KANs utilize spline-parametrized univariate functions, significantly improving interpretability and enabling dynamic learning of activation patterns. This novel approach has garnered considerable interest from the AI community and has seen rapid global adoption. While research on applying KANs to Machine Learning and Computer Vision has expanded, their application in audio processing remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we investigate the untapped potential of KANs in improving models for audio tasks. We propose the first Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based Audio Spectrogram Transformer (KAN-AST) for audio classification. Our study demonstrates how replacing MLPs with KANs enhances the performance of the AST model, highlighting the potential of KANs in advancing audio classification.

Title: Machine Learning Approaches for Acoustic Feature-Based Stress Level Classification
Abstract: Speech signals contain rich acoustic features that can reveal a speaker's emotional and physiological state, including stress levels. In this work, we investigate the effectiveness of three supervised machine learning models-Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-for classifying stress levels from speech-derived features. A secondary dataset containing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC1, MFCC2), Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), energy, and pitch was pre-processed through normalization and partitioned into training and testing sets. The SVM model aims to maximize the separation margin between stressed and non-stressed classes, the Decision Tree model iteratively partitions the feature space based on information gain, and the ANN model simulates neural information processing through weighted layers. Performance evaluation was carried out using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC analysis. The comparative results mention the strengths and trade-offs of each and every model, providing insights for selecting suitable algorithms in speech-based stress detection applications, and it is the optimal way.

Title: Utilizing Kolmogorov-Arnold Network in Self-Supervised Learning for Speaker Diarization
Abstract: Speaker diarization is essential in speech processing but remains difficult due to challenges like background noise, far-field audio, overlapping speech, and unknown numbers of speakers. Self-supervised learning (SSL) has recently shown strong performance in neural speaker segmentation (NSS), typically using pre-trained models with Transformer or Conformer decoders connected via a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) adapter. In this work, we enhance the WavLM-Conformer architecture by replacing the MLP with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), which offers better approximation of multivariate functions. Our KAN-based adapter improves the integration of SSL features into downstream tasks. Experiments show that our model achieves consistent gains over existing approaches, setting new state-of-the-art results on challenging diarization benchmarks such as AMI and AISHELL-4. These results demonstrate the promise of KANs in advancing deep learning architectures for speaker diarization.

Title: Long-Form Fuzzy Speech-to-Text Alignment for 1000+ Languages
Abstract: Conventional speech-to-text forced alignment typically operates at the utterance level. In practice, however, we do not usually have short segments (e.g., 10 seconds) of audio with exact, verbatim transcriptions (e.g., the LibriSpeech corpus) as in lab conditions. Instead, audio often comes in long-form (e.g., an hour-long lecture recording), and the available transcription may be non-verbatim or include unspoken annotations, making it misaligned with the actual speech. This motivates the need for long-form fuzzy speech-to-text alignment, which has practical applications - for example, preparing segmented supervised audio data for training machine learning models. We demonstrate the Torchaudio long-form aligner, which supports such use cases. Moreover, it can be equipped with any CTC model that predicts frame-wise labels, turning the model into a robust and powerful aligner.

Title: SENSE models: An open source solution for multilingual and multimodal semantic-based tasks
Abstract: This paper introduces SENSE (Shared Embedding for Nlingual Speech and tExt), an open-source solution inspired by the SAMUXLSR framework and conceptually similar to Meta AI's SONAR models. These approaches rely on a teacher-student framework to align a self-supervised speech encoder with the language-agnostic continuous representations of a text encoder at the utterance level. We describe how the original SAMU-XLSR method has been updated by selecting a stronger teacher text model and a better initial speech encoder. The source code for training and using SENSE models has been integrated into the SpeechBrain toolkit, and the first SENSE model we trained has been publicly released. We report experimental results on multilingual and multimodal semantic tasks, where our SENSE model achieves highly competitive performance. Finally, this study offers new insights into how semantics are captured in such semantically aligned speech encoders.

Title: Hybrid Solar/Diesel Central Heating Experimental Investigation and Control
Abstract: The traditional design of conventional central heating systems typically involves a circulating pump operating at a fixed speed and does not account for ambient variables, hourly/daily changes. On the other hand, Hybrid Solar/Diesel systems that use a preheating process via solar collectors or vacuum tubes also employ similar fixed-flow circulating pumps. This research investigates improvements to hybrid central heating techniques that preheat the inlet fluid to the boiler system using renewable energy sources, such as solar energy. A complete experimental setup of a Hybrid Solar/Diesel system was designed and installed on the Mechanical Engineering rooftop at the University of Jordan. The system includes state-of-the-art Internet of Things instruments capable of accurately measuring the diversity of the required system's process and environmental variables. The research work findings indicated that the tested Hybrid Solar/Diesel performance and efficiencies were strongly correlated with changes in ambient environmental conditions and the system's flow rate for both the Solar and boiler pump loops. When an online closed-loop PLC controller is incorporated to regulate the circulating pumps' speed, accounting for changes in ambient conditions, component degradation, and aging, the system operates in the best performance region. Furthermore, using an AI-based controller and optimizer enables better optimization and operation of the Hybrid Solar/Diesel system.

Title: MoLEx: Mixture of LoRA Experts in Speech Self-Supervised Models for Audio Deepfake Detection
Abstract: While self-supervised learning (SSL)-based models have boosted audio deepfake detection accuracy, fully finetuning them is computationally expensive. To address this, we propose a parameter-efficient framework that combines Low-Rank Adaptation with a Mixture-of-Experts router, called Mixture of LoRA Experts (MoLEx). It preserves pre-trained knowledge of SSL models while efficiently finetuning only selected experts, reducing training costs while maintaining robust performance. The observed utility of experts during inference shows the router reactivates the same experts for similar attacks but switches to other experts for novel spoofs, confirming MoLEx's domainaware adaptability. MoLEx additionally offers flexibility for domain adaptation by allowing extra experts to be trained without modifying the entire model. We mainly evaluate our approach on the ASVSpoof 5 dataset and achieve the state-of-the-art (SOTA) equal error rate (EER) of 5.56% on the evaluation set without augmentation.

Title: MFCC-Based Multilingual Speech Processing for Depression Classification
Abstract: A relatively underexplored research direction in depression detection involves the utilization of multilingual speech data for model development. Advancing multilingual audio-based depression detection systems is increasingly essential, as such approaches can enhance model robustness, improve cross-linguistic generalizability, and support more equitable mental-health assessment technologies on a global scale. This study conducts a comparative analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) with varying dimensionalities specifically 13, 20, 30, and 40 coefficients in distinguishing depressive and non-depressive speech using two multilingual audio datasets: MODMA and DAIC-WOZ. The extracted MFCC features were used to train three deep learning architectures: LSTM, BiLSTM, and GRU. The experimental results show that MFCC-40 consistently achieves the highest performance across models, obtaining an average accuracy of 82.23%, outperforming the lowercoefficient MFCC configurations. Furthermore, among the models trained with MFCC-40, the Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) demonstrates superior classification capability, achieving an average accuracy of 86%. These findings highlight that the combination of MFCC-40 and the BiLSTM architecture provides the most effective framework for multilingual depression detection based on speech.

Title: PatchTST-based Safety Variables Prediction for Severe Accident Progression in Nuclear Power Plants
Abstract: Severe accidents in nuclear power plants progress in complex and non-linear ways, making it difficult for operators to make quick and accurate situational assessment. To support proactive operator decision-making, this study constructed a deep learning model to predict the future behavior of safety variables in multi-steps during a severe accident. Based on the patch time series Transformer model, which shows high performance in time-series prediction, various severe accident scenario data generated by the modular accident analysis program simulation code were used for training. To improve the model's performance and robustness, a complex noise injection technique simulating instrument uncertainty was applied. Furthermore, the prediction uncertainty was quantified using Monte Carlo dropout. Performance evaluation results showed that the proposed model effectively predicted the dynamic behavior of the safety variables. In particular, the model trained with injected noise showed significantly superior robustness on noisy test data compared to the model trained on clean data, suggesting high applicability in real operational environments. In conclusion, the prediction framework proposed in this study confirmed its potential to be utilized as part of an operator support system that provides reliable future information as a decision support tool for operators during a severe accident.

Title: Combination of Traditional Teaching and AI-Guided Self-Directed Learning on Theoretical Learning and Academic Performance in High-Workload Immunobiology Courses
Abstract: This study examined the impact of integrating an AI-guided self-directed learning tool (MagicSchool) into the theoretical module of a high-workload immunobiology course. Academic performance in 2025 was compared with that in 2023 and 2024, and student motivation was assessed using the MUSIC Model of Academic Motivation Inventory. The AI-assisted group achieved higher theoretical module and exam scores than the previous scholar periods (p < 0.0001) and higher final course grades by 2024 (p = 0.0238). The motivation scores were high for usefulness, success, caring, and empowerment, although interest was low, suggesting the need for various learning strategies. These findings indicate that AI can complement traditional teaching to improve performance and support motivation; however, sustaining curiosity requires diverse and interactive methods.

Title: The pedagogical potential of using neural networks in the field of professional music education

Title: Biomimetic Aerodynamic Enhancements and AI Integration for Rocket Vehicle Performance
Abstract: This research investigates the synthesis of advanced aerodynamic principles, biomimetic designs, and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the efficiency and performance of rocket vehicles. The primary objective is to advance aerodynamic performance by integrating biomimetic features such as shark skin inspired scales on the rocket’s fuselage and double sharklets on the fins. These enhancements aim to reduce aerodynamic drag, improve flight stability, and efficiently utilize turbulence-generated energy to enhance rocket performance. By replicating the texture and structure of shark skin, which includes microstructures that reduce air friction, the application of these scales on the fuselage results in smoother airflow around the rocket, leading to reduced drag and improved fuel efficiency. Additionally, double sharklets on the fins are designed to address vortex-induced drag, thereby enhancing stability and control during ascent. AI is utilized to analyze extensive aerodynamic data, aiding in the development of optimized designs and configurations that enhance the rockets’ overall performance. The AI system processes data, enabling continuous improvements and precise adjustments to design parameters during simulations and testing. The analysis revealed two distinct optimums: a mathematically precise angle of 73.12∘ based on a weighted-sum score, and a more robust, Pareto-optimal angle of 65.32∘ identified by the NSGA-II algorithm, highlighting a critical trade-off in engineering design. From an industrial engineering perspective, this research offers benefits by reducing energy consumption required for launch, thus lowering operational costs and minimizing environmental impact. Furthermore, the application of AI for design optimization shortens the development cycle and enhances the reliability of rocket vehicles, making them more commercially viable and competitive. The incorporation of biomimetic features not only improves aerodynamic efficiency but also introduces innovative methodologies for enhancing rocket performance. By drawing inspiration from natural structures such as shark skin and sharklets, this research pushes the boundaries of traditional engineering and explores new possibilities for rocket enhancements.

Title: Optimization of DNNs Using a Hardware Aware Two Stage NAS for Automotive Embedded Targets
Abstract: Deep learning models are widely used in the context of automated driving. Achieving the goal of performance in Automotive Embedded Targets presents numerous challenges due to the trade-off between accuracy and run-time. This paper addresses the task of finding the best candidate that fulfills System-on-Chip (SoCs) constraints using two-stage neural architecture search. We employed this approach to find a balance between accuracy and run-time. Our method can be applied in the context of optimizing deep learning models. Starting from a search space and a neural network, we can automatically create a super-model (by replacing all layers specified in the search space) that can be trained in the first stage of NAS. In the second stage, we use the already trained model to subsample architectures to find the best trade-off between accuracy KPIs and runtime KPIs. These two metrics are not arbitrary; they define the main constraints of SoCs and were used in the construction of the Pareto front from which the users can choose a configuration that satisfies their expectations. We conducted multiple experiments, but the most important ones are: optimizing a YOLOv8s for Texas Instruments (TI) SoC with 8 TOPS per Neural Network Accelerator and a multitask network for RENESAS SoC that has 3.4 TOPS. We ran YOLOv8s experiments on a public COCO dataset and managed to find a neural network that runs approximately 16% faster on TI, with a drop of less than 1.1% in mAP. For the Multitask Network, we conducted experiments on a custom dataset and found a neural network that runs 13% slower on RENESAS, but with an increase of 0.4% in overall evaluation metrics.

Title: Rootalyx: Stealthy Dynamic Analysis for Linux Malware using Kernel-Level Instrumentation and a Hybrid LSTM-Transformer Model
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a stealthy dynamic analysis environment for Linux, named Rootalyx. The system addresses the challenge of evasive malware that can detect and circumvent traditional monitoring tools. Its core component is a kernel module that uses the ftrace subsystem to instrument system calls, integrated with rootkit-inspired hiding techniques to ensure a covert operational profile. The collected behavioral data, including system call arguments, is processed by a hierarchical hybrid model combining the LSTM and Transformer architectures for automated malware classification. Experimental results show that the proposed system introduces lower performance overhead compared to traditional tools for monitoring like strace and successfully evades detection by common security scanners. The machine learning model achieves a classification accuracy of 80.34% on the extracted data, validating the viability of kernel-level stealth monitoring for robust malware analysis.

Title: Faint Satellite Streak Detection Using the Raw Output of a YOLO-type Object Detector
Abstract: Space surveillance using optical instruments involves detecting faint streaks from long exposure images. As the space object moves, it creates a line segment trajectory in the image space, against the fixed star background. Clouds, light pollution, or the weak illumination of the object by the Sun may lead to a very small signal to noise ratio. The YOLO family of neural networks is a lightweight solution for detecting various objects from images. Starting from existing streak detection solutions, we have iteratively generated training datasets by a combination of manual and automatic annotation and augmentation. The bounding box output of the neural network detector must be further processed to detect the satellite streak's line segment. The unfiltered output of the neural network, containing multiple overlapping boxes, can be used to indicate the position of the line, without any additional processing cost. The complete processing pipeline can detect faint streaks from any type of input image, with real time performance.

Title: Seismometers Fault Identification based on Time-series Ambient Noise Analysis using CatBoost Classification
Abstract: Ensuring seismograph reliability is crucial for generating high-quality earthquake parameters. However, early detection of instrument degradation remains a challenge in large seismic networks. This study introduces an automated fault diagnostic that leverages statistical time series features and machine learning classification to identify seismometer malfunctions using background noise recordings from the 2020-2025 Indonesian Tsunami Early Warning System (Ina-TEWS) network. Seismic recordings were preprocessed, segmented into hourly windows, and converted into representative statistical metrics, including availability, Root Mean Square (RMS), median, mode, number of amplitudes, slope, and unique values. These features are labeled according to the seismometer's health status, including normal status and various types of instrument malfunctions. The resulting dataset is then used to train and evaluate a classification algorithm. We propose Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) as the primary classifier, with its performance benchmarked against Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). The boosting model consistently produces near-perfect confusion matrices with strong generalization validated through learning curve analysis. CatBoost achieves perfect accuracy (1.00) for normal-abnormal classification and 0.999 accuracy for multi-fault detection. These results confirm that simple statistical features can effectively convert seismometer fault characteristic patterns and that the CatBoost machine learning model is a reliable and scalable solution for automated seismometer fault identification. This framework provides a practical path towards predictive maintenance and data quality improvement for real-time earthquake monitoring.

Title: Research on Fault Detection Method of Airborne Electronic Equipment based on Deep Learning
Abstract: Driven by advancements in deep learning, significant breakthroughs have been achieved in the field of electronic product hardware detection, with related technologies successfully applied to identify functional circuits and component failures in electronic modules. However, existing hardware detection algorithms predominantly rely on general datasets where targets occupy a large proportion in images, leading to suboptimal performance when directly applied to small object detection tasks. To address this, the paper proposes an airborne electronic device fault detection method specifically designed for small targets. It employs pruning techniques, weight clustering, and Huffman coding to implement lightweight design for deep neural networks, thereby reducing network scale and parameter quantity while achieving higher computational efficiency under limited resources. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits notable advantages in identifying functional circuits and critical components within electronic hardware images, effectively meeting the demands for rapid fault detection and localization of airborne electronic components.

Title: Data Processing Algorithm for Bridge Structure Health Monitoring Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: In view of the problem that traditional methods in bridge structure health monitoring are difficult to balance multi-scale damage identification and anti-noise performance, this paper proposes an adaptive multi-scale attention fusion convolutional recurrent network (AMSACRN) algorithm. The algorithm innovatively constructs a three-level collaborative architecture: the adaptive multi-scale feature extraction module captures damage features of different sizes through dynamic weight adjustment, the attention fusion module strengthens key features and suppresses noise, the convolutional recurrent module deeply models the spatiotemporal correlation of data. The experiment uses 86,400 sets of measured data and 16,000 sets of simulation data (including 32 damage conditions) of a cable-stayed bridge, divides the data set into 7: 2: 1, and compares 5 representative algorithms. The results show that the damage identification accuracy of AMSACRN is 98.5%, the precision is 98.2%, the recall is 98.7%, and the F1 score is 98.4%, which are 6.2, 6.4, 6.0, and 6.3 percentage points higher than CNN-LSTM respectively, the RMSE of vibration displacement prediction is 0.023mm, and the MAE is 0. 018 mm, which is more than 30% better than the comparison algorithm, the accuracy is still 94.2% under 10 dB noise, and the performance degradation is only 4.3%. The algorithm has a single sample processing time of 42 ms, which meets the real-time monitoring needs. The research provides a high-precision and strong robust intelligent data processing solution for bridge health monitoring.

Title: A Multimodal Biosensing System for Real-Time Driver Monitoring and Adaptive Feedback
Abstract: This paper presents a multimodal biosensing driver monitoring system for real-time detection of driver drowsiness and psychological stress. The system leverages facial expression recognition, simulated EEG signal analysis, and EMG-based stress detection to assess the driver's physical and mental state. Three different machine learning models are used: a CNN for facial emotion classification, a Random Forest classifier for EEG-based drowsiness detection, and an MLP for EMG-based stress recognition. Each model is developed with a robust preprocessing pipeline and trained using either real or simulated physiological data. The outputs are analyzed by a central decision-making engine that autonomously adjusts the vehicle's music playback via the Spotify Web API, enhancing driver alertness and comfort. This architecture exemplifies the use of affective computing to support road safety, offering an intelligent and adaptive vehicle environment. Experimental results demonstrate reliable performance across all modalities, highlighting the system's potential for practical deployment.

Title: Chained Prompting for Better Systematic Review Search Strategies
Abstract: Systematic reviews require the use of rigorously designed search strategies to ensure both comprehensive retrieval and minimization of bias. Conventional manual approaches, although methodologically systematic, are resource-intensive and susceptible to subjectivity, whereas heuristic and automated techniques frequently under-perform in recall unless supplemented by extensive expert input. We introduce a Large Language Model (LLM)-based chained prompt engineering framework for the automated development of search strategies in systematic reviews. The framework replicates the procedural structure of manual search design while leveraging LLMs to decompose review objectives, extract and formalize PICO elements, generate conceptual representations, expand terminologies, and synthesize Boolean queries. In addition to query construction, the framework exhibits superior performance in generating well-structured PICO elements relative to existing methods, thereby strengthening the foundation for high-recall search strategies. Evaluation on a subset of the LEADSInstruct dataset demonstrates that the framework attains a 0.9 average recall. These results significantly exceed the performance of existing approaches. Error analysis further highlights the critical role of precise objective specification and terminological alignment in optimizing retrieval effectiveness. These findings confirm the capacity of LLM-based pipelines to yield transparent, reproducible, and high-performing search strategies, and highlight their potential as scalable instruments for supporting evidence synthesis and evidence-based practice.

Title: The Role of AI in Supporting Differentiated Instruction for Primary Education
Abstract: Differentiated Instruction or DI is differentiated pedagogy, curriculum or learning environment to make the learning experience appropriate for individual learners. This is why differentiated instruction in primary education is a key piece of the puzzle, because if there are students of different skill levels, complexities, and paces of learning, than it is critical to ensure that the teacher is providing every student with the kind of instruction that they need to be successful. However, it may be difficult to educators handle it due to various complications, such as insufficient time, resources, responding to the needs of various learners at the same time, and others. Artificial Intelligence has been well known to be an effective instrument that has been offered to other teachers by automation; enhancing differentiated instruction; creating new possibilities of personalized learning experience; streamlining teaching plans; and enriching learning processes and results. The AI-based educational technologies employs data analysis, adaptive learning technologies, and machine learning algorithm to monitor the performance of students and personalize learning pathways that should facilitate the process of differentiated instruction. An example is supporting student performance and needs, based on the intelligent tutoring system, through the application of Artificial Intelligence, which studies the behavior of students and provides tailored instruction and feedback based on the scaffolded support, depending on whether the student is performing well or not. These systems monitor the achievement of the learners and their weakness and provide the appropriate exercises and learning materials, which can be adjusted to the learning pace. This happens because struggling learners can be given the extra time they need and advanced learners can move on at a faster pace. Moreover, AI assessment software allows teachers to track student performance with greater precision. As traditional assessment provide us with a limited view on student learning, AI-driven analytics provide us with deeper insights and details on patterns of understanding and misunderstanding. These tools support teachers' analysis of students' misconceptions and allow them to modify their teaching strategies. And AI enhances formative assessment through more efficient feedback that saves instructors time that can be repurposed from the ponderous task of grading to developing instructional practice.

Title: Detecting Falsified Audio Through Recurrent-Convolutional Neural Network Analysis
Abstract: The advancement of deep fake technology has elevated audio fabrication detection to a critical research priority. Title: AUDIOSCOUT: Precise Audio Retrieval from Consecutive Interpretation Using Speaker Diarization and Natural Language Processing
Abstract: Consecutive interpretation audio clips pose significant challenges for information retrieval due to speaker overlaps, multilingual transitions, and the complexity of pinpointing specific content. This paper introduces AudioScout, a novel system designed to accurately identify timestamps where a speaker addresses a user's query. By integrating Speaker Diarization, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and multilingual embeddings, AudioScout enables precise query-driven retrieval of both textual responses and aligned audio segments. Unlike existing retrieval systems that struggle with alternating speakers and multilingual transitions, AudioScout bridges English-language queries with multilingual audio, ensuring seamless cross-lingual accessibility. Evaluated on a custom dataset of consecutive interpretation recordings, the system achieves high retrieval accuracy while significantly reducing manual search efforts. This work advances AI-driven multilingual speech retrieval, providing a scalable solution for structured access to interpretation-based spoken content.

Title: Application and Optimization of YOLOv11 for Traffic Object Detection
Abstract: In autonomous driving environment perception systems, accurate detection of road targets such as vehicles and pedestrians is a key technology for ensuring driving safety. However, existing methods still face challenges such as missed detection of small targets and insufficient stability in detecting occluded targets in complex scenarios. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved YOLOv11-based model. First, an Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) mechanism is integrated into the detection head, optimizing multi-scale feature fusion via dynamic weight allocation. This enhances the model's performance in detecting objects across different sizes. Next, to boost the detection of small targets, a four-head detection structure is employed, with the addition of high-resolution detection heads improving the retention of small target features. Moreover, a loss function based on the Normalized Gaussian Wasserstein Distance (NWD) is introduced, where bounding boxes are modeled as Gaussian distributions, and their similarity is calculated through distributional similarity, which helps mitigate positional deviations for small targets. Experimental results on both the KITTI and BDD100K datasets show that the improved model not only achieves significant gains in detection accuracy but also maintains its lightweight design. Overall, the proposed approach outperforms existing methods, validating its effectiveness.

Title: Measuring Reliability and Answering Times for Individual Questions in Digital versus Paper Mode for Inductive Reasoning Assessment Instruments
Abstract: Digital learning and evaluation tools allow researchers to easily capture detailed user behaviour data without compromising the academic experience captured in validated instruments, previously delivered in paper. However, often such instruments migrate to a digital format without testing for reliability of the delivery mode. This study aims to validate the reliability for digital implementation of paper-based inductive reasoning assessment instruments, as well as highlighting the novel benefits of digital delivery, from a behavioural measurement perspective. We replicate an experiment conducted using a subset of exercise items from the Raven Matrices Test, implementing the same format (two different groups, facing a standard or contextual version) both in paper and digital mode, designing and using the easily configurable PoCoPI platform to capture detailed user behaviour data. No significant differences were expected in performance between modes, albeit digital assessment is likely to be shorter. The study was conducted in person, using a convenient sample of university students (N=47), allocated randomly between delivery mode and test version. The mean success rate was 9.3 (out of 10), in average time 7 minutes. Results reveal that university students do not perform better on a contextualized version of the Raven Matrices Test than on the standard version; and confirm that subjects answer faster when the test is delivered digitally. Additionally we track the heterogeneity in response time and hesitation between participants, allowing to explore the discriminant capacity of the test. Further research can extend the validation of PoCoPI in other academic-type assessments.

Title: Argumentative Academic Writing Through Cluster Analysis: Towards a Typology of Profiles
Abstract: The assessment of academic writing is a key process in educational settings. Although there are instruments designed for this purpose, many of them focus solely on reporting individual results, without considering common performance structures. This study proposes an approach aimed at identifying performance profiles in argumentative academic writing, based on the analysis of collective patterns in texts produced by first-year pedagogy students at the university level. To this end, we worked with records obtained from an analytic rubric that evaluates four dimensions: (1) adherence to the discursive genre of the essay, (2) rhetorical organization of the academic essay, (3) cohesion and coherence relations, and (4) conformity to language norms. A total of 153 rubric records were analyzed. Using unsupervised learning techniques, specifically hierarchical clustering, two groups were identified, whose separation was statistically significant according to Mann-Whitney tests applied to each dimension (p < 0.001 in all cases). Group 2, representing 51.6% of the sample (n = 79), is characterized by higher performance across the four evaluated dimensions, with average scores of 3.85 (dim1), 3.57 (dim2), 3.00 (dim3), and 3.41 (dim4). In contrast, Group 1 (n =74) showed lower averages: 2.70, 2.60, 2.09, and 2.85, respectively. We conclude that students need to develop argumentative writing strategies, as the initial profile displays basic competencies related to textual quality and the development of viewpoints and arguments. To address this, it is necessary to implement didactic sequences that support self-monitoring and the development of critical thinking. In this way, opportunities should be created to foster the construction of written arguments. Additionally, to facilitate the exploration of group formation based on rubric-derived data, we developed a web-based tool that allows for the interactive exploration of new datasets generated by other researchers. Finally, we present ethical guidelines for the use of the tool.

Title: Ges-QA: A Multidimensional Quality Assessment Dataset for Audio-to-3D Gesture Generation
Abstract: The Audio-to-3D-Gesture (A2G) task exhibits significant potential across domains including virtual reality, computer graphics, and 3D animation production. However, current evaluation metrics, such as Fréchet Gesture Distance or Beat Constancy, fail at reflecting the human preference of the generated 3D gestures. To cope with this problem, exploring human preference and an objective quality assessment metric for AI-generated 3D human gestures is becoming increasingly significant. In this paper, we introduce the Ges-QA dataset, which includes 1,400 samples with multidimensional scores for gesture quality and audio-gesture consistency. Moreover, we collect binary classification labels to determine whether the generated gestures match the emotions of the audio. Equipped with our Ges-QA dataset, we propose a multi-modal transformer-based neural network with 3 branches for video, audio and 3D skeleton modalities, which can score A2G contents in multiple dimensions. Comparative experimental results and ablation studies demonstrate that Ges-QAer yields state-of-the-art performance on our dataset.

Title: The Zone Promotion using Binaural Beats
Abstract: Music is widely used in daily life and is essential for commuting, relaxation, and concentration. Especially in sports and learning, music has the effect of increasing concentration and motivation, contributing to improved performance. On the other hand, binaural beats using "swells,"which are certain pattern sounds, are also said to have healing effects and enhance cognitive abilities. Therefore, we examined the effects of listening to music on concentration from biometric measurements. In particular, we created a pseudo "the zone"(a hyper-concentration state: a state of high concentration and a sense of immersion) using binaural beats and verified its effects. Two female and four male subjects in their early 20s were evaluated by acquiring biological data (electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrocardiogram (ECG)) while performing an exercise task (cards tower: making a tower of playing cards) and a thinking task (Kraepelin test) that required concentration while listening to various types of music, and then evaluating the subjects in their lowest concentrated state. The binaural beats were applied to the state in which the subjects were least able to concentrate, and their state was examined to see if it changed. EEG analysis showed an increase in the ratio of the characteristic frequency band, Sensory Motor Rhythm (SMR): (αβ12-15 Hz), and a decrease in the stress level (β intensity/α intensity) in four of the six subjects to whom binaural beats were applied. In addition, the Poincaré plot of R-R interval (RRI) showed a reduction in area (increased density). From these experimental results, we confirmed the possibility that the binaural beats applied and evaluated in the lowest concentrated state promote an exquisite balance state and the zone of the autonomic nervous system.

Title: Masking-Augmentation on Mel-Spectrogram and MFCC for White-crowned Sparrow Vocalization Variants Classification
Abstract: This paper presents a study on the application of masking augmentation techniques on the frequency and time axis of Mel-spectrogram and MFCC features for classifying vocalization variants of the White-crowned Sparrow using MobileNetV3. The dataset consists of 860 audio recordings of nine variation groups recorded in California, USA. The study explores the impact of different masking parameters on model performance, evaluated using aggregated F1-score metrics across ten cross-validation folds. The results indicate that applying masking augmentation on Mel-spectrogram features yields the highest F1-score of 98%, outperforming MFCC features and non-augmented data. However, the study also finds several things that can lead to performance degradation attributed to low and high ranges of certain parameters, such as the number of mels or coefficients used to generate the features and the masking coverage on the augmented data.

Title: Efficient Realization of Audio Processing on FPGA
Abstract: Field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and advanced embedded computing boards have become essential to attain high performance in modern computing systems. This offers substantial control capability, improves productivity and efficiency across various applications. The current work incorporates audio processing and denoising using accelerated computing. The coefficients of the infinite impulse response (IIR) filter are fine-tuned to get optimal results. The audio signal comprises 64,000 samples, each with 16-bit resolution, having a sampling rate of 16 kHz. The audio processing using Verilog has been executed on two different platforms: the first is a general-purpose computer, and the second is an FPGA. It has been observed that audio processing on an FPGA-based platform offers higher computational efficiency. This can be good in handling real-time, computation-intensive digital signal processing (DSP) applications, such as image and audio denoising, and machine learning, where both performance and resource utilization are critical.

Title: NSM's SPOTLIGHT: An Unprecedented Journey into the Transient Universe
Abstract: SPOTLIGHT is a time-domain survey instrument to perform a real-time commensal search for Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) and Pulsars with a PetaFlop system installed at the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) funded under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM). The system executes real-time HPC and AI applications to ensure simultaneous time-domain detection and arc-second imaging localisation of the detected bursts across the GMRT observing band. With an unprecedented sensitivity, SPOTLIGHT is expected to find hundreds of FRBs with possible host galaxy associations, allowing the use of the bursts as cosmological probes. The AI-assisted trigger for genuine astronomical signals enables the capturing of voltage samples spanning the burst duration to study the spectro-temporalpolarimetric properties at microsecond time resolution to probe FRB progenitor models as well as propagation imprints. SPOTLIGHT, an AI-powered big data science project on indigenously developed hardware, enables transformational, high-impact science in time-domain astronomy with the GMRT. The initiative aims to build a robust technological and scientific workforce within the country to enable cutting-edge scientific applications.

Title: Adopting ChatGPT in Higher Education: UTAUT2 Findings and Student Sentiment from Brunei
Abstract: Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT are rapidly entering higher education, yet the drivers of student adoption remain under-examined outside Western contexts. This study investigates behavioural intention to adopt ChatGPT and students' perceptions in Brunei Darussalam. Using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) as the conceptual lens, we surveyed students from five institutions ($n=378$ for the UTAUT2 model; $n=168$ for the perceptions instrument). Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) established reliability and convergent validity; structural equation modelling (SEM) then tested seven hypothesised paths to behavioural intention (BI). Five of seven were significant-Performance Expectancy, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, Hedonic Motivation, and Habit-while Effort Expectancy and Price Value were not. A hybrid sentiment analysis of open-ended responses (lexicon seeding with VADER plus multinomial logistic regression) indicated predominantly positive views of ChatGPT as a study aid, alongside concerns about accuracy and reliability. The results provide context-specific evidence on technology acceptance for generative AI in Brunei higher education and suggest practical levers-supportive infrastructure, peer-led norms, and engaging use cases-for responsible student adoption.

Title: Research on Pointer-Type Scale Instrument Recognition Using Three-Stage Algorithm Framework
Abstract: This paper addresses the automatic reading requirements for pointer-type scale instruments in aerospace launch site environments by proposing an end-to-end recognition methodology based on deep learning. The approach employs a three-stage processing pipeline comprising "detection-correction-recognition", with core components including an optimized YOLOv5-based instrument detection module (YDM), an enhanced spatial transformation network for instrument correction (STM) with implicit offset modeling, and a value acquisition module (VAM) integrating semantic segmentation with sequence recognition. Through optimization strategies including anchor optimization, attention mechanisms, multi-scale training, implicit spatial offset modeling, and multi-task learning with balanced loss weighting, the method effectively handles challenges including complex backgrounds, perspective variations, and illumination changes. Experimental validation demonstrates superior performance in instrument localization, image rectification, and final reading interpretation, satisfying stringent accuracy and robustness requirements for practical deployment.

Title: Unveiling Indian Coral Biodiversity and Health Status via Multi-Task Deep Learning on Underwater Imagery
Abstract: The invaluable coral reefs, which are essential for marine ecosystem worldwide and especially in India, face serious threats from global warming, sea water pollution, and increasing sea temperatures. This environmental destruction causes extreme coral bleaching, illness, and ecosystem collapse, damaging sea life and effecting communities in the coastal regions which are dependent on these ecosystems for sustenance. Traditional methods for monitoring coral health, like manual surveys, are slow, costly, and obstructing rapid, comprehensive understanding. To solve this problem, our project presents an automated, efficient approach for coral reef health evaluation using deep learning on underwater images. We started with data collection and expansion, generating a dataset of over 100,000 coral images for model training using image augmentation. During the second phase, ten diverse deep learning models, including custom CNNs and pre-trained architectures like InceptionV3, were created. The third phase focused on fine-tuning these models, resulting in considerable increases in performance. Specifically, models like SimpleCNN and InceptionV3 achieved a remarkable 96% classification accuracy on a 20,000-image test set, successfully solving problems like class imbalance and overfitting. This project provides a strong groundwork for a reliable coral health monitoring system, offering marine experts a fast, accurate instrument for monitoring reef conditions and detecting initial signs of stress indicators, ultimately safeguarding India's invaluable coral reef biodiversity.

Title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Forecasting NIFTY50 and NIFTY500 Indices using Technical Indicators
Abstract: The stock market forecasting is a challenging issue because of volatility, nonlinear, and dynamic nature. This paper explores the predictive capabilities of three deep learning algorithms: LSTM, GRU, and CNN-LSTM in predicting the weekly closing prices of the primary Indian stock indices such as NIFTY50 and NIFTY500. We developed a custom Weekly dataset having historical features such as Open, High, Low, Close and Volume (OHLCV) data and technical indicators. Technical indicators are derived using OHLCV data like Relative Strength Index (RSI), point difference, percentage difference are used. Evaluation of the models is performed on the basis of such metrics as the Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R<sup>2</sup> score. Findings indicate a superior performance of CNN-LSTM in predicting NIFTY50 and LSTM in predicting NIFTY500, which proves the usefulness of hybrid deep learning models in time series forecasting in the financial sector.

Title: Intelligent Smart Metering Framework for Anomaly Detection in Battery Storage Systems and Energy Efficiency Enhancement
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and distributed battery storage into modern power grids necessitates intelligent monitoring mechanisms to ensure reliability and efficiency. Traditional metering systems lack the capability to identify anomalies in storage elements, leading to reduced battery lifespan, unexpected failures, and inefficiencies in grid performance. This study presents an Intelligent Smart Metering Framework designed for anomaly detection in battery storage systems while simultaneously promoting energy efficiency. The proposed framework employs advanced data analytics and machine learning techniques to monitor real-time parameters enabling early detection of irregular charging/discharging patterns, overvoltage, or capacity degradation. The methodology integrates predictive modeling and anomaly detection algorithms with smart meter data, ensuring accurate fault identification and proactive maintenance. The primary objective of this framework is to enhance operational reliability, extend battery life, and optimize the interaction between storage units and the power grid. The outcomes highlight the potential of intelligent smart metering to support sustainable grid operations and energy-efficient consumption in next-generation smart energy ecosystems.

Title: Automatic Document Classification and Intelligent Archiving System for Academic Administration Based on BERT-TextCNN Fusion Model
Abstract: Efficient management and classification of educational administrative documents is crucial for modern higher education institutions, yet manual archiving remains time-consuming and error-prone. This paper proposes a novel BERT-TextCNN fusion model that integrates global semantic understanding with local n-gram feature extraction for intelligent document classification. The model employs a dual-branch architecture where the BERT branch captures contextual semantics through pre-trained transformers, while the TextCNN branch extracts discriminative local patterns through multi-scale convolutional networks. Two key innovations are introduced: (1) a multi-granularity semantic fusion layer utilizing attention mechanisms to adaptively combine features from both branches, and (2) a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism that automatically balances branch contributions based on document characteristics. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset of 80,000 Chinese educational documents across 12 categories demonstrate that our model achieves 94.7% classification accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including BERT-base (88.5%) and BERT + BiLSTM (90.1%) by 6.2% and 4.6% respectively, while maintaining 26% faster inference speed (38.6 ms/doc). Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component, with the attention-based fusion contributing 3.4% and dynamic weighting contributing 1.9% performance gain. The model exhibits exceptional robustness across varying document lengths (93.8%-95.1% accuracy) through adaptive weight adjustment. A 3-month pilot deployment at a major Chinese university processed 12,547 documents with 94.2% accuracy, reducing manual archiving time by 86-89% and achieving 92% user satisfaction. These results demonstrate the practical value of our approach for intelligent educational document management systems.

Title: MS-YOLO: A Multi-Scale Method for UAV-Based Insulator and Defect Detection
Abstract: The automatic detection of transmission line insulators is critical to ensuring the reliability and safety of power grids. However, in complex aerial imaging environments, the multi-scale variations in insulators and defect targets pose significant challenges to the detection task. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved object detection model based on YOLOv11, named MS-YOLO. First, in the Neck of the model, the Inter-scale Feature Focusing and Diffusion Pyramid Network (IFDPN) is designed to optimize multi-scale feature extraction and fusion, while improving the utilization of fine-grained features Subsequently, a Dual-weighted Distance (DWD) loss is designed to improve the model's localization performance across multiple scales. Achieving mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 91.8% and 74.3%, respectively, on the self-constructed dataset, MS-YOLO sustains an inference speed of 195 FPS. This validates the effectiveness of MS-YOLO in detecting insulators and defects.

Title: CrowdShield: A Smartphone-Based AIoT Framework for Real-Time Women's Safety Using Emotion-Aware Voice Recognition and LLM-Powered Alert Classification
Abstract: Women's safety in public and private spaces remains a pressing global concern, often exacerbated by the limitations of conventional safety tools that require manual interaction during distress. This paper introduces CrowdShield, a smartphone-based AIoT framework that enables real-time emergency detection and multi-channel alert dissemination using speech emotion recognition and intent classification. The system integrates lightweight on-device convolutional recurrent neural networks (CRNNs) for emotion detection and quantized large language models (LLMs) for contextual intent understanding. Voice inputs are analyzed locally to preserve user privacy, with alerts propagated through a hybrid communication strategy combining Bluetooth mesh, cellular SMS, and cloud messaging. Privacy is ensured through ephemeral audio buffers, anonymization, and end-to-end encryption. Evaluated on standard emotion datasets (RAVDESS, CREMAD) and multilingual voice samples, CrowdShield achieves 91.3% emotion classification accuracy and sub-3s end-to-end alert latency, with low energy overhead. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse use-case scenarios, including public transport and isolated environments. By combining edge AI, ethical design, and resilient communication, CrowdShield establishes a scalable foundation for enhancing women's safety through proactive and privacy-conscious intervention.

Title: SmoothGuard: Defending Multimodal Large Language Models with Noise Perturbation and Clustering Aggregation
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved impressive performance across diverse tasks by jointly reasoning over textual and visual inputs. Despite their success, these models remain highly vulnerable to adversarial manipulations, raising concerns about their safety and reliability in deployment. In this work, we first generalize an approach for generating adversarial images within the HuggingFace ecosystem and then introduce SmoothGuard, a lightweight and model-agnostic defense framework that enhances the robustness of MLLMs through randomized smoothing and clustering-based prediction aggregation. Our method perturbs continuous modalities (e.g., images and audio) with Gaussian noise, generates multiple candidate outputs, and applies embedding-based clustering to filter out adversarially influenced predictions. The final answer is selected from the majority cluster, ensuring stable responses even under malicious perturbations. Extensive experiments on POPE, LLa VA-Bench (In-the- Wild), and MM-SafetyBench demonstrate that Smooth Guard improves resilience to adversarial attacks while maintaining competitive utility. Ablation studies further identify an optimal noise range (0.1-0.2) that balances robustness and utility. These findings establish Smooth Guard as a practical step toward secure and reliable multimodal reasoning, with future work extending the framework to audio-focused benchmarks to validate its generality across modalities. Code is publicly available here: https://github.com/GuangzhiSu/SmoothGuard.
