Title: Automated Layout Assessment for Metadata Enrichment via Local Rényi Entropy
Abstract: The paper presents a lightweight virtual instrument for the automatic detection of text blocks, column width, and inter-column space in digitized historical documents (manuscripts) using Local Rényi Entropy (LRE). Unlike computationally intensive deep learning models, the proposed technique works without training data, relying instead on local entropy profiles computed over binarized images to efficiently reveal column structures. By analyzing local entropy profiles along both axis of the page, the instrument reliably detects column boundaries in printed book layouts, even in those with marginalia (both text and iluminations on book margins). In addition to evaluating performance on high-resolution scans, we synthetically degraded the images, by applying blur and contrast reduction, to assess robustness under different archival conditions. Computational cost of the proposed virtual instrument is compared with commonly used methods such as Run-Length Smoothing Algorithm (RLSA), Connected Component Analysis (CCA), Projection Profile, Morpohological filtering and Docstrum. Results confirm that LRE detects layout characteristics efficiently, and preserves discriminative structures even in degraded visual contexts. The proposed virtual instrument can be particularly well-suited for large-scale metadata enrichment tasks in digital heritage repositories as it supports efficient structural analysis for layout-aware OCR, segmentation, and content extraction pipelines. This is valuable for cultural heritage institutions operating without high-end computing infrastructure such as GPUs or machine learning expertise.

Title: Enhancing Qur'anic Recitation Skills through an AI-Based Learning Program for Non-Native Arabic Speakers
Abstract: It studies the effectiveness of an AI-based learning program using Tarteel in improving Qur'anic recitation for learners who speak a language other than Arabic. The sample consists of 30 intermediate (B1) female students from Malaysia and Indonesia studying at a Teaching Center for Arabic for Non-Native Speakers at Mansura University, Egypt, for a total of 8 weeks (52 days) of AI immediate feedback, guided practice, and practice with teacher assistance. Assessment of performance was made through the Qur'anic Recitation Skills Observation Card. This has been validated in terms of content and internal consistency (Cronbach's α=0.715). The instrument measures six skill dimensions: pronunciation; differential sounds; application of silent nūn and tanwīn rules; application of silent mīm rules; elongation (madd); and pausing rules. Paired-sample t-tests showed significant improvements in all aspects (p<0.01). Effect size values (η2=0.929-0.993) indicated a strong overall impact of the program. Results clearly indicate that Tarteel, incorporated with a well-planned instructional framework, significantly improves accuracy, fluency, and adherence to Tajwid principles in recitation. It provides a practical model for integrating AI-aided tools into Islamic studies and Arabic language studies.

Title: A Holistic Countermeasure for Imbalanced Audio Deepfake Detection via Uncertainty Mining and Feature Regularization
Abstract: Constructing a large-scale training dataset encompassing representative spoofing attacks is widely recognized as essential for developing effective countermeasures (CMs) in audio deepfake detection (ADD). However, the popularization of audio language models (ALMs) enables low-cost generation of near-infinite spoofed speech data, exacerbating extreme class imbalance (limited bonafide vs. unlimited spoofed), which poses a critical challenge for CM model training. To address this issue, in this work, we propose a holistic CM framework integrating uncertainty-aware hard sample mining and discriminative feature regularization. Leveraging evidential deep learning, the proposal identifies challenging spoofed samples through predictive uncertainty estimation, thereby shifting the training focus from quantity to quality and improving learning efficiency under class imbalance. Furthermore, we impose feature-space constraints to anchor bonafide embeddings into a compact cluster while dispersing diverse spoofed representations. This strategy prevents model overfitting to spoofing representations and preserves intrinsic bonafide structure. The proposed approach synergistically optimizes training efficiency by focusing on high-impact spoofed samples while preserving discriminative feature structures, effectively mitigating performance degradation caused by class imbalance. Extensive experiments on Codecfake and ASVspoof datasets demonstrate significant improvements in robustness against unseen spoofing attacks and effective mitigation of data imbalance effects.

Title: ROBOAI: Real-Time Multilingual Spam Call Detection with Emotion
Abstract: Spam calls are becoming a bigger issue all around the world. Caller ID spoofing, VoIP technologies, and persuasive speech can all cause big money losses and mental health problems. Current methods of detection, such as metadata-based machine learning, static blacklists, voice-to-text NLP, and rule-based audio analysis, have only had moderate success when used with models like Naive Bayes, Decision Trees, Random Forest, SVM, LSTMand BERT. But these methods can't tell what the caller wants before the call is answered, they don't take into account prosody or emotion, they don't work well with multilingual and accented speech, and they rely on a lot of sensitive data that is processed in a single place. Also, a lot of these existing solutions are computationally high, so they might not work well on mobile devices, which need to be able to handle realtime requirements and new scam strategies that come out over time. This paper suggests a way to deal with these problems: A spam call detection system that works in real time, is aware of prosody, and protects privacy. It does this by combining short-audio analysis (unsupervised), emotion recognition, multilingual NLP, and federated learning. We use Whisper for multilingual transcription, OpenSMILE for prosodic and acoustic feature extraction, and Multilingual BERT for intent classification. The final prediction is made by combining the results of Random Forest and BiLSTM models. It runs on Android and uses Tensorflow Lite. It gets 95.6 % accuracy with 96.2% precision, 94.8 % recall, and less than 0.2. 9 seconds of latency on an offline multilingual dataset of five other languages that was used to set the confidence scores. making a ranking table Federated learning lets you update models in a decentralized way without actually sharing raw user data. This study showed that it was possible to accurately detect intent spam in real-world mobile communication while still keeping privacy using the proposed framework.

Title: Baseera: An AI-Based Sound Recognition and Visual Alert System for the Deaf
Abstract: Individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing face significant challenges in perceiving environmental sounds that are critical for safety and situational awareness. This paper presents Baseera, an intelligent sound classification system designed to detect and alert users to five high-priority auditory events: fire alarms, sirens, gunshots, car horns, and dog bark. The system follows a structured audio processing pipeline involving data preprocessing, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) feature extraction, and model evaluation using both classical machine learning algorithms - Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Random Forest (RF) - and a deep learning model based on a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN). Experimental results evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the curve (AUC), showed that while SVM achieved comparable overall test accuracy, it failed to produce valid AUC scores under a one-vs-rest setup, indicating limited reliability for multi-class sound classification. In contrast, the 1D-CNN consistently provided high accuracy (96%), balanced per-class performance, and valid AUC values across all classes (ranging from 0.73 to 0.97), demonstrating superior confidence calibration and robustness. Finally, the trained 1D-CNN was successfully deployed into a mobile application that delivers real-time visual and vibration alerts alongside a history log, demonstrating the practicality of the system in real-world scenarios and its potential to enhance safety and independence for individuals with hearing impairments.

Title: AI Perceptions and Writing Anxiety: A Correlational Study in the Context of Academic Writing Support
Abstract: This study investigates the relationship between EFL students' perceptions and attitudes toward AI-powered writing tools and their writing anxiety in the context of academic writing. As AI writing tools become increasingly integrated into higher education, understanding their psychological impact on students - particularly regarding writing anxiety - has become essential. The study aims to determine whether students' positive perceptions of these tools correlate with reduced anxiety during academic writing tasks. A quantitative correlational research design was employed. Forty-two undergraduate students in Yogyakarta, Indonesia participated in the study. Participants were selected using purposive sampling, ensuring prior experience with AI writing tools and enrollment in an academic writing course. Data were collected using two validated instruments: a self-developed AI Perception and Attitudes Scale based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and the Second Language Writing Anxiety Inventory (SLWAI). Descriptive statistics, normality testing, and both Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were conducted using SPSS. Findings revealed that while students generally held positive views toward AI writing tools, there was no statistically significant correlation between AI perceptions/attitudes and writing anxiety levels (Pearson r=-0.211, p=0.180; Spearman's ρ=-0.195, p=0.216). The results suggest that although AI tools are perceived as helpful for writing performance, they do not necessarily reduce the emotional or psychological barriers associated with writing. The study recommends integrating AI tools with pedagogical strategies that explicitly address writing anxiety to support students more holistically in academic writing contexts.

Title: Research on the Construction Technology of Electric Energy Metering Big Model and Intelligent Agent
Abstract: With the rapid development of smart grid technology, the demand for high precision, real-time performance, and adaptive capability in the field of energy metering is becoming increasingly prominent. This study focuses on the construction of large-scale models and intelligent agents in the field of electric energy metering, and proposes an intelligent metering framework that integrates multimodal data and deep learning technology. By integrating power quality parameters such as voltage, current, harmonic content, as well as multi-source heterogeneous data such as environmental variables and equipment status, a hybrid architecture model based on Transformer and Graph Neural Network (GNN) was constructed to achieve dynamic error prediction and anomaly detection of energy metering data. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the model in harmonic distortion rate prediction task reaches 98.2<sup>%</sup>, which is 21.4% higher than traditional methods. At the same time, it can accurately identify low-frequency anomalies (recall rate 92.3%), verifying its robustness in complex working conditions.

Title: Predictive Acoustic Analysis of the Graha Medika Ballroom: A Comparative Study of Ecotect Simulation and the Sabine Method
Abstract: Multipurpose spaces, such as the Graha Medika Ballroom at Brawijaya University, face unique acoustic challenges as they must accommodate conflicting reverberation time (RT60) requirements for both speech and music. A research gap exists in the lack of predictive acoustic analysis for this specific ballroom at the design stage. This study, therefore, aims to analyze and predict the space's acoustic performance, focusing on two key parameters: reverberation time and the risk of acoustic defects. The primary focus is on evaluating the RT60 and potential acoustic defects based on the interior design. The methodology used is a quantitative approach comparing digital simulation via Autodesk Ecotect with manual calculation using the classical Sabine method for verification. The simulation yielded an RT60 of 1.52 seconds, while manual calculation gave 1.74 seconds at 500 Hz. This slight difference confirms the validity of both methods, as both results fall within the ideal range. Geometric analysis also revealed no significant acoustic defects, indicating even sound distribution. In conclusion, this ballroom has good acoustic quality for its various functions, especially vocal activities and light music. For further optimization and to align with modern technological trends, a hybrid model combining traditional simulations with machine learning is recommended for more efficient acoustic prediction and dynamic design improvement. We also recommend adding carpet in the stage area and optimizing acoustics in the entrance and behind the ceiling.

Title: DeepBindPharma: A Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework with Cross-Attention Integration for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction
Abstract: This study presents DeepBindPharma, an innovative deep learning framework for drug-target affinity prediction. DeepBindPharma integrates multi-modal feature representations, including sequence-based, graph-based, and n-gram features of compounds and proteins, to overcome limitations of existing structure-based and non-structure-based methods. The framework employs four specialized channels: SynapseNet with dilated convolutions for SMILES sequence analysis, Hierarchical Graph Convolutional Network for molecular graph feature extraction, Parallel-Conv Fusion Architecture for multi-scale protein sequence modeling, and Generic Deep Net for processing n-gram protein features. A Cross-Attention Module dynamically balances feature weights between compounds and proteins, mitigating prediction bias. Evaluated on Davis and KIBA datasets, DeepBindPharma outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a 3.54% reduction in MSE, 0.9% improvement in CI, and 1.29% higher correlation index. Ablation studies confirm the necessity of each component, particularly the role of Cross-Attention Module in modeling interactions. While demonstrating robustness in five-fold cross-validation, the framework shows slight performance drops on unseen compound-protein pairs, highlighting generalization challenges. This work advances computational drug discovery by unifying diverse biomolecular representations through an interpretable, scalable architecture.

Title: Dynamic Backdoor Attack Based on Multiscale Local Binary Pattern
Abstract: The data security and integrity of deep learning model is very important. Backdoor attack poses a serious challenge to the security of deep learning system because of its concealment and destructiveness. Most of the existing backdoor attacks rely on static triggers and are easy to be detected by pattern analysis methods. This paper proposes a dynamic backdoor attack (lbpdba) based on multi-scale local binary pattern (LBP). In this method, LBP is used to extract the multi-scale texture features of the image, and the features of different scales are weighted by information entropy to generate dynamic triggers that change with the input image, so as to improve the concealment and adaptability of backdoor attacks. Experiments are carried out on cifar-10 and tiny Imagenet datasets. The results show that compared with badnets, blended and blind methods, lbpdba not only performs better in attack success rate, but also has less impact on the normal performance of the model. In addition, lbpdba can effectively circumvent the mainstream defense methods such as strip and spectre, showing strong concealment and robustness, and providing reference for the research of more effective defense methods.
Keywords: backdoor attack | deep learning security | dynamic trigger | Local Binary Pattern | stealthiness

Title: Exploring the Perceptions of Indian Business Students on the Effective Use of Technology to Enhance Entrepreneurial Intention
Abstract: This paper explores the views of Indian business students on the use of technology to improve their entrepreneurial intention. The study used a qualitative approach and collected data using semi-structured interviews with twenty business students from different institutions in India. It was found that Indian business students positively perceive the application of technology in education and consider it a significant instrument for the improvement of their learning experience and performance, an application that provides diverse advantages, among which include the availability of various resources, motivation, and flexibility in learning. However, barriers have equally been advanced toward effective usage of technology in education, such as inadequacy in its provision, poor Internet connectivity, and technical support.Some participants also feared the possible negative impact of too much technology on the traditional methods of teaching. The study, therefore, advocates that the best way to effectively integrate technology in education is by adopting a total or holistic approach that takes into consideration both students' needs and preferences and all infrastructure and support systems requirements for its usage.This study moves one step further toward better understanding Indian business students' perceptions of and actual usage of technology tools in their educational experiences. It provides an out-of-the-box view regarding the context of India. Policymakers, educators, and technology providers can use this study to create and sustain environments wherein learning is enhanced owing to increased technology use.

Title: Tensions and risks in the platformization of public schools in the state of Paraná, Brazil
Abstract: This paper explores the tensions and risks associated with the platformization of public education, focusing on the integration of AI-based digital platforms in basic education in Brazil. Drawing on a critical perspective informed by the literature on educational technology and teacher professionalism, the study examines how the implementation of adaptive learning systems affects the role and working conditions of teachers. The study is based on an analysis of empirical data collected in two public schools in the state of Paraná, Brazil. The Paraná state school system was the first in Brazil to implement the mandatory use of a wide range of digital platforms in basic education. The findings reveal a precarization of teaching work, manifested in the loss of professional autonomy, an increasing workload, and a drastic shift in pedagogical functions toward technical tasks associated with data management. Furthermore, it is observed that EdTech platforms, managed in this case by the government of Paraná, have become instruments of educational governance, reinforcing a model of teacher accountability based on performance metrics and diminishing the space for pedagogical judgment. The paper argues that this transformation challenges fundamental dimensions of education, raising urgent questions about the future of teaching in the age of algorithmic automation.

Title: AI-Driven Simulation and Digital Twin Technologies for Smart Business Planning
Abstract: This research paper explores the intersections between AI-based simulation and digital twin technologies to make intelligent business plans in intelligent business predictive maintenance, process optimization, and decision-making. The concept of a digital twin is developed on four machine learning models, namely- Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and gradual Boosting Machine (GBM) trained on a data set consisting of real-time and historical data of IoT connected industrial equipment such as CNC milling machines. The data include sensor measurements, SCADA data, maintenance data, manufacturing statistics, and environmental data, which are exposed to preprocessing techniques such as noise reduction, missing value filling, normalizing and feature engineering. The models are analysed based on their performance in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, accuracy, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and R2. ANN is the best of the other models with most predictive reliability and accuracy and has highest operations cost saving (22.7) and energy savings (25.6). GBM comes second as it is dependent on boosting mechanisms to make better predictions. RF has the most favorable trade-off between level of accuracy and efficiency. SVM has the worst performance since it is very sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and non-linearity. The findings determine the capabilities of AI-based digital twins to minimize downtime, decrease maintenance costs, and improve industrial processes. The analysis reveals that ANN can be the most suitable model of predictive analytics and business intelligence that are provided in real-time and, therefore, AI-based digital twins are the valuable instrument of industrial automation in the future. The next round of research might explore the field of hybrid AI methods to improve predictive capability and efficiency in smart manufacturing and optimization of business processes.

Title: Temporal Multimodal Memory Banks for Agentic Reasoning
Abstract: Current multimodal AI agents process inputs in isolation, lacking the ability to maintain and reason over episodic memories across extended time horizons. We introduce ChronoMem<sup>1</sup><sup>1</sup>https://github.com/TransformerTitan/ChronoMem, a novel architecture that enables agents to store, consolidate, and retrieve multimodal experiences for enhanced temporal reasoning. ChronoMem employs hier-archical memory encoding, cross-modal temporal indexing, and experience-guided retrieval to capture temporal dependencies across visual, audio, and textual modalities. Through comprehensive evaluation on three adapted public benchmark tasks spanning navigation (AVLMaps), human interaction (MTPChat), and scientific assistance (RVTALL), we demonstrate that ChronoMem achieves consistent but modest improvements over memory-augmented baselines: 3.3% average improvement in long-term task performance compared to extended context methods and 3.7% better memory retrieval accuracy compared to systems without persistent memory. Our work addresses fundamental limitations in current agentic systems and provides a principled approach for incorporating episodic memory into mul-timodal AI agents.

Title: Multimodal Datasets for Studying Expert Performances of Musical Scores
Abstract: In many musical styles, performing a piece of music means to produce an ‘interpretation’ of a score. This interpretation involves performers manipulating musical parameters such as timing, dynamics, timbre, and pitch to communicate their artistic conception of the piece, often to an audience. Much previous research into musical interpretations has examined aspects of expressive performance strategies. However, these studies have largely focused solely on the sounds produced in the performance, investigating players’ manipulation of musical parameters but little of the performance’s broader context and impact. Multimodal datasets, which contain multiple diverse data types offering distinct perspectives on the musical performance (e.g. audio, Musical Instrument Digital Interface, video, motion capture, physiological data), can support more holistic cross- and interdisciplinary study of performers’ interpretative decision-making and its effects on audiences. We propose a taxonomy of modalities relevant to the study of musicians’ interpretations of musical scores. These modalities are distinct facets of the performance or its context through which the performance and musical interpretation can be analysed (e.g. ‘venue acoustics’, ‘performer movements’, ‘performance sound’). We use this taxonomy to systematically review relevant open-access multimodal datasets and the modalities they support. Underrepresented modalities are then highlighted, along with practical suggestions for including data that support these modalities in future datasets. We next examine key challenges of reporting and working with multimodal datasets, emphasising the need for standardisation of data reporting and reliable options for data storage and access. Finally, we summarise the broader interdisciplinary applications of these datasets in artificial intelligence and performance research.

Title: Performance Analysis of Deep Learning-Based Direction Finding in the High-Frequency Band
Abstract: This study comparatively analyzes the performance of the traditional MUSIC algorithm and the deep learning-based CNN for direction finding, particularly for multiple HF band signals. Simulations in environments characterized by complex noise, and additionally by frequency variations and multipath effects, reveal that MUSIC's RMSE significantly increases under low SNR conditions, whereas CNN consistently exhibits lower errors. Furthermore, while MUSIC's RMSE rises with increasing separation angles of the input signals, CNN maintains stable performance. These findings indicate that CNN overcomes grid-based resolution limitations, achieving optimal estimation performance by closely approaching the CRLB under diverse conditions.

Title: ACKurate-DQN: Adaptive Throughput-Based Congestion Control Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
Abstract: ACKurate-DQN is a Deep Q-Network (DQN) TCP controller that replaces hand-tuned Additive Increase, Multiplicative Decrease (AIMD) logic with a single, scale-invariant reward. A lightweight dual-mode estimator tracks the path's throughput ceiling, and the agent automatically balances throughput and delay to maximize performance, without manual weight tuning. In ns-3 dumbbell-topology tests, ACKurate-DQN sustains more than 95% link utilization and RTT comparable to a recent DQN-AIMD baseline across both static links and a bandwidth-shift scenario with a fixed RTT. This ceiling-aware feedback stabilizes learning and enables more robust operation than existing DQN-based AIMD methods.

Title: FastAFPN: Infrared Surgical Navigation with Adaptive Fusion for Reflective Sphere Localization
Abstract: To resolve environmental noise interference, low localization accuracy, and poor real-time performance in 3D reflective sphere recognition for infrared optical surgical navigation, this paper proposes FastAFPN - a novel detection network integrating a progressive feature pyramid and adaptive fusion mechanism. The method reconstructs YOLOv8n's backbone by replacing its C2f module's Bottleneck with FasterBlock to enhance dynamic feature extraction, and designs an Adaptive Feature Pyramid Network (AFPN) with ASFF-weighted fusion that optimizes cross-scale feature integration while suppressing noise. These innovations significantly improve multi-scale spherical target detection, particularly for small objects. Experimental results demonstrate 96.2% recognition accuracy with real-time efficiency, providing an effective solution for high-precision localization in surgical navigation systems.

Title: AW-BF-MSR: An Image Enhancement Method Based on MSR by Adding BF and AW Module
Abstract: With the rapid development of image processing and deep learning, as raw data for model input, the image dataset's quality can affect the performance of model segmentation, recognition and object detection. For problems such as uneven lighting and low brightness in images, image enhancement techniques are needed to highlight the features of target objects in the image. On the basis of MSR (Multi-Scale Retinex) algorithm, an improved image enhancement method for different fields is proposed in this paper. Firstly, convert the image to be processed to HSI space and extract the I component of the image; Then, when extracting the reflection component using the MSR algorithm, BF (Bilateral Filtering) is introduced; Finally, to address the issue of manually setting weights for multi-scale merging, image information entropy is introduced to adaptively calculate the weight W<inf>k</inf>. The enhanced I component is obtained by multi-scale merging, and the final enhanced image is obtained by merging it with the H and S components. By conducting experiments on images in fields of transportation, industry and power transmission, and comparing them subjectively and objectively with other algorithms, the enhancement effect and universality of the proposed algorithm are verified, which can provide high-quality input data for subsequent image recognition, tracking and understanding.

Title: Harnessing Legacy Air Platforms Data with NLP for AI Training
Abstract: Challenge of using different test environments in previously developed air platforms is a major obstacle for testing avionics. To train an AI, useful set of data is required. However, every platform has different environment, data and test sets, which are specifically created for specific platform and specific requirements. Since every platform creates distinct test sets, every platform uses same type of test cases and procedures, useful set of data will be increased. This paper introduces novel approach to address challenges to collect relevant data in legacy platforms using in-house developed agents and automated verification software. Aselsan Avionics Verification Communication and Identification Instrument (AVCII) will use legacy platforms' data to create test cases automatically. AVCII parses system requirements and models according to requirement standards with NLP and match with ICD attributes in legacy platforms to create test cases automatically. Tester has configuration field in the software for additional considerations such as test environment configuration, time, resolution and asynchronous continuous tests execution for performance requirements. This way, test cases in legacy platforms are standardized and unified. Additionally, database is utilized to store all system design, development and verification data to feed knowledge database. Structural coverage analysis is also performed after test case generation. After structural coverage analysis, it is seen that %85 requirements are completely covered by test cases for modern platforms, which is higher than previous automated test case generation studies [1] due to strict rules in development and requirement verification in aviation platforms which are used in our study. Additional test cases and procedures were created for achieving complete coverage. Only requirement coverage is aimed in test generation, thus no action is taken for defensive code analysis. Process is repeated for remaining legacy platforms. Then, interface control documents, requirements, test cases and test results of old platforms fed into AI-Based Next Generation Test Tool for training.
Keywords: AI Training | Legacy Systems Reusability | NLP

Title: Deconstructing AI Detection Tools: Accuracy Limits, Bias, and Human Consequences
Abstract: This is the first study to systematically evaluate AIcontent detectors using dual-direction adversarial edits across multiple genres while simultaneously addressing the ethical gray zone of human-AI collaboration. Nevertheless, there is a critical research gap, as the current literature fails to cover the Gray Zone of the human-AI collaborative authorship and does not have dual-sided adversarial appraisal methods. This study addresses the question raised in the current literature Should the text be considered AI-generated if the AI is used for minor edits. Our two-way evaluation simultaneously evaluates AI-to-human and human-to-AI adversarial changes, applying targeted and strategic changes in order to make human text look like it was produced by AI and the reverse as well with existing commercial AIDetectors as a representative system. The outcomes demonstrate how challenging it is to spot instances of collaborative authorship because even minor typographical adjustments or paraphrases reveal serious flaws in the detection techniques currently in use. Additional algorithmic constraints can be seen in the systemic variation in performance between content types as further shown by genre-specific analysis. The study shows that authorship problems continue even after grammar and style corrections, suggesting that the binary classification method is not effective to capture the complexity of modern human-AI collaboration. Apart from technical criticisms, we also draw focus on practical consequences like academic sanctions for valid work and concerns brought up by institutional policies. It is confirmed by statistical validation that these are systematic limitations rather than problems with implementation. The findings indicate that binary classification is inadequate and that detection tools ought to be reconceptualized as interpretive instruments requiring spectrumbased classifications and human oversight.
Keywords: academic integrity | adversarial robustness | AI-content detection | algorithmic fairness | detection bias | human-AI collaboration

Title: Multimodal Transformer Framework Optimized with Sinusoidal Graylag Goose Algorithm for Performance Analysis of Visually Impaired Adaptive E-Learners
Abstract: Adaptive e-learning systems are designed to provide the significant supporting model for the visually impaired students due to the consideration of resources based on the unique needs. The existing performance analysis approaches depends on unimodal inputs and the models prone to over-fitting and limited prediction accuracy and generalizability. To overcome the challenges, this study proposed a multimodal deep learning framework that integrated speech signals and structured data for robust learner performance analysis. The input speech signals are processed using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) to capture salient audio features and structured data are normalized to enhance compatibility. Finally, the transformer-based model is employed for classifying learners into high, medium, and low performance groups. To optimize learning efficiency of the transformer model, the Sinusoidal Graylag Goose Optimization (SiGO) algorithm is introduced, wherein chaotic sinusoidal mapping within the conventional Graylag Goose Optimization to optimize the loss function.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Recommendation Engine for Intelligent Cross-Selling and Upselling in E-Commerce Systems
Abstract: These days, no e-commerce platform is complete without cross-selling and up selling tactics, which boost revenue and delight customers alike. The success of these initiatives depends on accurately gauging consumer opinion. With order to aid with up selling and cross-selling, this study devised a sentiment analysis method for evaluating user-generated material. A comprehensive data cleansing procedure was executed, which comprised tokenization, converting text to lowercase, and removing stop words and punctuation. After the data was cleaned up, it was categorized using the LGCU-CS-DBN model, a DBN based deep learning technique. The GCU-CSO technique was used to optimize the DBN architecture in order to further boost the model's performance. With this method, they were able to fine-tune the activation functions and hidden-neuron count. Achieving a precision of 94.80%, the optimized model demonstrated high sentiment categorization capabilities. Standard performance metrics-based comparative evaluations validated its superiority over more conventional algorithms. These findings show that the LGCU-CS-DBN model is a powerful instrument for e-commerce systems to employ intelligent up selling and cross-selling methods. Because of its flexibility and high accuracy, the model may be used in real-world applications, allowing businesses to make better recommendations and engage customers more effectively.

Title: Comparative Analysis of Vgg19 and Efficientnet-B3 for Automated Bird Species Classification Using Deep Learning
Abstract: Bird species identification is a prerequisite to biodiversity tracking, ecological studies, and wildlife conservation. Clearly identifying the species of birds enables researchers to monitor populations, detect changes in habitats, and inform effective conservation measures. However, the classification carried out traditionally by bird experts is usually time-consuming, laborious, and subject to human error, necessitating the use of strong automated mechanisms. In this research, we present a framework based on the use of deep learning techniques to classify bird species based on convolutional neural networks (CNN). VGG19 and EfficientNet-B3 were used, implemented, and analyzed on a dataset comprising 200 bird species with diverse visual features, totaling 2,400 images. Detailed experiments were conducted to determine the output of the competing models based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. VGG19 achieved an accuracy of approximately 79.70 percent, while EfficientNet-B3 delivered superior performance with 98 percent accuracy, demonstrating the benefit of optimized compound scaling and efficient feature extraction. Our results indicate that birds can be automatically recognized very effectively based on the use of deep CNN-based models, representing important instruments used in ecological research as well as biodiversity conservation. This framework is capable of being used to support the conduct of largescale monitoring programs as part of developing smart wildlife management systems. The significant performance gap between the two architectures highlights the importance of model selection in fine-grained classification tasks. Both VGG19 and EfficientNetB3 were fine-tuned using ImageNet pre-trained weights, so as to leverage the transfer learning for better performance on the bird dataset. Such initialization helped the models to retain rich low-level visual features learned from large-scale natural images and accelerated the convergence on our limited dataset. By transferring these generalized representations, the networks required less training samples and resulted in significantly higher accuracy on fine-grained bird species recognition.

Title: Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Meets Machine Learning: Bridging Model-Based Signal Processing and Data-Driven Inference
Abstract: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation is a core problem in array signal processing with applications in wireless sensing, radar, sonar, acoustics, and robotics. Classical subspace and sparse-reconstruction methods enjoy solid theoretical guarantees, yet their performance can deteriorate under model mismatch, limited snapshots, or coherent multipath. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has achieved strong empirical gains by leveraging high-capacity models and large-scale synthetic data. This work reconciles these lines of research: we review the landscape, articulate complementary strengths and limitations, and present a hybrid framework that integrates physics-based priors with learning-based inference. The approach employs covariance-domain representations, deep unfolding, and transformer encoders together with physics-regularized objectives to enhance robustness to array perturbations and domain shift. Simulations across SNR, source coherence, mutual coupling, and calibration error indicate consistent improvements over classical baselines (MUSIC, ESPRIT, SBL) and representative learning-based models, while maintaining interpretability and sample efficiency.
Keywords: array signal processing | deep learning | deep unfolding | DOA estimation | physics-informed learning | sparse Bayesian learning | transformer

Title: Design and Development of an Intelligent Framework for Audio Authenticity Verification in the Digital Era
Abstract: As methods for the generation of non-live audio continue to evolve, the separation of real speech from manipulated voices has emerged as one of the biggest challenges in communication safety and trustworthiness. This work suggests a verification method through deep audio embeddings that is capable of extracting a high-level representation of speech signals. Embeddings are able to extract detailed acoustic and temporal structures efficiently, which are usually not extracted by conventional analysis techniques, allowing for the identification of fine differences in audio between original signals and tampered audio. Then a classification step is used on those embeddings, leveraging the compact representation of audio to feature sets, with no loss of accuracy in real-versus-fake speech discrimination. The experiments show that the suggested framework offers stable and robust system performance across diverse sets of recordings and datasets. Considering the representational power of deep feature extraction and highly effective classification approaches, the framework developed is an appropriate and powerful tool for audio verification and can be used effectively in real-world circumstances, such as security and authentication scenarios.

Title: Multi-Objective JVM Optimization Framework with Enhanced Machine Learning Techniques: An Automated Approach to Performance Tuning
Abstract: Java Virtual Machine (JVM) parameter tuning is a crucial part of a performance and memory utilisation optimization of application execution in the enterprise environments. This paper outlines a detailed multi objective optimisation model in which the use of Optuna in self-guided tuning of JVM parameters is made. Our approach simultaneously maximises execution latency and memory usage through Pareto front program analysis, thus dealing with the complex trade-offs with which JVM configuration is replete. The framework incorporates a powerful graphical user interface to monitor and provide the necessary decision to determine optimisation progress in real- time. The experimental findings indicate considerable performance improvement: the automated variant achieves a reduction of 56.4 percent in execution time and a reduction by 78.8 percent of memory consumption as compared to the comparative default JVMs. The system provides exhaustive analytics, such as the impact of the parameters assessment, performance trend assessment, and configuration recommendations, thus, making the instrument available to both non-expert and expert users.

Title: Te-Autoformer: Integrating Astronomical Features for Enhanced Tidal Energy Forecasting
Abstract: Accurate tidal energy forecasting is essential for grid integration and operational planning, yet existing methods struggle to capture the complex multi-periodic dynamics driven by celestial mechanics. This paper proposes the Temporal-Enhanced Autoformer (TE-Autoformer), a physics-informed deep learning architecture that synergistically integrates astronomical domain knowledge with adaptive temporal modeling for long-term tidal forecasting. Our model introduces three key innovations: (1) an Astronomical Feature Extraction module that computes seven celestial parameters including lunar phase and solar-lunar angular separation to provide explicit physical inductive biases; (2) an Adaptive Multi-Scale Decomposition mechanism that dynamically weights semi-diurnal, diurnal, and weekly periodicities through learnable attention; and (3) enhanced auto-correlation mechanisms tailored for tidal signal characteristics. Extensive experiments on the Marine Institute Tide Prediction Dataset demonstrate that TE-Autoformer achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing Root Mean Square Error by 12 0-15.4% compared to PatchTST and 15.2-20.7% compared to standard Autoformer across 24-72 hour horizons. The model maintains superior accuracy during critical spring-neap transitions, demonstrating robust generalization. These improvements directly translate to enhanced operational reliability for tidal energy systems, enabling more accurate generation forecasting and improved grid integration planning.

Title: EM-Net: A Deep Learning Model Using Enhanced Attention and Multi-Scale Feature Fusion for Text Image Forgery Detection
Abstract: In this paper, we propose an EM-Net for detecting the tiny regions of subtle features, which includes three stages. To restore the size, in the Feature Fusion decoder module (FFU-module), the multi-level information by integrating the global features and location details, so as to improve the performance of locating the forgery areas. Title: The Future of Precision Medicine and Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery: A Comprehensive Analysis of Instruments and Methods
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionised drug discovery and development by improving the speed, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness of the traditional method of finding novel therapeutic candidates. Computational and meta-analytical findings are used in this review to assess AI's effectiveness at different phases of drug discovery. It highlights important AI technologies like natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL), which are being used more and more in precision medicine, virtual screening, pharmacological target identification, and repurposing. A quantitative synthesis of 12 independent studies using random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird method) revealed a pooled accuracy of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.38-0.76) in predicting drug-target interactions (DTIs). Furthermore, the study incorporates mathematical formulations for AI model performance evaluation, including Mean Squared Error (MSE), Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) area, and precision metrics. Despite challenges such as data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and ethical governance, the integration of explainable AI (XAI), multi-omics data fusion, and real-time analytics promises to restructure the future of pharmaceutical innovation.

Title: Transformer-aided Subspace Method for Near Field Localization
Abstract: With the development of technologies such as largescale MIMO and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, spatial information processing in the near-field region has emerged as a significant research topic in wireless communication and intelligent sensing. Existing model-based deep learning methods, such as covariance matrix-based subspace methods, while performing high estimation accuracy and robustness under severe conditions like sources correlation and limited snapshots, their performances are sub-optimal, particularly in feature extraction and longcontext understanding, present significant potential for further optimization. Therefore, a novel near-field DOA estimation method is proposed that integrates Transformer structure with subspace method, named NFTranSNet. This method utilizes a Transformer network to extract spatial correlations and temporal features from the received signals and constructs a surrogate covariance matrix. Combined with the 2D-MUSIC algorithm, it achieves joint estimation of the angle and distance of near-field signal sources. Simulation results demonstrate that NFTranSNet significantly outperforms traditional subspace methods and existing deep learning models in complex scenarios such as multisource, coherent signals, low SNR, limited snapshots, and array perturbations.

Title: The Influence of Denoising Pre-processing on the Performance of Kulkul Sound Classification Using Transformers
Abstract: The kulkul, a traditional Balinese slit drum, is a vital communication tool for relaying community messages. Automating the classification of distinct sounds offers significant potential for cultural preservation and modernizing community information systems; however, ambient noise in real-world recordings poses a substantial challenge to model reliability. This study systematically evaluated the influence of denoising pre-processing on the performance of a transformer-based model for classifying three kulkul sounds: bulus (danger), sangkep (assembly), and kematian (death). Using a dataset of 318 recordings, we compared a baseline (no denoising) with traditional signal processing methods (Spectral Subtraction, Wiener Filter, Spectral Gating) and an advanced deep learning approach, CycleGAN. Our results show that CycleGAN-based denoising yields superior performance, achieving an F1-score of 86.34

Title: UAV Small Object Detection via Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Adaptive Attention Mechanism
Abstract: An advanced object detection approach grounded in the RT-DETR framework is developed to enhance small object identification in UAV imagery, effectively mitigating challenges related to poor feature expressiveness, scale-level semantic inconsistency, and hardware constraints during real-world deployment. At the feature extraction level, a lightweight convolutional feature extraction structure (LCFE) is constructed, which employs an improved Conv3XCC3 module to effectively capture fine-grained low-level features of small objects while significantly reducing computational complexity. At the crossscale modeling level, a Scale Sequence Attention Module (SSAM) is designed, integrating the GSConv and ScalSeq mechanisms to achieve dynamic dependency modeling across scales and enhance semantic perception in complex scenes. At the feature fusion level, a Dynamic Adaptive Feature Fusion Module (DAFM) is proposed, which leverages the Zoom-cat operator and an adaptive gating mechanism to accomplish multi-scale semantic alignment and small-object feature enhancement, effectively mitigating information conflicts and detail loss during the feature fusion process. Performance evaluation reveals that the optimized network attains a 2. 1% increase in mAP and a 1. 8% rise in mAPs compared with the baseline, respectively, on the VisDrone2019 dataset, while reducing the weight file size by 17.28%, which demonstrates the proposed model's capability and effectiveness.

Title: High-Bit Implementation of PDM-to-PCM Conversion Based on Depthwise Separable Convolution
Abstract: Digital micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) can output pulse density modulation (PDM) signals with high sampling rates, but in the field of audio signal analysis, they usually tend to handle pulse code modulation (PCM) signals. Therefore, before analyzing the audio signal, converting the PDM signal to a PCM signal is a necessary step. Currently, onedimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN) can efficiently achieve 8-bit accuracy reconstruction in the conversion from PDM to PCM and have a relatively low inference delay. However, in the face of widely used 16-bit audio signals, the abovementioned method, due to the limited model expression ability, is difficult to accurately restore high-resolution waveforms, which limits its application in high-quality audio processing. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight neural network architecture based on Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC), which enhances the feature expression ability by introducing a learnable channel expansion mechanism. Combining the calculation method of Half-Precision Floating-Point Format (float16), the overflow and rounding errors in the conversion of high-bit wide signals are effectively alleviated to improve the reconstruction quality of 16-bit PCM signals. This method was successfully deployed on the Xilinx Zynq-7020 FPGA platform. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.00218 on the self-built PDM speech dataset. The Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) reached 65.72dB, which was significantly superior to the existing neural network methods. Although its performance is still inferior to that of dedicated industrial-grade audio conversion chips, the construction of a highly reusable technical path on a generalpurpose FPGA platform has verified the feasibility of deep learning models in high-bit PDM-to-PCM conversion, providing a reproducible and transferable implementation example for the research of reconfigurable and adaptive audio systems.

Title: CD-TA-RTM: A Dual-Pathway Deep Learning Architecture for Rainfall Estimation Using Commercial Microwave Links
Abstract: Commercial microwave links (CML) create opportunities for rainfall sensing by leveraging signal attenuation patterns as indicators. However, existing CML-based rainfall estimation methods face several challenges. These include difficulties with complex spatiotemporal precipitation patterns, fixed parameter dependencies, poor regional adaptability, and systematic underestimation of heavy rainfall events. To address these challenges, we propose CD-TA-RTM, a dual-pathway deep learning architecture which exploits Convolutional Downsampling (CD) for spatial pattern extraction, Temporal ion (TA) for multi-scale temporal dynamics, and Raw Temporal Modeling (RTM) for preserving original sequence information. To balance contributions of imbalanced rainfall intensities during training, we also introduce an Adaptive Rainfall-Intensity Weighted (ARIW) loss function that dynamically addresses underestimation bias during heavy precipitation events with small proportion in the dataset. Experiments based on dual-frequency E-band CML data demonstrate that our approach achieves excellent prediction performance across the entire test dataset with PCC of 0.8915 and R2 of 0.7805 while maintaining remarkable robustness to noise.

Title: Multi-Track Audio Fusion for Emotion Recognition Using Machine and Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract: Emotion recognition from audio signals is essential for human-computer interaction, affective computing, and mental health monitoring. However, traditional single-track systems often fail to capture the full range of emotional nuance in complex audio environments. Motivated by this challenge, we propose a multi-track audio fusion-based approach to improve emotion classification accuracy. Using Bangla song recordings, we extract Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, spectral, and temporal features, then apply feature-level fusion to build enriched audio representations. These features are classified using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and compared against classical machine learning models, including SVM, RF, and CatBoost. The CNN model achieved superior performance, with a 99.45% accuracy rate on multi-emotion classification. Our results confirm the robustness of multi-track fusion and deep learning in building more precise and scalable emotion recognition systems.

Title: Emotion Detection in Speech Using Lightweight and Transformer-Based Models: A Comparative and Ablation Study
Abstract: Emotion recognition from speech plays a vital role in the development of empathetic human-computer interaction systems. This paper presents a comparative analysis of lightweight transformer-based models, DistilHuBERT and PaSST, by classifying six core emotions from the CREMA-D dataset. We benchmark their performance against a traditional CNN-LSTM baseline model using MFCC features. DistilHuBERT demonstrates superior accuracy (70.64%) and F1 score (70.36%) while maintaining an exceptionally small model size (0.02 MB), outperforming both PaSST and the baseline. Furthermore, we conducted an ablation study on three variants of the PaSST, Linear, MLP, and Attentive Pooling heads, to understand the effect of classification head architecture on model performance. Our results indicate that PaSST with an MLP head yields the best performance among its variants but still falls short of DistilHuBERT. Among the emotion classes, angry is consistently the most accurately detected, while disgust remains the most challenging. These findings suggest that lightweight transformers like DistilHuBERT offer a compelling solution for real-time speech emotion recognition on edge devices. The code is available at: https://github.com/luckymaduabuchi/Emotion-detection-.

Title: Intelligent Human Scream Detection for Crime Control Using Audio Signal Processing and Machine Learning
Abstract: The human scream detection system is increasingly useful for fostering safety in public transport, urban, homely, and school settings. Conventional surveillance cameras often fail to discern distress signals when visual coverage is obscured, or when a person cannot trigger an alarm manually. In such scenarios, the automatic detection of vocal distress would be a useful boost. This paper presents a method to detect and classify human vocalization into screams or non-screams by signal processing and machine learning. Mel spectrograms are used to preprocess the audio for subsequent extraction of relevant sound features. Three models were developed and tested: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The performance of these models was assessed on a realtime basis using a dataset of 27 scream audios and background noise, giving a realistic impression of their performance. CNN-based detection achieved 88.6% accuracy, while that of SVMs and RFs was 80.1% and 81%, respectively. The method exhibits level flexibility across different acoustic settings and adds to the overall detection reliability. Along with its high accuracy, the system is promising in emergency response frameworks, smart surveillance systems, and public safety setups. It has assisted in the development of smart safety systems that identify distress signals and trigger timely intervention quickly.

Title: A Unified Analytical Framework for Systematically Comparing Classical and aI Approaches in Radar Systems
Abstract: The paper conducts a systematic analysis and comparison of signal processing and object identification methods used in radar systems for intelligent transportation. We propose a unified analytical framework that evaluates classical model-based algorithms, subspace methods, and modern deep learning-based approaches. Our analysis synthesizes these paradigms through consistent performance metrics, computational complexity, and robustness, offering a new perspective for assessing practical trade-offs. We examine a range of problems, including detection, parameter estimation, and vehicle classification. The results are organized to provide engineers and researchers with practical guidance on selecting optimal processing architectures, identifying unresolved issues, and exploring promising research directions in the field of autonomous transportation systems.

Title: Deep Neural Networks Analyzing Age and Fat Component Correlation in Kyrgyz Women
Abstract: This paper examines the relationship between age and fat factors in Kyrgyz females based on the deep neural network (DNN) approach. A feed forward model of neural network is used to examine structured data, such as age, body fat percentage, BMI, and lifestyle factors. Normalization and standardization are some of the data preprocessing that are employed to bring consistency to the features. The model of DNN is trained on Adam optimizer and assessed with the help of Mean Squared Error (MSE) to estimate the percentage of fat by age. Cross-validation of models is used to verify their performance in order to prevent overfitting. The research tries to extract major trends in age role in fat composition and gives insight on the application of deep learning on analysis of data concerning health. The findings reveal that DNN model is useful in capturing the complex relationship between age and components of fat and provides a potent instrument of health research of diverse groups of people.

Title: Scalable VLSI Design for Edge AI Acceleration in Real-Time Audio-Visual Processing Systems
Abstract: The high rate of Edge AI application development requires scalable streamlined energy-effective hardware solutions, which can handle real-time audio-visual processing at the edge with little latency and consumption. Current accelerators such as GPUs and FPGAs frequently do not support multimodal data streams which is utilizing high energy, with an efficient synchronization. In a bid to avoid these constraints, the proposed Scalable VLSI Design Framework to Edge AI Acceleration in Real-Time Audio-Visual Processing Systems is a synthesis of hierarchical dataflow-based VLSI architecture, systolic array-based parallel computing, and dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) as means of optimizing performance. Swift compression-conscious interconnects and dynamic hardware division are also built in to the design in order to create the efficient synchronization of audio and visual channels. The proposed model is analysed with 7 nm CMOS technology that demonstrates the notable enhancements in throughput processing and efficiency of power along with interference latency estimation which is less than 10 ms per frame and accuracy enhancement of 13% which is better than the other existing frameworks. The obtained results are clearly depicting that the proposed framework is well suitable for real time applications such as smart surveillance, UAVs and in HMIs.

Title: Scene Classification of High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images via CNN-Transformer Feature Fusion
Abstract: High-resolution remote sensing (HRRS) images hold considerable application worth in domains like urban planning and natural disaster surveillance. Nevertheless, their notable intra-class variation and strong inter-class resemblance present substantial hurdles for scene classification. Conventional machine learning approaches depend on manually designed features and exhibit poor generalization, whereas standalone CNN or Transformer models find it difficult to effectively integrate multi-scale and global-local information. To tackle these shortcomings, this study puts forward a scene classification approach that combines CNN and Transformer architectures. First, four cascaded Transformer encoder blocks are adopted: linear spatial self-Attention is utilized to lower computational costs, and convolutional feed-forward layers are employed to refine positional encoding, thereby extracting features across four distinct scales. Next, spatial and global attention mechanisms are introduced to suppress redundant content and amplify critical features. Finally, global average pooling is leveraged to learn dynamic weights, enabling linearly weighted integration of multi-scale features and thus reinforcing the guidance offered by scale-related information. Experiments carried out on the UCM dataset indicate that our approach attains an overall accuracy of 98.51%, surpassing other state-of-The-Art algorithms. Ablation experiments verify that the feature enhancement and adaptive fusion modules lead to significant performance improvements. This approach provides an innovative solution for HRRS images classification and i is highly suitable for scenarios such as urban planning and disaster surveillance.

Title: Radionuclide Identification System Based on Embedded Artificial Intelligence
Abstract: Traditional radionuclide identification systems suffer from large volume, poor real-time performance, and low identification efficiency in low count rate, making it difficult to meet the requirements for miniaturization and intelligence of equipment in the fields of nuclear safety, security, and facility decommissioning. This paper proposes and implements a radionuclide identification system based on embedded artificial intelligence, aiming to provide a highly efficient and portable solution. The hardware platform adopts the STM32H750 microcontroller, combined with analog front-end circuits and peak-finding algorithms for precise acquisition, and directly accumulates the collected peak voltages into a energy spectrum feature vector. Then it is fed into the core identification algorithm using a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) model, achieving end-to-end embedded intelligence from data acquisition to radionuclide identification. Experimental results show that the system exhibits excellent accuracy in front-end signal processing, and the constructed nuclear energy spectrum is highly consistent with the results of traditional methods, with clear characteristic peaks. The MLP model deployed on the STM32H750 can accurately identify multiple radionuclides such as Am, Cs, Co and their mixture, verifying the feasibility and practical value of this system in improving identification efficiency and achieving equipment miniaturization.

Title: Transparent and Efficient Fraud Detection in Power-Grid Smart Metering with Explainable AI
Abstract: Smart meters in power grids enable data-driven operations, yet electricity theft and tampering cause major non-technical losses. Many machine learning (ML) models achieve high accuracy but act as black boxes, limiting operator trust. We present an explainable AI (xAI) framework that augments supervised (Random Forest, CatBoost) and unsupervised (VAE, LSTM-AE) baselines with attribution-driven feature selection. Using daily readings from more than 40,000 customers over three years, we show that xAI reduces dimensionality and inference latency without degrading detection quality. The method highlights abnormal consumption, sudden drops, and time-of-use anomalies, surfacing customers and days for field inspections. CatBoost and LSTM-AE emerge as most effective supervised and unsupervised baselines, respectively, with about 400 selected features balancing accuracy and speed. Explainability is introduced without performance loss, supporting faster, auditable, and trusted utility operations.

Title: Efficient-DEIM: An Enhanced DEIM Framework for Small-Target Detection in UAV Aerial Imagery
Abstract: To address the limited detection performance of small objects in aerial imagery, this study proposes an improved DEIM-based deep learning detector. First, the feature extraction network replaces conventional depthwise separable convolution with a partial convolution structure, effectively reducing computational redundancy and enhancing multi-scale feature representation. Second, we introduce a novel multi-scale feature fusion module that integrates a meta-operations mixer and a convolutional gating unit, enabling deep fusion of multi-level features through adaptive weighting to substantially improve the model's ability to capture global contextual information. Experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset show that, relative to a baseline model, the proposed approach achieves a significant improvement in detection performance, with mAP50 rising by 5.8 percentage points and mAP50:95 rising by 3.4 percentage points. Compared with existing mainstream algorithms, the method demonstrates superior performance for aerial small-object detection tasks.

Title: Research on Microphone Array Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Techniques Based on Deep Learning
Abstract: The microphone array direction finding technique is widely used in the problem of DOA estimation, in which the representative MUSIC algorithm can realize highresolution unbiased estimation. Still, the performance is reduced in complex acoustic environments. The deep learning technique is expected to overcome the limitations of traditional algorithms and bring new development opportunities to this field. Concretely, this paper applies the multilayer perceptual machine model and proposes deep learning-based gridded and ungridded MUSIC algorithms from multi-label classification and regression perspectives, respectively. Simulation experiments show that the proposed algorithms have high estimation accuracy and interference resistance, and under the same conditions, the running time of direction measurement with an eight-element line array is shortened to one-sixth of the original running time; under the condition of a low number of snapshots, the mean-square error of the improved algorithm of deep learning decreases by about 80 % compared with that of the original MUSIC algorithm; under the condition of low signal-To-noise ratio, the mean-square error of the proposed algorithm, MLP-WMUSIC, is always significantly lower than that of the MUSIC algorithm.

Title: Robot Target Recognition Algorithm with Dual-Layer Deep Feature Fusion
Abstract: Aiming at the problem of insufficient accuracy and real-Time performance of robot target recognition in complex environments, this paper proposes a dual-layer deep feature fusion algorithm. The bottom layer uses an improved convolutional neural network to extract multi-scale basic features, and the upper layer uses the channel and spatial attention mechanism to mine contextual semantic information, and integrates dual-layer features through weighted fusion and adaptive parameter optimization strategies. Experiments were conducted on COCO, self-built warehousing and industrial inspection datasets, with Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5 and other algorithms as controls. The results show that the mAP of this algorithm on the warehousing dataset reaches 92.3%, which is 7.8% higher than YOLOv5; the mAP in the industrial inspection scene is 90.5%, which is 10.2% higher than Faster RCNN. Faced with complex conditions such as lighting changes and 30%, and the average inference time is only 0.08s, meeting the real-Time requirements. Ablation experiments show that two-layer feature fusion and adaptive parameter optimization increase mAP by 5.6% and 3.2% respectively. The algorithm provides an efficient solution for robot target recognition.

Title: A Real-Time Multi-Modal Fatigue Detection System Using Deep Learning and Facial Behavior Analysis
Abstract: Fatigue and drowsiness are significant contributors to road accidents, with studies suggesting they account for about 10-20 percent of cases worldwide. Similar trends are also observed in India, where around one-fifth of accidents involve drivers who are sleep-deprived or fatigued. These conditions can also reduce productivity during prolonged periods of screen use, showing that their impact extends beyond transportation safety. To address this problem, this research proposes a multimodal detection system that integrates physiological signals with real-time monitoring of facial features, including the eyes, mouth, and head. By combining signal processing and deep learning algorithms, the system is designed to be robust and responsive while providing timely audio-visual alerts. The proposed approach supports deployment on portable and embedded devices, making it suitable for real-life applications. This work proposes a solution to improve road safety and promote digital well-being by addressing challenges in camera reliability, multimodal integration, and real-time performance.

Title: From Encoded Features to Quantifying Disfluency: A Deep Learning Approach for Stuttering Severity Classification
Abstract: Stuttering is a speech disorder marked by interruptions in the natural flow of speech, affecting millions globally. Accurately assessing its severity-categorized as mild, moderate, or severe is essential for guiding effective interventions and enhancing speech therapy outcomes. In this study, we address the task of stuttering severity classification using two publicly available datasets: FluencyBank Timestamped and LibriStutter. We extract diverse feature representations from Whisper, Wav2Vec2.0, and MFCCs to capture both learned and handcrafted speech characteristics. These features are evaluated using three deep neural network classifiers: CNN, ResNet50 and Transformer. Among the combinations tested, Whisper-Small embeddings paired with ResNet50 yielded the highest performance, achieving an overall accuracy of 82.1% and an F1 score of 0.778. While, the other Whisper variants also performs fairly competitive with an accuracy of 77.7% on Base and 76.6% on tiny model using ResNet50. Our proposed setup establishes a strong benchmark and a potential state-of-the-art-for future research in automatic stuttering severity assessment.

Title: Automating Photometric Measurements Using LabVIEW-Python-Based AI: Enhancing Precision in Luminous Intensity, Responsivity, Illuminance, and Flux Analysis at Saudi Standards, Metrology, and Quality Organization-SASO-KSA
Abstract: - This work explores the automation of a photometry laboratory by integrating LabVIEW as the primary control and data acquisition platform, coupled with a Python-based artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm for intelligent analysis and optimization. The system is designed to measure and analyze critical photometric parameters such as luminous intensity, luminous responsivity, illuminance, and luminous flux—all of which are essential for evaluating the performance of light sources like tungsten halogen lamps, LEDs, displays, and optical sensors. By automating traditionally manual processes, the system enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of photometric testing. LabVIEW provides an intuitive graphical interface to control instruments, log data, and visualize results in real time. Meanwhile, the Python AI component improves decision-making by learning from historical data, predicting trends, and detecting anomalies or inconsistencies in measurements. The AI model optimizes calibration routines, reduces human error, and enables adaptive testing scenarios based on environmental conditions or device behavior. Together, LabVIEW and Python form a powerful, flexible platform that brings modern intelligence to photometry labs, making them faster, smarter, and more reliable. This approach demonstrates how combining industrial automation tools with machine learning can revolutionize traditional optical testing environments, paving the way for advanced lighting technologies and robust quality assurance systems.

Title: Leveraging domain-adaptation to improve chlorophyll-a estimates from satellite derived multispectral data.
Abstract: — Monitoring the health of essential freshwater and coastal ecosystems like lakes and estuaries requires estimating water quality indicators (WQIs) like chlorophyll-a from remote sensing data. Machine learning (ML)-based regression tools are a popular choice for this estimation task. Training such models requires a labeled dataset comprising of co-located measurements of remote sensing variables and WQIs. To address this need, practitioners primarily use co-located in situ measurements of remote sensing reflectance and WQIs to train ML models. While these ML models outperform other analytical/empirical methods for the chlorophyll-a estimation tasks on labeled in situ datasets, their performance deteriorates quite significantly when applied to satellite datasets. Using satellite-based training datasets is infeasible given the paucity of co-located measurements of satellite-derived variables and WQIs, especially for newer sensors. To address the discrepancy between the training (in situ) datasets and application (satellite) datasets, we will leverage domain adaptation (DA), i.e., an ML trick to transfer knowledge from a source (in situ) domain with abundant labeled examples to a related target domain with little or no labeled data (satellite). To demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, we implement Domain Adaptation for REgression by aligning inverse GRAM matrices (DARE-GRAM) for the chlorophyll-a estimation task. This regression-specific domain adaptation technique uses the labeled source (in situ) data and unlabeled satellite data (i.e., only the remote sensing reflectance) to build a model with improved chlorophyll-a estimation for satellite datasets. We test this approach using data from two popular multispectral sensors, namely, Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI) and Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Imager (OLCI). The DARE-GRAM shows improvements of between 20-50% across a wide range of regression metrics, indicating a comprehensive improvement in the estimation performance relative to classical ML methods. The DARE-GRAM method also shows significantly improved agreement for chlorophyll-a estimates from near-simultaneous acquisitions from the different sensors. This improved harmony is expected to be an important step in creating consistent cross-sensor products.

Title: Audio Recognition-based Method for RF Transmitters Classification using CNN-LSTM model
Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Radio Frequency transmitter classification that adapts audio recognition techniques to enhance device identification accuracy. By leveraging Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) and spectral characteristics traditionally used in audio processing, combined with a hybrid CNN-LSTM deep learning architecture, our method achieves 93.6% classification accuracy across 8 devices in same-scenario testing. The approach demonstrates strong initial performance comparable to state-of-the-art RF fingerprinting methods, while also providing insights into cross-scenario challenges under varying operational conditions. Our experimental results, conducted using a dataset of commercial RF transmitters, highlight both the potential of audio-inspired features for RF fingerprinting and the persistent challenge of maintaining classification reliability across different operational conditions. This work contributes to the growing field of physicallayer security by demonstrating how cross-domain adaptation of proven audio processing techniques can enhance RF device identification.

Title: Research on the Application of Transformer, GAN and Q-learning in Piano Improvisational Accompaniment Teaching
Abstract: In recent years, the integration of cloud computing and artificial intelligence technologies has brought revolutionary changes to the field of education. This study proposes a cloud-based AI framework, leveraging Transformer, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), and Q-learning technologies, aiming to optimize the efficiency and personalized experience of piano improvisational accompaniment teaching. Through Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), the digital conversion of audio signals into MIDI format is achieved, and digital information processing technology is used for feature extraction. The methods include system architecture design supported by distributed cloud computing, sequence modeling with Transformer, stylized accompaniment generation with GAN, and reinforcement learning optimization with Q-learning. Experiments were conducted using Muqam-style musical score data for testing, verifying the framework's adaptability under different emotional styles. The experimental results indicate that the framework significantly outperforms traditional teaching methods in terms of feedback accuracy (96.1%±1.2%), learning efficiency (improved by 34.7%±3.5%), model stability (variance 0.015), and response time (0.22 seconds). This research provides a new paradigm for the engineering application of AI technology in the field of music education. Future work may further optimize performance in high-concurrency scenarios.

Title: AI-Driven Data Cleansing and Representation Learning for CRM Optimization: A Webly-Supervised Approach
