Title: CNN-Based Vision-to-Speech Recovery: Training with Chirp, Testing with Speech
Abstract: Vision-based remote sound recovery is an emerging technology that reconstructs sound by extracting sub-pixel level intensity variation in video frames of vibrating surfaces induced by acoustic waves. State-of-the-art methods rely on computationally intensive motion extraction algorithms, which limits their practicality. In this paper, we propose a novel approach using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to directly extract vibrations from video frames. The conventional machine learning methods that used for audio signal processing is trained using speech or audio data set. Here, the CNN model is trained using chirp signals instead of speech signal, which provide a controlled and complete representation of frequencies across the spectrum. This training strategy ensures robust vibration extraction and enhances the ability of the system to generalize across diverse sound sources. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in sound recovery quality and computational efficiency, setting a new benchmark for vision-based sound recovery. This work highlights the effectiveness of chirp signals for training and provides a flexible framework for real world applications.

Title: Unsupervised Indoor Relative Positioning and Group Proximity Prediction Based on CIR Graph Convolutional Network and MDS Embedding
Abstract: Accurate modeling of proximity relationships between individuals and groups in urban spaces is critical for public safety alerts, emergency evacuation planning, commercial flow analysis, and urban planning optimization. Existing indoor localization techniques-including TOA/TDOA/AoA geometry-based methods, visual SLAM, inertial navigation (PDR), and RSSI/UWB fingerprinting-Achieve high accuracy in static environments but rely heavily on large-scale manual labeling, strict clock synchronization, or dense anchor deployment, and struggle to accommodate both trajectory continuity and dynamic environmental changes. To address these limitations, we propose a dual-modal deep learning framework based on Graph Convolutional Networks and Multidimensional Scaling embedding. First, channel feature similarities are computed from CIR sequences sampled continuously by mobile terminals, and an attentionenhanced proximity graph is constructed. Then, the graph adjacency matrix is fed into the MDS algorithm to recover the relative low-dimensional layout of observation points, enabling robust reconstruction of crowd density and flow topology. To mitigate class imbalance and manage positive and negative pair ratios both within and across trajectories, we introduce a spatiotemporal pair generation strategy and employ a weighted binary crossentropy loss during training. Simulation results demonstrate that under sparse sampling and dynamic conditions, our method significantly outperforms traditional thresholding and existing unsupervised baselines in both precision and recall, and approaches the performance of supervised methods under moderate label noise. This framework offers an efficient, annotation-free solution for indoor crowd density estimation and flow analysis.

Title: mAP-C: A Coverage-Based Metric for Robust Cross-Instrument Sunspot Detection Using YOLOv8
Abstract: Sunspot detection is critical for mitigating space weather impacts, yet evaluating models across datasets with divergent annotation granularities remains challenging. Traditional IoU-based metrics often misrepresent performance when predicted and ground truth bounding boxes differ in precision (e.g., tight predictions vs. loose annotations). We propose Coverage-based Mean Average Precision (mAP-C), which measures the fraction of a predicted box overlapping any part of a ground truth region, enabling fairer cross-instrument evaluation. Using YOLOv8 trained on two datasets (OGAUC: tight annotations; ROB: loose annotations), we demonstrate that models trained on OGAUC achieve mAP-C@0.6 > 0.81 on ROB—indicating robust detection—while traditional IoU metrics fall to <0.12 due to strict geometric alignment requirements. Training on a fusion of both datasets yields balanced performance (mAP-C@0.6: 0.77 on OGAUC, 0.80 on ROB). These results validate mAP-C as a more reliable metric for multi-instrument sunspot detection, supporting consistent evaluation in operational space weather monitoring.

Title: Perception and Exception Detection of Road Pavement based on an Enhanced DETR model
Abstract: Accurate and efficient detection of road pavement distress is essential for AI-driven maintenance systems in modern infrastructure management. Pavement distress exhibits significant size variability while maintaining similar local characteristics, necessitating detection models that can effectively capture both local and global features. However, existing approaches relying solely on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) or Transformers often result in either global feature loss or inefficient feature extraction processes. To address these limitations, we propose PD-DETR, a novel pavement distress detection model that integrates the advantages of real-time object detection Transformer (RT-DETR) architecture. Our method incorporates an optimized NextViT backbone enhanced with Depthwise Separable Convolutions (DSConv) and a fine-tuned MLP ratio, enabling superior capture of both global and local characteristics of pavement distress while maintaining model efficiency. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative AttentionGate mechanism within the hybrid encoder, which facilitates more effective multi-scale feature fusion through channel weighting after feature concatenation. Extensive experiments on the challenging RDD2022 dataset demonstrate the superior performance of PD-DETR, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 64.27% with a compact parameter size of 30.0M. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models, including YOLOv5s (57.85%) and YOLOv9s (60.12%). This work represents a significant advancement in Transformer-based architectures for pavement distress detection, particularly in complex real-world scenarios, offering both improved accuracy and computational efficiency for practical road maintenance applications.

Title: Machine Learning Models for Student Stress and Academic Performance Prediction: A Systematic Literature Review
Abstract: This study aims to identify and analyze trends, techniques, and findings from recent research on predicting student stress and academic performance using machine learning. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following the PRISMA protocol, focusing on articles published between 2019 and 2025 from Scopus and other academic databases. Twenty relevant studies were reviewed, covering algorithm types, data preprocessing, feature types, and model performance. Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Neural Networks emerged as the most frequently used algorithms. Predictive features included psychological, behavioral, and physiological data collected from standardized instruments (e.g., DASS-42, PHQ-9), wearable biosensors, and facial expression analysis. Common preprocessing steps included text cleaning, tokenization, normalization, and dimensionality reduction. To handle class imbalance, most studies implemented SMOTE or undersampling techniques. Model optimization was typically conducted using grid search or Bayesian optimization, with some models achieving up to 97% accuracy. Geographically, India, China, and Indonesia were the most active contributors. Research was categorized into stress prediction (10 studies), academic performance prediction (5), and combined models (5). This review provides valuable insights into the use of intelligent systems for improving student well-being and academic success and highlights the need for explainable AI and multimodal data integration in future predictive modeling.

Title: Achievable Rates of Full Duplex Cooperative Relay Selection-Based Machine Learning
Abstract: Machine learning (ML) is an advanced artificial intelligence technology that addresses the ever-growing complexity in communication signal processing. In this paper, the concept of ML-based classification model to choose the best relay is investigate in a full duplex (FD) cooperative system. Specifically, a K-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based relay selection is applied to accurately predict and evaluate the achievable rate of the optimal FD relay. The core idea of the multi-class KNN is to identify the optimal relay that yields the highest achievable rate performance by utilizing a large set of offline training data derived from the channel state information (CSI), ensuring that no further training is required during system processing. The results indicate that the KNN-based FD relay selection can achieve an achievable rate comparable to the optimal exhaustive search method with lower computation complexity.

Title: Integration of Conformal Prediction in Automated Forex Trading Systems: Development and Evaluation
Abstract: Automated trading systems are widely used in the forex market to make decisions based on predictions from machine learning models. However, these models often produce point predictions without clear information about their uncertainty. This can lead to risky trades and financial losses. This study investigates the integration of Conformal Prediction (CP) into our forex trading bot to handle this issue. CP may be a statistical strategy that makes expectations interim rather than giving point estimates, which highlights the degree of vulnerability in the figures. This helps reduce ineffective or harmful trading actions by enabling the algorithm to execute trades only when it has high confidence. The inspiration for this study is to enhance the security and reliability of robotized forex trading by employing a strategy that tells the framework designed to measure the level of confidence associated with its predictions. The most significant commitment of this work is the advancement of a forex trading bot that combines CP with price prediction models and trading decision rules. It interfaces specifically to the MetaTrader 5 platform, making real-time trading decisions based on both predicted prices and their associated volatility levels. This study evaluates the framework using empirical data from the XAU/USD (Gold/US Dollar) instrument. Title: TAM reveals AI negativity bias in VR music performances
Abstract: Virtual reality concerts are gaining traction, yet very little is known about its experience. The present study employs the Technological Acceptance Model (TAM) to assess user perception and enjoyment of virtual reality (VR) concerts. More specifically, it aims to investigate the so-called AI negativity bias in the context of VR concert adoption. An experiment was conducted in which one group of participants believed the concerts were generated by artificial intelligence (AI), while another group believed the musical performances were live recordings translated into VR environments. Afterwards, participants evaluated their stance towards VR concerts. Results showed that the TAM measures of Perceived Enjoyment, Perceived Ease of Use, and Perceived Usefulness significantly differed across conditions, with higher scores for the live recording condition. Moreover, general attitude towards VR, as well as immersive tendencies, correlated with technological acceptance. Differences between participant groups could not be explained by familiarity or liking of the artists and songs, strengthening the theory of an AI negativity bias. As such, this study adds to the literature on perceptions of AI usage, extending it into the domain of virtual concert experiences.

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Angle of Arrival Estimation for a Moving Signal Source
Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks for robust single-source Angle-of-Arrival (AoA) estimation. The model is trained on a synthetic RF dataset and evaluated on both real-world acoustic signals from the LOCATA Challenge and a live over-the-air (OTA) RF testbed. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN-BiLSTM model achieves real-time AoA tracking on a CPU-only system with inference latency under 20 ms per frame. It closely tracks the theoretical Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) at low SNR and outperforms traditional deep learning baselines across SNRs. Compared to the classical MUSIC algorithm, the proposed approach achieves superior performance at low SNR and significantly lower cumulative RMSE when averaged across all conditions. Importantly, the CNN-BiLSTM model maintains constant inference complexity, making it suitable for deployment in time-sensitive or large-scale antenna array systems.

Title: Real-Time Tracking of Instrument Motion to Enable Machine Learning Approaches to Laparoscopy Training
Abstract: Laparoscopic approaches to surgery have become widely adopted, due to several advantages over open surgery. However, as an unavoidable consequence of the nature of the laparoscopic setup, skills are more difficult to acquire and sufficient quality feedback on simulator training is costly to procure. We propose a real-time algorithm to track instrument trajectories in 3D within traditional physical laparoscopic simulators. This enables feedback and performance assessment via machine learning techniques. The algorithm has been characterised using a robotically controlled laparoscopic setup as a ground truth and achieves dual instrument tracking up to 60 frames per second at ≈ 5mm accuracy.

Title: CNN-Based Mineral Classification: Epoch Performance Analysis and Web Usability Evaluation
Abstract: This study addresses the challenge analyze system mineral identification, which traditionally relies on manual observation and expert interpretation - methods that are often subjective and time-consuming. While several machine learning models have been applied to image-based mineral classification, limited research has explored how training dynamics, particularly epoch variation, affect model performance. To bridge this gap, we present a web-based mineral classification system using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), enabling users to upload mineral images and receive instant predictions via an accessible interface. The model is evaluated using five different epoch values (10, 25, 50, 75, 100) to analyze its learning behavior over time. The dataset consists of 5,610 labeled images from seven mineral classes, divided into 80% training and 20% validation sets. The model achieves its highest accuracy of 0.74 at epochs 10 and 50, with stable performance across other epochs. Weighted precision and recall reach 0.78 and 0.74, respectively, outperforming macro metrics due to class imbalance. Usability testing with five participants was conducted using Single Ease Question (SEQ), System Usability Scale (SUS), and Net Promoter Score (NPS). SEQ results ranged from 5.4 to 6.0, SUS scored 81.5 (excellent), and NPS recorded 100% promoter responses. These findings demonstrate the system's potential for reliable classification and positive user experience, particularly for educational applications in geoscience.

Title: Accuracy Enhancement of Arabic Handwritten Signature Verification: A Case Study of Mobilenet-V2
Abstract: The verification of Arabic handwritten signatures is an important research area in the fields of computer vision, machine learning, and deep learning. It is essential to distinguish between genuine and forged signatures due to their significance in preventing fraud and forgery, as well as in various legal contexts. Handwritten signatures vary due to several influencing factors, such as mood, writing surface, and writing instrument. In this research paper, three different datasets were utilized: the first dataset (Dataset1) is an English signature dataset known as CEDAR; the second dataset (Dataset2) is an Arabic signature dataset specifically created for this research; and the third dataset (Dataset3) combines the CEDAR dataset with the Arabic signatures. These datasets were utilized to develop a transfer learning model for signature recognition called MobileNet-V2, which is a deep neural network (DNN) model developed by Google, aimed at achieving a balance between accuracy and performance speed. It is primarily designed for image classification tasks in resource-constrained environments. Standard training and k -fold cross-validation (CV) methods were applied to evaluate the model's performance. The model achieved an accuracy of 97.74% on the CEDAR dataset, 98.49% on the Arabic dataset, and 99.49% on the combined dataset.

Title: The Use of AI Chatbots in Enhancing Customer Satisfaction in the E-Commerce Industry
Abstract: AI chatbots are becoming widely used due to the e-commerce industry's explosive growth and the increased demand for quick and effective customer service. These systems aim to improve service efficiency and lower operating costs by providing real-time, automated support through machine learning and natural language processing. This study integrates the DeLone & McLean IS Success Model (D&M) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to examine how AI chatbot features affect customer satisfaction in the e-commerce industry. Three hundred sixty-five purposefully chosen e-commerce users who had previously interacted with AI chatbots were given a quantitative survey. The research instrument evaluated constructs such as Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Trust, Information Quality, System Quality, Service Quality, Customer Satisfaction, and Intention. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4.0 to verify the measurement model and investigate the relationships between variables. The study provides a thorough framework for comprehending the factors influencing chatbot adoption and how they affect customer satisfaction in the e-commerce industry.

Title: A Hybrid Deep-Learning-Statistical Approach for Large-Scale Time-Series Forecasting
Abstract: Accurate and stable forecasting of large-scale time series data is crucial for various applications. This paper presents a hybrid approach that integrates deep learning and statistical modeling to enhance forecasting performance. We employ Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to capture non-linear features and long-term dependencies in the time series data. Subsequently, the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model is utilized to model the residuals from the LSTM predictions, correcting systematic biases. An adaptive weighting strategy is then applied to combine the strengths of both models, dynamically allocating weights based on their respective prediction errors in different data segments. This approach minimizes local prediction biases and enhances overall consistency. To address the challenges posed by large-scale time series data, we incorporate a lightweight LSTM network architecture and a block parallel processing mechanism. Experimental results on power load and industrial equipment energy consumption datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms individual models, achieving a 15.2% reduction in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and an 8.7% reduction in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) compared to LSTM, and a near 10 percentage point increase in prediction accuracy compared to ARIMA, reaching 92.5%. The results validate the effectiveness of our method in improving prediction accuracy, stability, and generalization ability, offering a reliable solution for time series forecasting in energy management, industrial production, and other fields.

Title: A MUSIC-Based Adaptive Beamforming Approach for Mobile Jamming Mitigation in 5G Networks
Abstract: Mobile jammers pose a critical threat to 5G networks, particularly in military communications. This paper investigates an anti-jamming framework that enhances a strong adaptive beamforming baseline comprising Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) for Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation and Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) for interference suppression with a lightweight machine learning (ML) model for predictive error correction. Extensive simulations in a realistic highway scenario demonstrate that the integrated system achieves a high DoA estimation accuracy of up to 99.8% and an average Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) improvement of 9.58 dB. Analysis reveals that the MUSIC-MVDR baseline alone accounts for the vast majority of this performance gain (9.46 dB), indicating that the primary benefit of the simple ML model lies in correcting outlier estimates rather than providing a substantial systemic SNR increase. The framework's computational efficiency validates the effectiveness of the core beamforming approach and highlights the critical trade-off between ML model complexity and practical performance gains for securing 5G communications in contested environments.

Title: SAWP: Scaled Adaptive Wavelet Pooling for Audio Classification Tasks
Abstract: Audio classification is a rapidly advancing field that spans various domains, including speech, music, and environmental sound classification, each demanding a different balance of local details and global structure for the classification. Traditional pooling methods such as max pooling and average pooling are widely used in deep learning models but are inherently fixed and unable to adapt to specific dataset characteristics. Recent developments in adaptive pooling methods have shown promise in learning feature aggregation strategies that better align with dataset-specific properties and adaptive wavelet-based approaches are particularly suited for identifying frequency components that distinguish between local and global features. In this paper, we propose a modified Scaled Adaptive Wavelet Pooling method for audio classification tasks, which employs fast wavelet transforms to decompose the input features into multiple scales, reducing the feature dimensions by removing the fine-scale subbands. Our approach parameterizes wavelet decomposition filters and subband weights as learnable variables, enabling the model to discover optimal frequency-based representations that align with the needs of the task. Our approach is validated on speech, music, and environmental sound classification tasks using the IEMOCAP, GTZAN, and ESC-50 datasets. Experimental results show that Scaled Adaptive Wavelet Pooling consistently achieves superior performance compared to traditional and adaptive pooling baselines, achieving average classification accuracies of 6 8. 1 2% on IEMOCAP, 89.92% on GTZAN and 88.82% on ESC-50 datasets, highlighting its effectiveness in learning task-specific spectral representations.

Title: Development of an Innovative Learning Management System Integrating Local Wisdom to Bridge Community Potential and Digital Education
Abstract: This study develops an innovative Learning Management System (LMS) that integrates local wisdom to enhance digital education in rural communities. User testing with 50 community members confirmed consistent performance across Effectiveness (81.84%), Appeal (81.44%), User Experience (80.00%), and Efficiency (79.36%). These results demonstrate the system's ability to address both technical and socio-cultural learning needs. The study highlights how embedding local wisdom and community participation into digital platforms fosters inclusive and sustainable learning. Future research should explore broader implementation and the addition of offline capabilities and AI-personalized features to enhance accessibility and long-term impact.

Title: CRAFT-Net: Contour-Refining Attention and Fusion Network for Concrete Crack Segmentation
Abstract: Concrete crack segmentation remains challenging due to the thin, irregular nature of cracks, complex background textures, and variable lighting conditions that often lead to fragmented segmentation results with poor edge precision. We propose CRAFT-Net, a novel Contour-Refining Attention and Fusion Network that systematically addresses these limitations through a comprehensive feature enhancement pipeline. Our approach integrates EdgeAwareConv modules for high-resolution contour preservation, C2f-Attention blocks for focused crack feature extraction while suppressing background noise, and Concat-BiFPN layers for intelligent multi-scale feature fusion with learnable weights. Additionally, we introduce a lightweight Mask Refinement Network that combines low-resolution segmentation outputs with shallow high-resolution features to generate precise full-resolution masks. Extensive experiments on concrete crack datasets demonstrate that CRAFT-Net achieves superior performance in both segmentation accuracy and edge fidelity compared to existing methods, while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for practical deployment in structural health monitoring applications.

Title: Comparison of Machine Learning Models for Error Reduction in Photovoltaic Radiometers
Abstract: This work presents a comparison of correction methods based on machine learning models to reduce the measurement error of photovoltaic radiometers. The devices under analysis were placed in three different geographic locations of Argentina and measurements for over two years were taken. Each radiometer was compared against a commercial class B pyranometer placed in the same station. All the measurements were processed along with GPS-aided timestamps and coordinates to get Sun trajectory and clarity indices. After determining the measurement error against the reference instruments, several machine learning models were trained to reduce that error: linear regressors, K-nearest neighbors, multilayer perceptrons and tree-based models. Histogram gradient boosting models showed the best performance, with RMSE and MBE reductions over 45 % and 95 % respectively in minute-averaged irradiance.

Title: Automatic Detection of Burned Areas in SAOCOM (SAR) Images
Abstract: Land and forest fires are extremely interesting due to their consequences for the environment and human activities. Thus, tools for its early detection are necessary to implement private and government actions. Remote sensing offers valuable instruments that can help develop automatic mechanisms to detect burned areas through synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. In the present work, an exploratory analysis of machine learning and deep learning techniques is conducted with the aim of distinguishing between burned and unburned areas. These algorithms were trained with features obtained from SAOCOM images, which include polarization bands and well-known burnt indices. The proposed methodology was applied to an image corresponding to San Pedro Norte, Córdoba, Argentina, where a fire occurred in 2020. To assess the performance of the considered models, accuracy, F1-score, area under the ROC curve, and training time were computed. Gradient Boosting and Support Vector Machines showed good behaviour in balancing efficiency and computational cost.

Title: Automatic Speech Emotion Recognition using Machine Learning Algorithm for Human Computer Interaction
Abstract: Addressing and improving Bioastronautics challenges in space, the digital processing of speech signals and emotion recognition can significantly enhance the performance of human-computer interaction systems. Space missions are long, isolating, and confined. Companion robots can help mitigate feelings of loneliness, stress, and anxiety by providing interaction and emotional support to the astronauts on board. Existing methods involve extracting signal features using various algorithms and classifying with different machine learning models. Each model presents its own merits and demerits, with the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) achieving a maximum accuracy of 64.77 percentage for speaker-independent systems to date. The proposed methodology employs a comprehensive two-stage approach. In the first stage, feature extraction is conducted using three distinct techniques: Linear Prediction Coefficients (LPC), Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), and Perceptual Linear Prediction Coefficients (PLPC). These techniques are chosen for their effectiveness in capturing the nuanced features of speech signals. Following feature extraction, classification is performed using the K-Nearest Neighbour (K-NN) clustering algorithm, which is known for its simplicity and effectiveness in classification tasks. Parallel to this, the methodology explores a novel approach wherein the image form of the audio signal is directly analysed and classified using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). This dual approach not only diversifies the analytical methods but also enhances the robustness of the emotion recognition system. This innovative methodology has been tested on a dataset encompassing seven distinct emotions. The results of these tests demonstrate a significant improvement in accuracy over traditional individual classifiers. Specifically, the feature extraction and KNN clustering model achieved an accuracy of 74.64 percentage. However, the image processing-CNN model significantly outperformed this, achieving an impressive accuracy of 92.19 percentage in speaker-independent emotion recognition tasks. Furthermore, the integration of three feature extraction techniques—MFCC, LPC, and PLPC—combined with K-NN clustering, proves to be more accurate and effective than systems based on individual feature extraction methods. This integrated approach harnesses the strengths of each feature extraction technique, resulting in a more comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the speech signals. In conclusion, the proposed two-stage methodology, involving both advanced feature extraction techniques and innovative image-based classification, represents a significant advancement in the field of speech emotion recognition.

Title: Abnormal Sound Detection Method for Microfans Based on Lightweight Attention Capsule Network
Abstract: Abnormal sound detection of microfans is key to ensuring product quality. Traditional manual auditory detection methods are subjective, while deep learning-based approaches can improve detection accuracy but often require large datasets, which are difficult to obtain in industrial applications. To address this, an abnormal sound detection method is proposed based on a lightweight attention capsule network (LACNet). First, A-weighting filtering is applied to the audio signals, and they are converted into time-frequency maps using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). In the feature extraction phase, LACNet uses an optimized EfficientNet as the backbone, removing certain MBConv layers to achieve network lightweighting. Moreover, an adaptive attention mechanism is used to dynamically select key features from multi-scale representations. In the feature fusion phase, the dynamic routing mechanism of capsule networks is utilized to enhance the spatial hierarchical expression of features. Experimental results demonstrate that LACNet achieves excellent detection performance on both the MIMII dataset and our self-built microfans abnormal sound dataset, validating its effectiveness.

Title: Precision-Driven Instrument Enumeration in Laparoscopic Surgery via YOLOv11 and Cutting-Edge Tracking Paradigms
Abstract: In minimally invasive surgery, accurate real-time detection and enumeration of instruments remain a challenge due to rapid movements, occlusions, and overlapping tools. This paper proposes a deep learning-based system combining the latest YOLOv11 model with advanced tracking algorithms - ByteTrack and BoT-SORT - for robust surgical instrument detection and tracking. YOLOv11, re-released in September 2024, is optimized for both speed and accuracy, making it highly effective in dynamic surgical environments. The integration of ByteTrack enhances processing speed, while BoT-SORT ensures precise tracking, even under complex conditions. Comprehensive evaluations across YOLOv11 variants (n, s, m, standard, and x) confirm the model's adaptability and performance, with YOLOv11n achieving 98.7% precision. This fully automated approach significantly reduces the risk of miscounts, improves workflow efficiency, and minimizes cognitive load on surgical teams. By enabling reliable instrument enumeration in real-time, the system contributes to safer, smarter, and more efficient operating rooms.

Title: AI-Driven Environmental, Social, and Governance Score Predictions: A Machine Learning Approach Using SDG Indicators
Abstract: Sustainability has become a crucial priority for global development, specifically Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) scores that serve as criteria for judging ethical and sustainable behavior. Machine learning models are applied to predict ESG scores with respect to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicators which lead us to a primary discussion of some challenges faced in ESG analytics, namely data sparsity, indicator interdependencies, and non-linear relationship. Through the Gradient Boosting methodology, PCA, and advanced feature engineering, we showcase a robust predictive framework that outperforms traditional statistical methods with respect to performance. This is a novel approach combining multi-source SDG data with advanced preprocessing techniques to deal with missing values and multicollinearity issues. The proposed model is significantly more accurate when compared to baseline methods and offers unique insights regarding feature importance within the environment, society, and governance domains. The present study highlights the importance of ESG metrics in sustainable development, the model performance is evaluated using various metrics, and the actionable implications for decision-makers are considered. Such interpretability is enhanced for practitioners, affirmed by the visual representation of results using feature importance plot, predicted vs actual score graph, and statistical comparison of models.

Title: Missing Person Face Recognition Using Hybrid LBP and Siamese CNN
Abstract: Automated face recognition has become a critical instrument in missing person search with public surveillance systems. Yet, traditional recognition techniques tend to fail when used with real-world CCTV data, especially in low-resource situations like elevators. Such environments are often characterized by low-resolution images, partial occlusion, different facial orientations, and illumination, all of which severely impair the performance of rule-based or handcrafted feature-based methods. To overcome these constraints, this work introduces a modular face recognition system designed to be optimal for lowquality surveillance videos. The system starts with face detection by the YOLOv8m model, which achieves a good balance between speed and precision. Next, two face recognition methods are investigated: Local Binary Patterns (LBP), a computationally lightweight texture-based approach, and Siamese Convolutional Neural Networks (Siamese CNN), a deep learning model designed to learn discriminative facial embeddings for similarity comparison. The system operates on individual frames taken out of CCTV videos and checks faces detected against an existing database of known people. Experimental evaluation is based on recognition accuracy and resistance to challenging visual conditions. Results show that the Siamese CNN approach outperforms the LBP method consistently, achieving recognition accuracy of up to 9 1. 5% in low-resolution, varying lighting conditions, while LBP had less than 80 %. These results highlight the strengths of deep learning-based models in surveillance applications, demonstrating their viability for more efficient and scalable deployment in real-world missing persons identification systems.

Title: A Hybrid Transformer - Classifier Technique for Guitar Play Recognition
Abstract: Automatic identification of guitar-playing technique is important for music analysis, identification of performers, and interactive learning. This paper presents a hybrid Transformer-classifier model that utilizes sophisticated spectrogram-based feature extraction techniques to improve classification accuracy. Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Constant-Q Transform (CQT), Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), and Gammatone spectrograms are used in order to extract the fine-grained frequency and time-domain features of the guitar sound. These spectrograms are processed through Vision Transformers (ViTs) and Swin Transformers, which extract spatial and temporal features in an efficient manner. These extracted features are subsequently classified through ML classifiers. The experimental demonstrates that the MFCC delivers the highest classification accuracy when coupled with Vision Transformer and Swin Transformer. More precisely, with SVM and MLP classifiers, both models record an accuracy of 97 %. In the case of Linear SVM, Vision Transformer outperforms marginally with a 98 % accuracy, and Swin Transformer records 97 %. These findings highlight the high performance of hybrid Transformer-classifier models in guitar technique recognition without compromising computational efficiency.

Title: Wavelet Transform Enhanced Signal Processing for Low-Latency Audio Recognition in Edge Devices
Abstract: Low-latency audio recognition in edge devices is critical for real-time applications such as voice assistants, surveillance, and wearable tech. Wavelet Transform has emerged as a powerful tool in signal processing due to its ability to analyze non-stationary signals at multiple resolutions. However, existing methods often suffer from high computational costs, limited noise resilience, and suboptimal performance under constrained edge environments, making them less suitable for real-time deployment. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel framework named WESP-LAR (Wavelet Enhanced Signal Processing for Low-latency Audio Recognition), which leverages Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for efficient time-frequency feature extraction and integrates lightweight neural models for classification. WESP-LAR is optimized for low-memory usage and real-time execution on edge processors. The proposed method enhances audio feature representation while significantly reducing latency and computational overhead, making it ideal for embedded AI scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that WESP-LAR achieves superior accuracy and robustness across diverse audio datasets, outperforming traditional FFT-based and raw waveform approaches.

Title: STUDENT WELL-BEING IN THE ENGINEERING CONTEXT
Abstract: Mental well-being is fundamental to both the academic performance and overall success of engineering students. Given the demanding curricula and high expectations inherent in engineering programs, many students experience significant chronic stress that can hinder their ability to engage fully with their studies and reach their potential. To better understand these challenges, we developed a comprehensive survey instrument and distributed it among engineering students, aiming to delve deeply into their experiences and identify areas where enhanced support could enrich student life within the department. Our survey findings revealed a spectrum of experiences. A majority of participants reported positive interactions with campus resources and conveyed that they felt valued at East Tennessee State University. However, some students also expressed a need for additional support, particularly in areas such as career preparation and mental health services. Furthermore, respondents highlighted external challenges-ranging from financial constraints to the impact of global events-that further affect their mental well-being. These insights underscore the importance of a community-centered approach, one that not only leverages existing resources but also continuously seeks innovative strategies to address emerging challenges. By reinforcing support systems and fostering engagement and dialogue, we can create an environment where every engineering student has the opportunity to thrive both academically and personally.

Title: A Time-Series Forecasting Framework for Stock Market Prediction Using LSTM and Technical Indicators
Abstract: This paper proposes a real-time framework of stock market prediction based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and prominent indicators. The first is to enhance the effectiveness of more accurate forecasting by measuring temporal dependencies and the non-linearity model in the data on finance. The Yahoo Finance API retrieves historical stock information augmented to indicators like the Relative Strength Index (RSI), Moving Averages (SMA, EMA), MACD, and Bollinger Bands. The model is an LSTM tested and compared against conventional machine algorithms such as Linear Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forest. Performance evaluation is done through Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and R 2 Score. The findings prove that the offered LSTM model demonstrates even better accuracy, with the value of MSE equal to 0.004 and R Sq Score reaching 0.95. By combining real-time information and deep learning, the interplay opens up an effective stock prediction model, a massive advancement compared to traditional forecasting systems.

Title: A Study of Slide Annotation Generating System from Online Presentations
Abstract: Nowadays, online presentations and meetings have been common with advancements of information communication technologies. People often attend a lot of meetings without moving to the venues. As a result, it becomes hard for them to keep concentrations to fully understand them and catch the points from vocal explanations by presenters. In this paper, we study a system that automatically generates annotations at slide pages from the recorded video in an online presentation. It integrates audio-to-text conversion, LLMs for keyword extraction, and optical character recognition (OCR). It proposes a new method for direct annotation-to-slide alignment, by producing annotations that relate keywords from spoken text to specific slide contents through semantic similarity and their corresponding bounding box coordinates. For preliminary evaluations, we conducted a controlled test using a single presentation video. The proposal successfully generated coherent annotations with relevant keyword extraction. However, the annotations-slide text alignments received subpar performance, and the video processing stage consumed approximately 83.6% of the total execution time of 712 seconds.

Title: AI in Creative Economy as a Key Factor Influencing Gen Z Employee Productivity
Abstract: The creative economy industry is one of the most impacted by the implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology. The implementation of AI in the industry can increase innovation and efficiency in various business processes. Generation Z as the digital generation, having characteristics that are very adaptable to the work environment, especially those based on AI. Although AI is considered to improve performance productivity, there is still a gap in how AI can improve job satisfaction. This study investigates the influence of AI adoption variables on employee productivity and job satisfaction in Gen Z employees in Indonesia's creative industry. This research uses a quantitative method with research instruments in the form of an online survey of 200 samples. The SEM-PLS technique was used to analyze the data. Researchers found that AI adoption has a significant positive influence on employee productivity and job satisfaction. In addition, researchers also found that job satisfaction has a positive effect on employee productivity by strengthening a balanced AI integration strategy. However, the indirect impact on the relationship between AI adoption on employee productivity through job satisfaction was found to have no significant effect. These findings lead researchers to recommend to organizations that in addition to adopting AI, they also need to consider employee well-being so that the benefits obtained can be optimal. This study provides insights for companies in creating AI-based strategies to manage a sustainable Gen Z work environment in the digital age.

Title: Real-Time Speech Emotion Recognition Using Deep Learning for Emotion Based Music Recommendation
Abstract: Affective state is a key factor affecting the music preference and the user experience. Traditional music recommendation systems do not have the capability of emotional sense, and the recommendations may then be contradictory to the user who wants to listen to music in a certain mood. This paper introduces a real-time Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) system, which employs a hybrid model of a CNN and a BiLSTM to recognize the user's emotions from speech input. The model is trained on public available databases - CREMA-D, and RAVDESS - and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) features with 50 dimensions are used. The system is tailored for mobile implementation with TensorFlow Lite and packaged in a native Android app. Emotion recognition outcome plays emotion-based music according to a pre-stored play-list. The performance of the system is tested under different real-world scenarios ranging from noisy to silent conditions. User testing has shown that users can decern between positive, neutral and negative emotions. In addition, the mobile app possessed good usability and learned user satisfaction, which further implied that it had the possibility to be used to facilitate emotion efficiently using personalized music experiences.

Title: Sightless Showdown: a Comparative Study of AI and Human Performance Without Vision in a Fighting Game
Abstract: This paper presents a comparative evaluation of a blind reinforcement learning agent and visually impaired human players in a fighting game using only audio inputs. The study employs DareFightingICE, a fighting game platform with enhanced sound design tailored for visually impaired users, to assess whether a blind AI trained with audio inputs can perform comparably to domain-expert human players under sightless conditions. The blind Artificial Intelligence (AI), trained over 900 rounds using three audio encoders (1D convolutional neural networks, fast Fourier transform, and Mel-spectrogram) and data from 25 domain-expert human players (21 male, 3 female, 1 non-binary; age range = 18-35 years), was tested against a weakened Monte Carlo Tree Search opponent. Results indicate no statistically significant difference in performance between the blind AI and human players, suggesting that audio-driven AI can serve as a viable proxy for human testing during early-stage sound design validation in accessible game development.

Title: Enhanced Analysis of Viva Dialogues: Classification of Questions, Answers, and Statements with BERT and CatBoost
Abstract: Manually analyzing the viva interactions can be tedious and inconsistent, underscoring the requirement of an automatic method. In this study, we introduce a machine learning-based methodology to classify viva interactions into categories such as questions, answers and statements using embeddings like BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency), RoBERTa and other embeddings on audio transcriptions of the viva. The tested models suggest the potential of BERT embeddings in achieving higher accuracy scores with CatBoost which reported a test accuracy and F1-Score of 83.68% and 83.73%, respectively. By automating this categorization of viva content, it allows for a more uniform and detailed analysis, thus enabling better educational feedback and research.

Title: Genetic Algorithm-Driven Portfolio Optimization Across Equities, Cryptocurrencies, and ESG Assets
Abstract: This paper presents a study on the use of genetic algorithms (GAs) for portfolio optimization across diverse assets, including equities, cryptocurrencies, and ESG-focused instruments. The optimization framework incorporates real-world constraints such as full capital allocation, cardinality limits, and diversification bounds, with objectives centered on maximizing risk-adjusted returns like the Sharpe Ratio. The GA methodology is outlined with details on portfolio encoding, fitness evaluation, and genetic operators. Performance is compared against traditional mean-variance optimization and meta-heuristics like Particle Swarm Optimization and Ant Colony Optimization using historical market data. Results show that GAs consistently achieve superior risk-adjusted returns and demonstrate greater robustness under complex constraints, particularly in portfolios adhering to ESG criteria.

Title: Evaluating LSTM, GRU, and Transformer Architectures for Music Note Pattern Generation with Small MIDI Datasets
Abstract: The application of deep learning in music generation has drawn significant interest, notably with architectures such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Transformers demonstrating strong sequence modeling capabilities. This study evaluates the effectiveness of these architectures in generating musical note patterns using a reduced dataset of 130 classical MIDI files, reflecting real-world constraints commonly encountered in Information Systems (IS) environments. To ensure comparability, models were trained under identical conditions and evaluated quantitatively through loss, accuracy, and F1 score, as well as qualitatively through visual inspection using MuseScore. The results showed that LSTM achieved the best overall performance, attaining the highest F1 scores across training durations (0.2176 at 10 epochs, 0.3726 at 15 epochs, and 0.6737 at 30 epochs). GRU exhibited faster training and comparable melodic generation, though with slightly lower metric performance. Transformer models, while powerful in data-rich contexts, performed poorly under small-data conditions, achieving low accuracy and slow convergence. This work adopts a Design Science Research (DSR) lens by treating these models as design artifacts and contributes to the IS domain through insights into lightweight, generative components for creative systems operating under resource limitations.

Title: Adaptive Weighted Loss for Sequential Recommendations on Sparse Domains
Abstract: The effectiveness of single-model sequential recommendation architectures, while scalable, is often limited when catering to 'power users' in sparse or niche domains. Our previous research, PinnerFormerLite, addressed this by using a fixed weighted loss to prioritize specific domains. However, this approach can be sub-optimal, as a single, uniform weight may not be sufficient for domains with very few interactions, where the training signal is easily diluted by the vast, generic dataset. This paper proposes a novel, data-driven approach: a Dynamic Weighted Loss function with comprehensive theoretical foundations and extensive empirical validation. We introduce an adaptive algorithm that adjusts the loss weight for each domain based on its sparsity in the training data, assigning a higher weight to sparser domains and a lower weight to denser ones. This ensures that even rare user interests contribute a meaningful gradient signal, preventing them from being overshadowed. We provide rigorous theoretical analysis including convergence proofs, complexity analysis, and bounds analysis to establish the stability and efficiency of our approach. Our comprehensive empirical validation across four diverse datasets (MovieLens, Amazon Electronics, Yelp Business, LastFM Music) with state-of-the-art baselines (SIGMA, CALRec, SparseEnNet) demonstrates that this dynamic weighting system significantly outperforms all comparison methods, particularly for sparse domains, achieving substantial lifts in key metrics like Recall@10 and NDCG@10 while maintaining performance on denser domains and introducing minimal computational overhead.

Title: Multimodal Conversational Learning to Improve Mathematics Learning in Low-Resource School Settings in Peru
Abstract: This study aimed to determine how a multimodal conversational agent improves mathematics learning among students at an educational institution located in Ate, contributing to SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production. This study was applied, with a quantitative approach, experimental design, and explanatory scope. The population was 110, and the study sample was 52 students from a public educational institution. The techniques used included observation data sheets, and the instrument used was the registration form. The findings showed that mathematics learning improved from an average of 4.88 to 7.47. The Wilcoxon test was also used to test hypotheses. The significance level obtained was less than 0.05, confirming that the multimodal conversational agent improved mathematics learning. It was concluded that the implementation of the conversational agent did significantly improve mathematical learning. The data obtained from the pretest and posttest showed significant progress, demonstrating that the chatbot efficiently assisted students, a fact that was beneficial for their performance.

Title: Optimizing Power, Performance, and Area in Digital Design Using ML Based Design Space Exploration
Abstract: With increasing complexity in VLSI design and shrinking technology nodes, optimizing Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) has become a critical challenge. Traditional manual and heuristic-based methods often fall short in exploring the vast design space efficiently. This work proposes a machine learningbased design space exploration approach using Synopsys DSO.ai integrated with Fusion Compiler for RTL-to-GDSII digital flow. The methodology intelligently explores various design parameters at the compile, clock, and route stages, guided by user defined metrics. Compared to the traditional Fusion Compiler flow, the DSO.ai enhanced flow achieved notable improvements: congestion was reduced by 19.42 %, standard cell area decreased by 5.27 %, and frequency increased by 16.44 %. In addition, all timing violations were resolved, including WNS and TNS, and the total power consumption was reduced by approximately 10.22 %. The design also saw significant reduction in design rule check (DRC) violations and better overall utilization. These results validate the effectiveness of AI-driven optimization in improving design QoR, reducing closure time, and minimizing manual intervention, thereby paving the way for intelligent, automated, and scalable physical design flows.

Title: A Multimodal Framework for Translating Video Speech and Emotions into Sign Language
Abstract: The proposed system offers an innovative solution to bridge communication gaps for deaf or hard-of-hearing individuals. Unlike traditional systems that rely solely on text or audio, this model uses video input to extract both verbal content and emotional cues through advanced AI techniques like OpenAI Whisper, Google Speech-to-Text, and NLP (Natural Language Process) models such as BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers). Facial expressions and tone are analyzed to interpret emotions, which are then conveyed using a 3D animated avatar rendered in Unity or Blender. This avatar performs sign language that is both linguistically accurate and emotionally expressive. Performance analysis confirms its effectiveness, with a gesture mapping accuracy of 94%, speech-to-text accuracy of 92.4%, and emotion detection F1-score of 91.3%, all while maintaining real-time latency of just 480 milliseconds. Additionally, the system is software-based, hardware-efficient, and adaptable to multiple regional and linguistic sign languages. Designed for use in education, workplaces, and public spaces, it ensures inclusive, scalable, and empathetic communication. Overall, the system marks a substantial advancement toward emotionally intelligent and human-centric assistive technologies.

Title: Face Recognition Access Control System Based on YOLOv8
Abstract: In the area of intelligent security, face recognition access control systems encounter difficulties in achieving high detection accuracy and real-time performance when dealing with complex lighting, partial occlusions, small faces, and crowded situations. This paper introduces an improved face detection model based on YOLOv8, which greatly boosts robustness through three key innovations: a lightweight backbone network, optimized dynamic loss function, and multi-scale bidirectional feature fusion. Specifically, dual attention mechanisms (SE and CA) are added to dynamically boost key facial features. SE adjusts channel weights through global average pooling, and CA captures spatial coordinates to enhance resilience to occlusion and lighting. To tackle instability in small target boundary box regression, the Wise-IoUv3 loss, with dynamic focusing factors and outlier metrics, adaptively modifies gradient weights, reducing low-quality predictions. Normalized Wasserstein Distance (NWD) loss is used together to boost the robustness of small face localization. Also, a weighted bidirectional feature pyramid (BiFPN) takes the place of traditional FPN - PAN structures, allowing for adaptive multi - scale fusion. The experimental results indicate that the enhanced model reaches 9 4. 5% mAP @ 50 on a self - constructed dataset. In backlight, mask occlusion, and crowded scenes, the recall rates hit 92.4 \%, 89.7%, and 95.6% respectively. Meanwhile, the false detection rates stay under 1.8%. This shows its efficiency and adaptability for edge device deployment.

Title: Light-FPYOLO: An Efficient Detection Network with Faster Block and Feature Pyramid Shared Convolution
Abstract: The integration of UAV remote sensing and deep learning has been extensively utilized in plant resource monitoring in recent years. The standard SPPF module is replaced with a newly designed FPSC module, which incorporates multi-scale dilated convolution and shared weights to enlarge the receptive field and enhance detail representation, facilitating efficient integration of contextual information across different scales. Results on Malania oleifera remote sensing imagery confirm that Light-FPYOLO achieves a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency, supporting its application in intelligent monitoring of plant resources.

Title: State of Charge Estimation for Hybrid Supercapacitors Under Multiple Temperature Conditions Based on A Hybrid Neural Network Model
Abstract: The dual advantage of power and energy density renders hybrid supercapacitors(HUCs) a strategic focus in next-generation energy storage research. Achieving reliable and precise estimation of the state of charge (SOC) in HUCs is vital for enhancing system management efficiency and promoting their industrial-scale deployment. In practical applications, energy storage systems often face challenges due to significant temperature fluctuations. In response to this challenge, we propose a deep learning architecture that integrates a convolutional neural network, an attention mechanism, and a Bi-directional long short-term memory (CNN-AM-Bi-LSTM) network. This model first uses an attention mechanism to weight the output features of convolutional layers, enhancing the model's reliance on important information, It then model captures temporal dependencies across multiple time scales through the use of a Bi-LSTM network, further improving the model's accuracy and generalization ability. The model is validated under different temperature conditions of DST operation, and experimental results show that the CNN-AM-Bi-LSTM network can adapt to the characteristics of HUCs at different temperatures. Typically, the estimation error remains below 2%, and the model maintains good performance even at lower temperatures.

Title: Channel Attention Multi-scale Fusion Network with Attention Weight Propagation Mechanism
Abstract: As computer vision technology continues to advance swiftly, image classification has emerged as a fundamental task in numerous applications. In complex image classification tasks, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) demonstrate notable benefits over traditional machine learning methods. Although CNN-based attention mechanisms have made substantial progress in classification tasks, they still face limitations in capturing multi-scale features and handling complex scenes. To enhance the association between channel features and multi-scale receptive fields, a novel plug-and-play image classification module-the Channel Attention Multi-scale Fusion Network (CAMF-Net) is proposed. This module optimizes feature fusion strategies through a multi-branch structure, effectively extracting and integrating both local and global features. CAMF-Net combines sparsity, multi-scalability, locality, and globality, incorporating an attention weight propagation mechanism to improve the capture and integration of multi-scale information. Finally, the proposed module's effectiveness and performance benefits are confirmed through comparative and ablation studies conducted across various benchmark datasets. The experimental findings indicate that CAMF-Net surpasses current methods in both classification accuracy and computational efficiency across a range of benchmark models, highlighting its potential for application in complex visual tasks.

Title: A Supervised Learning-based Framework for Failure Detection in Toy Cars Using Acoustic Signal Analysis
Abstract: Failure detection in toy cars has emerged as a critical area of study in both academic and industrial contexts. Traditional techniques are often inefficient, time-consuming, and error-prone. Title: AcousticWMD: Windows malware detection using machine learning models based on acoustic signal processing
Abstract: Malware or malicious software is becoming increasingly complex, making traditional detection methods less effective. To address this issue, we propose a new method that transforms Windows executable files (Portable Executable or PE files) into sound signals. These signals are then analyzed using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques to detect malicious patterns. While this approach has been widely applied to Android application files (APK files), its use for detecting Windows PE malware remains under-investigated. In this study, we compare two types of audio features: MelFrequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), which capture basic frequency patterns, and VGGish embeddings, which offer deeper semantic representations based on large-scale audio datasets. Our experimental results show that models trained on these features can achieve high detection accuracy, reaching up to 96.5 % accuracy and an F1-score of 96.8%. When VGGish embeddings are combined with a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), an AUC score of 96.21% is achieved, highlighting the benefit of deep contextual features. Additionally, we evaluate three binary-toaudio conversion methods: Direct Binary Conversion, EntropyBased Conversion, and MIDI Conversion. Among them, Direct Binary Conversion provides the best trade-off between simplicity and performance. This research demonstrates that audio-based analysis powered by AI is a promising new direction for malware detection, with strong potential to uncover both known and sophisticated emerging threats.

Title: Optimizing Audio Performance through Speaker Equalization Calibration Heuristics in Controlled Acoustic Environments
Abstract: Achieving optimal audio performance in controlled environments presents a significant challenge due to the complex effects of room acoustics, which introduce distortions. While automated speaker equalization (EQ) solutions exist, they are often limited by proprietary algorithms that lack transparency and accessibility. This study aims to explore and compare various heuristics for speaker calibration, incorporating both traditional and innovative algorithmic approaches, to assess their effectiveness in optimizing audio performance. The research is conducted in an acoustically treated environment, utilizing a calibrated measurement microphone and tone sweeps to capture baseline frequency responses. Four distinct heuristics are evaluated: deviation-based EQ adjustments, K-Means clustering, logarithmic band distribution, and an AI-driven approach leveraging machine learning techniques. EQ corrections are applied through specialized software, and post-calibration frequency responses are analyzed using the Manhattan distance metric. The study employs statistical comparisons to evaluate the accuracy, efficiency, and practicality of each method.

Title: Psychological State Classification Using Acoustic Features: A Deep and Machine Learning Based Application on MELD Dataset
Abstract: This study aimed to measure stress and anxiety levels through audio analysis using machine learning and deep learning methods. The Multimodal EmotionLines Dataset was used in the study, which includes audio, text, and video data. The specific goal was to classify audio recordings according to emotion categories (happiness, anger, fear, etc.). Data preprocessing included data cleaning, noise reduction, missing data removal, and min-max normalization. Principal component analysis was used in the feature selection process, and it was observed that acoustic properties such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients, pitch, and energy were important in characterizing the data. In the modeling phase, machine learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machines and Random Forest were compared with deep learning algorithms such as Multilayer Perceptron and Long Short-Term Memory. Performance evaluation included metrics such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and True Positive Rate - False Positive Rate curve. Furthermore, the generalization ability of the model was tested using K-Fold cross-validation. The Multilayer Perceptron model achieved the best result with an accuracy rate of 74.5% when principal component analysis was not used. The study conducted a comparative analysis of machine learning and deep learning algorithms using acoustic features extracted from audio signals. Model performance and generalization capabilities were extensively investigated using methods such as data preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, and hyperparameter optimization. This presented a novel and comprehensive Artificial intelligence-based approach for stress and anxiety detection.

Title: TurkAds-Emotion: Analyzing Emotional Impact in Turkish Advertising Audio and Text
Abstract: Modeling the subjective effects of advertising is inherently challenging, particularly for morphologically rich and low-resource languages such as Turkish. To address this gap, we introduce and publicly release TurkAds-Emotion, a novel dataset comprising 2,500 Turkish commercials. Each advertisement in our dataset includes both textual transcripts and audio recordings, annotated with scores (0-10 scale) across five functional dimensions: call-to-action (harekete geçirici), trustworthiness (güven verici), cliché (klişe), entertaining (eǧlenceli), and emotional (duygusal). To establish strong performance benchmarks, we first evaluated unimodal models to understand the predictive power of text and audio separately. For text, we compared sentiment-aware BERT and general-purpose RoBERTa models; for audio, emotion-driven Wav2Vec2 and noise-resistant Whisper models were assessed. Our experiments utilized a rigorous 5-fold cross-validation strategy, providing robust evaluation metrics. The fully fine-tuned RoBERTa model emerged superior for rhetorically complex labels, such as harekete geçirici (0.7146 F1). Conversely, the fine-tuned Wav2Vec2 model significantly outperformed other audio models on non-linguistic labels like eǧlenceli (0.700 F1). Leveraging these complementary strengths, we then developed a multimodal fusion architecture employing cross-modal attention, which integrates text and audio modalities synergistically. This fusion model notably enhanced prediction performance for functional labels such as eǧlenceli and güven verici (0.7478 F1), surpassing our strongest unimodal baselines. However, the multimodal approach did not consistently yield improvements across all labels, specifically underperforming on the klişe and duygusal labels. This study contributes both a valuable new resource and demonstrates the efficacy and nuanced potential of multimodal approaches for comprehensively analyzing complex emotional and persuasive effects in advertising.

Title: Toward a Hermeneutic Model for Digital Art and Cross-Disciplinary Performance
Abstract: This paper proposes a hermeneutic model for digital art practice, developed through a comprehensive review and reflection on a cross-disciplinary performance project that integrates digital technology, visual art, and classical music. The project centered on the visualization of René Magritte’s artworks within a live concert setting, employing digital technologies not as spectacle, but as subtle and flexible mediators that could bridge artistic disciplines. While the musical compositions were pre-selected and the visual references predetermined, the central challenge of the project lay in the interpretive task: how to deeply understand both media to enable meaningful technological mediation and construct a coherent and immersive experience for the audience. This study translates the praxeological insights from our collaborative creative process into a hermeneutic model designed to inform and inspire future cross-disciplinary artistic practices. By emphasizing the interpretation of distinct layers – elementary, semiotic, rhetorical, contextual, and speculative – the model enables artists and designers to articulate a shared metaphorical framework across disciplines. This layered approach offers a vocabulary through which technology, music, and visual art can engage in mutual dialogue during the compositional process. In parallel, the hermeneutic framework is positioned as a philosophical response to issues of authenticity in digital art. As digital reproduction and AI-generated media increasingly permeate artistic domains, questions surrounding meaning, authorship, and originality demand new theoretical grounding. Our model argues that, through thoughtful, critical, and creative interpretation, even technologically mediated works – such as reproductions or reinterpretations – can retain or generate philosophical and aesthetic depth. Rather than diminishing authenticity, digital media, when guided by reflective hermeneutic practice, can serve to extend the expressive potential of traditional art forms in ways that remain conceptually grounded and artistically coherent.

Title: Mitigating Temperature Effects in Rogowski Coils' Accuracy Through Physics-Informed Model
Abstract: Low-Power Instrument Transformers (LPITs) are increasingly being deployed across power networks, either to replace or operate alongside traditional inductive instrument transformers. While LPITs offer several advantages, they are also known for their sensitivity to various influencing factors. This research focuses on one specific type of LPIT-the Rogowski coil-and examines the influence of temperature on its performance, considering both the ratio error and phase displacement components. Leveraging standardized testing procedures as defined by IEC standards, the study captures the coil's behavior at three controlled temperature points. These empirical results are then used to train a physics-informed deep learning (DL) model capable of generalizing the coil's accuracy indices across a continuous range of temperatures. The proposed approach enables the estimation and compensation of temperature-induced errors without requiring real-Time thermal calibration or additional sensing hardware, thereby reducing complexity and cost. By embedding physical knowledge into the data-driven model, the methodology ensures that predictions remain robust and interpretable, even outside the originally tested temperature points. The results demonstrate that the integration of domain knowledge with modern DL tools can significantly mitigate one of the most critical error sources in Rogowski coils, enhancing their reliability for grid monitoring, protection, and control applications. This work paves the way for more resilient LPIT deployments in smart grid environments.

Title: Integration of a photoplethysmogram sensor to a single-board computer with cBP-Tnet edge AI for continuous blood pressure estimation
Abstract: Deep learning (DL) methods for continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring utilizing photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals have been confined only to research modeling and not applied. Recently, research on the weighing-scale-based system proved potential DL practical deployment (Edge AI) as existing systems rely on the Pulse Transit Time (PTT) method. The PTT method depends only on manual feature extraction, limiting its performance, and requires inconveniently one additional sensor per method (electrocardiogram, ballistocardiogram, and impedance plethysmography). This study deployed a DL model, cBP-Tnet Edge AI, into a single clip-on BP measuring system mounted on the sensor bar of a body-fat weighing scale, aiming for practical use case. This setup ensures familiar and secure skin contact minimizing motion artifacts. Specifically, we evaluated the performance of integrating a PPG sensor (MAX30102) to single-board computer (Raspberry Pi 5), deployed with cBP-Tnet edge AI for continuous BP estimation. To validate, we recruited 10 volunteer participants and compared cBP-Tnet Edge AI's performance to established PTTbased and traditional cuff oscillometric BP measurement methods. In comparison to PTT-based, cBP-Tnet Edge AI attained Pearson correlations of r=0.788 for systolic blood pressure (SBP) and r = 0. 8 4 1 for diastolic blood pressure (DBP). When compared to traditional cuff-based BP, measurements were preliminarily feasible (SBP: p=0.063; DBP: p=0.791). The mean absolute errors were 9.7 mmHg for SBP and 6.3 mmHg for DBP, with overall accuracies of 91.7 % and 91.2 %, respectively. Thus, cBP-Tnet Edge AI is comparable in performance to both established PTT-based and traditional cuff-based methods, providing potential to include SBP and DBP measurements to commercial body-fat scales.

Title: Enhancing Cryptocurrency Market Forecasting Through Advanced AI-Driven Predictive Analytics
Abstract: Cryptocurrency market forecasting remains a challenging task due to high volatility (3-7 % daily price fluctuations), sentiment-driven market behavior, and decentralized trading environments. This research presents an AI-driven predictive analytics framework utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, sentiment analysis (BERTbased classifiers), and blockchain analytics to improve forecasting accuracy. The proposed LSTM model achieves a precision of 0.96, recall of 0.97, and F1-score of 0.96, significantly outperforming conventional models such as CNN (F1-score: 0.82), ARIMA (F1-score: 0.79), and Transformerbased models (F1-score: 0.90). The Mean Squared Error (MSE 0.001), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE0.03), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE 2%) validate the model's superior predictive capabilities. The Sharpe Ratio (1.5) further confirms its effectiveness in risk-adjusted market forecasting. A wide dataset of 500,000+ daily tweets related to cryptocurrency, Binance historical price, and on-chain transaction data were used to optimize model performance. The findings reveal that short-term (24 -hour) forecasting leads AI-based cryptocurrency predictions (68.6 %), whereas longterm forecasting (120 -day) is underutilized (1.4 %). The hybrid AI architecture combines deep learning, financial sentiment analysis, and blockchain analytics and results in 18 % increased forecasting accuracy compared to current methodologies. This research sets the stage for LSTM-based neural networks as a more effective forecasting instrument, opening doors to future development in real-time AI-based financial prediction.

Title: Integrated Channel Estimation and Phase Optimization in RIS-Assisted MIMO Network: An End-to-End Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Downlink channel estimation and achievable rate optimization are critical challenges in current RIS-assisted MIMO systems. The two issues are studied separately: deep learning is used for channel estimation, and convex optimization is employed for rate maximization. But the step-by-step execution will lead to an increase in computational complexity and algorithmic complexity due to the separate handling of each task. To overcome these limitations, we propose an end-to-end integrated deep learning framework that jointly executes channel estimation and optimizes phase configuration to improve system performance. Specifically, a two-stage deep neural network architecture is introduced, which is trained using a multi-task optimization strategy. Moreover, the optimal network structure was explored by adjusting the scale of each stage and the training weight ratio. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces computational overhead while maintaining high system performance.
